files.title: Christian's Warfare, The
files.author: Robert Murray McCheyne
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Christian's Warfare, The
sourceMetadata.description: In this tract, Robert Murray McCheyne gives a vivid description of the warfare that plagues all true believers. He first explains why there is no such warfare for an unbeliever. In short, the unbeliever hates the law of God and will not obey it, happily pandering to his sinful flesh. But when he comes to Christ, this is all changed. He can now truly say that he loves God’s law, which has been written on his heart. He soon discovers, however, that this sets off continuing conflict against indwelling sin. In the midst of these battles, the believer feels wretched about his sin, seeks the Lord for deliverance, and gives thanks for each victory. The fight against the flesh never ceases in this life, but according to McCheyne, there is a sure promise that in the end sin shall be rooted out altogether.

files.title: Comfort for Christians
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Comfort for Christians
sourceMetadata.description:
"God has a 'people,' the objects of His special favor: a company whom He has taken into such intimate relationship unto Himself that He calls them 'My people.' Often they are disconsolate: because of their natural corruptions, the temptations of Satan, the cruel treatment of the world, the low state of Christ’s cause upon earth. The 'God of all comfort' (2Co 1:3) is very tender of them, and it is His revealed will that His servants should bind up the broken-hearted and pour the balm of Gilead into their wounds. What cause have we to exclaim: 'Who is a God like unto thee' (Mic 7:18), Who has provided for the comfort of those who were rebels against His government and transgressors of His Law.

"The contents of this little volume have appeared from time to time in our monthly magazine during the last thirty years. They were, previously, sermons which we preached long ago in the USA and Australia. Here and there is an expression (especially where prophecy is touched upon) that we would not use today; but since the Lord was pleased to bless them in their original form to not a few of His distressed people, we have not revised them. May it please Him to speak peace by them to afflicted souls today, and the glory shall be His alone."

—A. W. Pink, 1952

files.title: Compensations in the Lot of Every Christian
files.author: John Dickie
files.audience: children; new believers; parents; teachers; youth
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Compensations in the Lot of Every Christian
sourceMetadata.description: John Dickie argues that there are really no "evil" circumstances in a Christian’s life, for all details are arranged by God, and we know “His way is perfect.” A Christian’s life may seem pleasant or unpleasant. We may gladly be thankful for the pleasant, not seeing the danger it may pose to us, for God’s good gifts to us may easily be misused. The trials God sends to His children may be unpleasant to them, but with God’s blessing, they are precious, “yielding the peaceable fruits of righteousness.” Dickie examines the compensation each Christian may receive when they submit to God’s good will for them and unquestioningly accept all that He allows.

sourceMetadata.title: Consistent Christian, The
sourceMetadata.description: “The Consistent Christian is without doubt the richest book we have ever read on practical Christian living. In order to gain the most spiritual profit from the book, it must be carefully perused. It is much like the book of Proverbs, where each line must be contemplated. Secker abounds in the use of comparisons and contrasts, often using several analogies in the same sentence. Similar to the Old Testament authors, at times Secker ‘purposely exaggerates’ the wording to make his point. This handbook for Christian living will be a treasure to all serious Christians.”           —The Editor, 1660

files.author: George Whitefield
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Conversion of Zaccheus
sourceMetadata.description: In this booklet, Great Awakening evangelist George Whitefield uses the conversion of Zaccheus to illustrate that salvation is a free gift of God. He shows, in the first place, that there is nothing in Zaccheus that makes him fit for salvation. On the contrary, as a publican, he was “in all probability a notorious sinner.” Whitefield further points out that Jesus calls him by name. Zaccheus had come to see Jesus out of curiosity, but according to His sovereign, electing grace, Jesus, who had known this man from eternity, now effectually calls him in time. Concluding his sermon, Whitefield implores his listeners, “Make haste, O ye publicans and sinners, and give the dear Lord Jesus your hearts, your whole hearts.” He ends with a plaintive prayer, “O that you may know the things that belong to your everlasting peace, before they are eternally hid from your eyes.”

files.title: Danger of Delaying Repentance
files.author: Thomas Boston
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Danger of Delaying Repentance
sourceMetadata.description: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep. So shall thy poverty come as one that traveleth, and thy want as an armed man. Proverbs 6:10-11. Thomas Boston begins by explaining his application of the text as follows, “The point I intend to speak to from these words is: the delaying and putting off of repentance is a soul-ruining course among gospel-hearers.” As he expounds on this, Boston shows why gospel-hearers delay repentance and why such a delay is so extremely dangerous. He points out that most have not decided they will never repent, but just not right now, and then offers nine reasons why this might be the case. He winds up by showing how perilous and terrifying are the potential consequences of delaying repentance, declaring that a moment’s delay risks eternal, irreparable loss—because any moment could be one’s last.

files.author: Thomas Watson
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Doctrine of Repentance, The
sourceMetadata.description: The Doctrine of Repentance is, by the witness of many, the finest exposition found in print of this vital Biblical doctrine. In his explanatory style filled with vivid illustrations, Watson presents the reader with the Biblical call for repentance. In concise chapters, he reveals counterfeit repentance as mere worldly sorrow over suffering the consequences of sin. He then describes the nature of true repentance, its necessity, motives, and effects. He closes with strong exhortations to repent from every sin, how to remove impediments, and the means for true repentance. It is truly a Christian classic—as useful in our day as it was over 300 years ago.

children.title: As Doutrinas da Graça No Evangelho de João
children.description: Em todas as gerações, os cristãos, no púlpito e nos bancos das igrejas, têm tido necessidade de uma visão clara do evangelho, que é “o poder de Deus para a salvação de todo aquele que crê” (Romanos 1:16). É de extrema importância que o evangelho proclamado e crido seja as “boas novas” de Deus, sustentado por sua autoridade e, portanto, baseado em sua palavra. Por essa razão, eu preparei esse breve estudo.Escolhi o Evangelho de João porque ele foi exclusivamente escrito pelo discípulo “amado” de Jesus para trazer os homens a fé em Jesus Cristo (20:30-31). Neste evangelho, a nossa atenção é focada constantemente em Jesus Cristo. Lemos sobre seus sinais e suas solenes palavras aos homens. O evangelho contém um relato autêntico de uma testemunha ocular que registrou o que viu e ouviu e, como apóstolo, escreveu uma interpretação autoritária das obras e palavras de Jesus Cristo sob a direção do Espírito Santo (14:25, 26; 15:26, 27; 16:13-15, 20:30 31; 21:24).Outro motivo para a escolha deste evangelho é que tenho sugerido a homens, mulheres, rapazes e moças espiritualmente interessados que iniciem seus estudos da Bíblia na leitura deste evangelho. As igrejas que pastoreei por mais de 21 anos distribuíam o evangelho de João como forma de evangelizar. Também observei que isso tem sido praticado por muitos pastores e igrejas evangélicas.Como cristão evangélico, que crê e proclama o evangelho de Jesus Cristo, tenho a preocupação de que o que acredito e prego seja as mesmas “boas novas” que Jesus pregou e comissionou seus apóstolos e sua igreja a pregarem em todo o tempo. (Ver Mateus 28:18-20; Lucas 24:44-49; o Livro de Atos.) Os que são cristãos evangélicos hoje estão divididos no que diz respeito a certas características do evangelho. Quer admitam, quer não, ou eles são calvinistas, ou são arminianos.

Ito ay isang mahusay na tool para sa indibidwal na pag-aaral ng Bibliya o pag-aaral ng grupo.

children.title: Los deberes de los padres
children.description: Los Deberes de los Padres se ha convertido en una de las obras más queridas y respetadas de J. C. Ryle. Para que esto se cumpla con tal exhortación práctica, se habla de la capacidad del autor para hacer que su fuerte medicamento para las familias sea accesible y atractivo. Habla con la autoridad de un ministro maduro de la Palabra de Dios. El folleto describe 17 áreas para que los padres las consideren y las apliquen con oración, tanto en las acciones externas como en las actitudes internas. Sigue siendo necesario leer para cada hogar en este siglo como lo ha sido durante los últimos 150 años.

files.title: Earnest Request for Salvation of the Lord
files.author: Joseph Charles Philpot
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Earnest Request for Salvation of the Lord
sourceMetadata.description: “How is a man brought and taught to want to be visited with God’s salvation?” So asks J. C. Philpot in this short tract. The answer? He must see himself as condemned and utterly lost. Only when the hand of God brings him to that desperate place will he beg for a “manifestation of God’s salvation to his soul.” This then is true salvation, not the casual decision to add Jesus to the rest of one’s interests, which occurs all too often these days.

children.title: Une requête fervente pour le salut du Seigneur
children.description: Dans ce court traité, J.C. Philpot demande : « Comment un homme apprend-il à désirer une ‘visitation’ du salut de Dieu ? » La réponse ? Il doit se voir comme entièrement perdu et condamné. C’est uniquement lorsque la main de Dieu l’amène à désespérer de lui-même qu’il suppliera le Seigneur de lui accorder une « manifestation du salut de Dieu pour son âme ». C’est cela le salut authentique, et non la décision désinvolte d’ajouter Jésus à nos intérêts personnels, ce qui arrive bien trop souvent de nos jours.

files.title: Encouragement for Christian Mothers
files.author: James Cameron
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Encouragement for Christian Mothers
sourceMetadata.description:
Encouragement for Christian Mothers exalts motherhood as a work that glorifies God and advances His kingdom, highlighting the eternal impact of a mother’s influence and giving helpful words of wisdom for the fulfilling of this great mission. While challenging mothers with the greatness and weight of their task, this booklet encourages Christian mothers to take heart because God Who has called them to this work is sufficient for all they need. In a day when motherhood is minimized and even despised, this booklet offers timeless encouragement for Christian mothers everywhere.

Encouragement for Christian Mothers is taken from his “Three Lectures to Christian Mothers,” which were first preached in his own congregation in the course of his ordinary pastoral instruction. Due to their effectiveness, the messages were preached again in Edinburgh at the request of women from several denominations. Although not originally intended for publication, the messages were eventually printed, and thus have been preserved for us today.

files.title: Entering the Strait Gate by Faith Alone
files.author: Edward Fisher
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Entering the Strait Gate by Faith Alone
sourceMetadata.description:
Entering the Strait Gate by Faith Alone is an excerpt from The Marrow of Modern Divinity by Edward Fisher (c.1612-c.1657). The Marrow influentially stated the doctrine of unconditional grace, advocating a free offer of the gospel without condition. It was at the center of the later Marrow Controversy.

Here Fisher gives a dialogue between a gospel minister and struggling souls to correct misconceptions regarding the Law, grace, and works. Fisher urges, "Come to Christ by believing that He will accept of you, justify, and save you freely by His grace, according to His gracious promise. This is neither pride nor presumption: for Christ having tendered and offered it to you freely, believe it, it is true humility of heart to take what Christ offers you."

sourceMetadata.title: Every Christian a Publisher
sourceMetadata.description: In this tract, Reisinger reminds every Christian of the importance of using literature to help spread the Gospel. A Christian who is ignorant of fundamental Bible doctrines and where certain Bible verses may be found is almost certainly a main cause of the deadness and weakness of many churches. Christian influence has been passed down, as links in a chain, leading many souls to salvation, by use of printed religious literature. Christians should take every opportunity to read and distribute good literature in order to help build a stronger church.

files.title: Experimental Salvation
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.audience: children; new believers; parents; teachers; youth
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Experimental Salvation
sourceMetadata.description: Salvation was planned by the Father for His elect before the foundation of the world. Purchased for God’s children by the righteous life and substitutionary death of Christ, it is applied and wrought in them by the Holy Spirit, enjoyed through prayer, faith, and Scripture study. Pink speaks of those multitudes who sincerely believe themselves to be saved, but are total strangers to a work of divine grace in their hearts. He shows the possibility of a belief in Christ which is merely intellectual, and not unto salvation. True godliness is an internal work in the heart, while human religion is a surface change of behavior for the praise of others. Pink discusses the characteristics of true salvation, and who receives it.

children.title: Salvação Experimental
children.description: A SALVAÇÃO pode ser vista de vários ângulos e contemplada sob vários aspectos, mas a partir de qualquer lado que olhamos para ela, devemos sempre lembrar que “a salvação é do Senhor”. A salvação foi planejada pelo Pai para Seus eleitos antes da fundação do mun-do. Foi comprada para eles pela vida santa e morte vicária de seu Filho encarnado. Ela é aplicada neles pela operação do Espírito Santo. Isto é conhecido e apreciado através do estudo das Escrituras, através do exercício da fé, e através da comunhão com o Triuno Jeová.

files.title: Eye of Faith, The
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Eye of Faith, The
sourceMetadata.description: Faith is frequently represented in Scripture by the metaphor of eyesight. Pink discusses what characteristics resulted in the eye being the chosen symbol for the heart of faith. Among many other features, the eye is passive: it does not send out light or give anything to the things it beholds. Even though the eye is little, it has capacity to see all around. So may faith extend into all that lies within God’s Word: eternity past and future, Heaven and Hell, the vanity of worldly pleasures. As the eye is easily damaged, so, too, is faith a delicate grace: it thrives best in a pure conscience, yet is easily hurt by sin. As the eye weeps after an injury, so faith is helped by godly sorrow.

sourceMetadata.title: Faith
sourceMetadata.description: Faith is Spurgeon’s clear and concise explanation of mankind’s connection to the Gospel. In nine short essays, he delineates the reason for, ground of, warrant of, result of, Scripture’s declaration regarding, and misunderstandings of faith. He concludes by most helpfully describing what Biblical faith includes and excludes, so that believer and un-believer alike can understand how God works salvation for those who seek Him.

children.title: La fe
children.description: La fe es una explicación clara y concisa de Spurgeon de la conexión de la humanidad con el Evangelio. En nueve ensayos breves, describe la razón, el fundamento, la garantía, el resultado, la declaración de las Escrituras con respecto a ella, y los malentendidos de la fe. Él concluye describiendo muy útilmente lo que incluye y excluye la fe bíblica, para que tanto creyentes como no creyentes puedan entender cómo Dios obra la salvación para aquellos que lo buscan.

files.title: Faith No Fancy
files.author: James Durham
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Faith No Fancy
sourceMetadata.description: “Faith is called for, but take not every sort of faith for saving faith. It would make tender hearts bleed to see so many mistaken in the matter of their faith. There are some who say they had faith all their days—that they were convinced of the lamentable deceit and delusion they are under! Learn to distinguish between Faith and Fancy, between historical and temporary faith, and true saving faith. Though historical and temporary faith are not delusions, yet in so far as you rest on the same, and mistake them for saving faith, you are deluded, for saving faith puts you out of yourselves to rest on Jesus Christ; it brings the soul from the covenant of works to a new holding of life by Christ and His righteousness.”

files.author: Ernest C. Reisinger
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Faith, Assurance, and Perseverance of the Saints
sourceMetadata.description: Faith, Assurance, and Perseverance is a biblical explanation of five great doctrines of the Christian faith, including self-examination and the gospel in Christ. After developing each doctrine, each is examined in its relation to others in order to expand understanding and application. Faith and repentance, assurance and faith, self-examination and assurance, perseverance and assurance, perseverance and preservation—these and other relationships unfold the full meaning God has given us in the Scriptures. The author explains, “These five doctrines can be studied separately, but should never be studied independently of each other. They are vitally related and need each other in order to understand and establish all five of them.”

sourceMetadata.title: The Faithfulness of God
sourceMetadata.description: In this issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster, we focus on “The Faithfulness of God.” A. W. Pink encourages the reader to look above the scenes of unfaithfulness in the world to the One Who is faithful in all things and at all times. Edward Pearse holds forth the staggering truth of God’s faithfulness being based upon His unchangeableness. Charles Bridges takes the reader to the Psalms to see that the LORD is faithful even in the affliction of His children. John Flavel assures the saints that God’s faithfulness is the believer’s security and city of refuge in a world of disappointments. Richard Sibbes follows by drawing on the thought that God is faithful in His nature, faithful in His Word, and faithful in His works. Thomas Manton shows forth God’s consistent faithfulness being put on display in every generation. Charles Simeon highlights God’s faithfulness in His inability to lie. Charles Spurgeon closes out the subject by exalting the Lord Jesus as the Amen of God in all His purposes and promises.

articles.title: Faithfulness of God, The*
articles.description: God is faithful in His person, Word, and works.

articles.title: God is Faithful Because He Is Unchangeable
articles.description: We should find great joy and comfort in God’s unchanging character because He will faithfully glorify His name, defend His people, and destroy His enemies.

articles.title: God Will Fulfill His Word
articles.description: The faithful God cannot lie. The unconverted should repent of their hopes that He will, and the Lord’s people must abandon their fears that He might.

articles.title: God’s Faithfulness in Afflicting His People
articles.description: Believers suffer only because of God’s faithful fulfilling His promises of love.

articles.title: God’s Faithfulness from Generation to Generation
articles.description: Throughout the ages, God’s people experience the stability of His promise, unshaken by time and change, and wait for the fulfilment of all.

articles.title: The Faithfulness of God: The Saint's Refuge
articles.description: God’s people have an unshakeable place of safety against all fear: the faithfulness of God.

articles.title: The Saint's Hiding Place in the Evil Day
articles.description: Humility and faith must fill our hearts whatever our circumstances because of God’s faithfulness.

articles.title: Christ: the Faithful Amen
articles.description: Our Lord Jesus is the manifestation of God’s faithfulness as God and Man. He is God’s Amen to His own Word of promise, and He is the Amen in Himself Who faithfully redeemed His people.

children.title: La fidelidad de Dios
children.description: Enriquece tu apreciación de Dios con estos artículos sobre su fidelidad. Nuestro Dios hace lo que dice que hará. El nunca cambia.

sourceMetadata.title: Faithfulness of God, The
sourceMetadata.description: According to A. W. Pink, many in the church are ignorant of the scriptural meaning of foreknowledge. Because of this ignorance, it is easy for unlearned teachers to spread erroneous doctrine. A common error is the following: in opposition to the clear teaching of Scripture that God sovereignly chose certain people for salvation, these teachers argue that God, in His “foreknowledge,” looked into the future and saw that certain people would believe—and so predestined them to salvation. This turns Scripture on its head, making man the final arbiter of his salvation rather than God. In repudiating this error, Pink explains the true meaning of foreknowledge as taught in Scripture, showing that it is “never used in connection with events or actions, but always refers to persons.” It is individual people that God is said to foreknow, not the actions of those people.

sourceMetadata.title: Faith's Communication
sourceMetadata.description: Anti-Christian cults flourish in many places, but far worse, much of what is preached today as the “gospel” is nothing but Satanic delusion. God’s demands for repentance are left out, Christ’s terms of discipleship are not required, and saving faith is diminished to a mere act of the will. Blind church members are gladly led by blind preachers, and eventually both fall into the ditch. Pink answers the question that all who truly seek Christ should ask: What must I do to be saved? Using Romans 10:13, Pink defines saving faith, shows the mighty power of God in salvation, and what is required of those who would be saved.

sourceMetadata.title: Family Duty
sourceMetadata.description: John Bunyan, in this excerpt from the booklet Christian Behavior, addresses the roles and relationships between immediate family members. Fathers are responsible for commanding all aspects of their family’s spiritual and physical well-being. “He will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the LORD.” Wives should respect the authority and leadership of their husbands. Parents are responsible to instruct and correct their children, to “bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.” Children are commanded to “obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.” This booklet provides practical instruction for all who desire to model their family relationships after the Scripture pattern.

children.title: Deberes familiares
children.description: En este fragmento del folleto *Christian Behavior* (La conducta cristiana), John Bunyan aborda los roles y las relaciones entre los miembros de la familia inmediata. Los padres tienen la responsabilidad de dirigir todos los aspectos del bienestar espiritual y físico de su familia. «Él mandará a sus hijos y a su casa después de sí, y ellos guardarán el camino del SEÑOR». Las esposas deben respetar la autoridad y el liderazgo de sus maridos. Los padres son responsables de instruir y corregir a sus hijos, de «criarlos en la disciplina y amonestación del Señor». A los hijos se les manda: «Obedeced a vuestros padres en el Señor, porque esto es justo». Este folleto ofrece instrucciones prácticas para todos aquellos que deseen modelar sus relaciones familiares según el patrón de las Escrituras.

sourceMetadata.title: Family Worship
sourceMetadata.description:
The biblical basis, practice, and benefits of family worship.

There are many important outward ordinances implied in Scripture, which are an indication of the state of our hearts and whether or not we have an ardent love for God and His service. One of the most important duties of a true believer is that of family worship. A precedent is set early in Scripture with the example of Abraham, of whom God said, “For I know him, that He will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment.” Fearful threatenings are pronounced on those who neglect this duty. “Pour out thy fury upon the heathen that know Thee not, and upon the families that call not upon Thy name.” Pink warns that private worship is not enough: believers are required to honor God in their families as well. He speaks of the advantages and blessing that come from family worship: preventing sin and conveying a sense of God’s majesty and authority.

children.title: Culto familiar
children.description:
El fundamento bíblico, la práctica y los beneficios del culto familiar.

Existen muchas ordenanzas externas importantes implícitas en las Escrituras que reflejan el estado de nuestro corazón y revelan si sentimos o no un amor ferviente por Dios y por su servicio. Uno de los deberes más importantes de un verdadero creyente es el culto familiar. Las Escrituras establecen un precedente desde el principio con el ejemplo de Abraham, de quien Dios dijo: «Porque yo sé que él mandará a sus hijos y a su casa después de sí, que guarden el camino del Señor, haciendo justicia y juicio». Se pronuncian terribles advertencias contra quienes descuidan este deber: «Derrama tu furor sobre las naciones que no te conocen, y sobre las familias que no invocan tu nombre». Pink advierte que el culto privado no es suficiente: se requiere que los creyentes honren a Dios también en el seno de sus familias. Él destaca las ventajas y bendiciones que se derivan del culto familiar, tales como prevenir el pecado y transmitir un sentido de la majestad y la autoridad de Dios.

sourceMetadata.title: Fatal Results of Carnal Christianity
sourceMetadata.description: Using 2 Timothy 3:5-9, Pastor Shelton speaks about those who have a “form of godliness”. These are not the regular worldlings, neither are they true children of God. They hide beneath a cloak of profession of faith, but their speech and lifestyle betray them: they deny the power of the Gospel, which breaks sin’s power, and transforms the soul. These are teachers of false doctrine and error who deceive spiritually immature people who have not understood the truth about themselves or God. These teachers promise liberty to their hearers, while they are servants of corruption. They twist Scripture to say they have liberty to do whatever it is they want to do. Pastor Shelton encourages every believer to search his heart to see if he be in Christ or if he has been deceived by a false gospel which leads to hell.

sourceMetadata.title: Fight of Faith, The
sourceMetadata.description: “Let go, and let God.” This is the pet slogan of many who insist that God is willing to do all our fighting for us, and the Christian should turn the battle over to Christ. This is a half-truth, and carried to extremes it becomes error. Pink examines what responsibility a Christian carries in fighting the fight of faith. His circumstances are his battleground: the flesh is never satisfied, always wishing to improve his circumstances or change them altogether. Pink shows that true faith looks away from circumstances, delighting itself in the peace and joy of the Lord.

sourceMetadata.title: Five Facts Every Christian Should Know
sourceMetadata.description: This tract is a concise exposition of the five components of the “Golden Chain” found in Rom. 8:29-30. In this passage the Apostle Paul declares that God foreknows, predestines, calls, justifies, and glorifies every true Christian. The chain cannot be broken. If God does one of these things, He does them all. And if He does them all, then every person that He foreknows He will surely glorify. This should give believers great encouragement and hope for the future. As the author says, “Whereas these facts have to do with your personal and eternal salvation, none of them depend upon you for their fulfillment, but were determined long before you ever existed and are according to the good pleasure of His will, to the praise of the glory of His grace (Eph. 1:5-6).

files.title: Fourfold Salvation, A
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Fourfold Salvation, A
sourceMetadata.description: In this short booklet, A. W. Pink gives a clear and uncomplicated explanation of God's salvation. After noting that this subject has provoked age-long controversy among professing Christians, he assures us that “every genuine Christian has been saved, is now being saved, and will yet be saved.” Under four headings he delves into the four aspects of salvation: salvation from the pleasure of sin (regeneration), from the penalty of sin (justification), from the power of sin (sanctification), and from the presence of sin (glorification). In summary, Pink shows that God’s sovereign work of salvation spans eternity and time, stretching from election in eternity past, to justification and struggle with indwelling sin in this life, and culminating in a merciful end to the struggle as we leave this earth for our eternal home in heaven—never to see or experience sin again.

sourceMetadata.title: Gadsby's Catechism
sourceMetadata.description: Catechisms are especially useful in teaching children the main points of doctrine about Scripture and the God who inspired it. As Charles Spurgeon said, “Even if children do not understand the questions and answers, yet it abides in their memories, and will be of infinite service when the time of understanding comes. If we would maintain orthodoxy in our midst, and see good doctrines handed down from father to son, we must use the method of catechizing, and endeavor with all our might to impregnate their minds with the things of God.” Gadsby’s catechism is a useful tool to teaching many biblical doctrines. Learning these questions and answers will help parents “train up a child in the way he should go.”

sourceMetadata.title: Glorious Gospel, The
sourceMetadata.description: Much of the future lies veiled before us, yet one event is certain: every person will meet with God after death. But “all have sinned and come short of the glory of God.” Every person stands condemned, deserving the righteous judgment of God. The only defense the sinner may use is to own his sin, and plead with God for mercy. At the Cross, both man’s hatred of God and God’s heart of love toward sinners was fully shown. Because of Christ’s death for sinners, we may find mercy in that day when we stand before God.

sourceMetadata.title: God's Gospel of Grace
sourceMetadata.description: God’s Gospel of Grace is a unique collection of outstanding messages from past centuries on the doctrine of salvation. These authors describe with a unified voice the biblical faith of our fathers. They speak powerfully to the present day with grace-exalting, Christ-centered instruction. Ancient errors dressed in modern theological robes are leading many away from the historic Reformation faith once handed down to Christ’s churches. Our day needs a return to the old paths that lead to everlasting life in Christ Jesus. Feast on the sound doctrine and spiritual nourishment found in these pages.

children.title: El evangelio de la gracia de Dios
children.description: El Evangelio de la Gracia de Dios es una colección de mensajes sobresalientes de siglos pasados que hablan sobre la doctrina de la salvación. Estos autores apuntan unánimemente a la fe bíblica de nuestros padres, y hablan poderosamente hasta nuestros días con instrucción Cristo-céntrica, exaltando la gracia. Herejías antiguas vestidas en túnicas de teólogos modernos están llevando a muchos lejos de la fe histórica que los Reformadores legaron a las iglesias de Cristo.  Por lo tanto, deléitate en estas doctrinas, en esta comida spiritual que se encuentra en estas páginas para que el pueblo de Dios pueda caminar un vez más en la senda antigua que guía a la vida eternal en Cristo Jesús.

files.title: Gospel Preaching Commanded
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Gospel Preaching Commanded
sourceMetadata.description: Many unsaved remain unsaved because they have no desire to hear the gospel. God has spread a feast, yet no one is hungry. If God had done no more than spread the feast, every seat at the table would remain empty for all eternity. But thankfully, for all God’s elect, He sent His servant to compel guests to come to His feast. None would be believers tonight without being compelled by God to come to Him. Men are lost and dead in sins, and only Almighty power of God will bring him to life. Some say that only a certain number are counted among God’s elect, and the gospel should be preached only to these souls. Pink shows why this belief is unscriptural. God commands His servants to preach to every creature. We are to obey Him, not to argue with Him. “Go ye into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.”

children.title: Prêcher l’Évangile, c'est un ordre
children.description: Beaucoup de personnes non sauvées le demeurent parce qu'elles n'ont aucun désir d'entendre l'Évangile. Dieu a préparé un festin, et pourtant, personne n'a faim. Si Dieu s'était contenté de préparer ce festin, chaque place à la table serait restée vide pour l'éternité. Mais heureusement, pour tous les élus de Dieu, Il a envoyé son serviteur pour contraindre les invités à venir à son festin. Personne ne serait croyant ce soir sans avoir été contraint par Dieu de venir à Lui. Les hommes sont perdus et morts dans leurs péchés ; seule la puissance toute-puissante de Dieu peut leur donner la vie. Certains soutiennent que seul un nombre restreint de personnes compte parmi les élus de Dieu et que l'Évangile ne devrait être prêché qu'à ces âmes. Pink démontre pourquoi cette croyance n'est pas conforme aux Écritures. Dieu ordonne à ses serviteurs de prêcher à toute créature. Nous devons Lui obéir, et non discuter avec Lui. « Allez par tout le monde, et prêchez la bonne nouvelle à toute la création. »

sourceMetadata.title: Gospel, The
sourceMetadata.description:
The most important message in all the world is the Gospel of Jesus Christ. This issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster presents the saving message recorded in the pages of the infallible Word of God. Thomas Boston describes Christ's gospel as a report from heaven. J. I. Packer then details the four essential elements of the gospel message. Thomas Manton gives us two articles: the first, which shows us that the gospel is rooted in God's eternal love, and the second, which tells us why God requires faith. Because we will never truly understand our need for the gospel apart from seeing the darkness and pollution of our sin, J. C. Ryle instructs us in this important matter. In a second article, he teaches us of our need for repentance. Jonathan Edwards then makes clear that even the greatest of sins is no obstacle to coming to Christ. Finally, three of Charles Spurgeon's articles appear in this Broadcaster. He first unfolds the importance of believing Christ's crucifixion, resurrection, and substitution. He then supplies another note that is frequently missing from modern preaching: God's judgment. Lastly, he tells us in the plainest terms why this gospel alone is worthy dying for.

Audio narrated by Duane Disalvo.

articles.title: Why Is Faith Required?
articles.description: discusses faith and its relation to God, Christ, and obedience.

children.title: El Evangelio
children.description: Evangelio

files.description:
The most important message in all the world is the Gospel of Jesus Christ. This issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster presents the saving message recorded in the pages of the infallible Word of God. Thomas Boston describes Christ's gospel as a report from heaven. J. I. Packer then details the four essential elements of the gospel message. Thomas Manton gives us two articles: the first, which shows us that the gospel is rooted in God's eternal love, and the second, which tells us why God requires faith. Because we will never truly understand our need for the gospel apart from seeing the darkness and pollution of our sin, J. C. Ryle instructs us in this important matter. In a second article, he teaches us of our need for repentance. Jonathan Edwards then makes clear that even the greatest of sins is no obstacle to coming to Christ. Finally, three of Charles Spurgeon's articles appear in this Broadcaster. He first unfolds the importance of believing Christ's crucifixion, resurrection, and substitution. He then supplies another note that is frequently missing from modern preaching: God's judgment. Lastly, he tells us in the plainest terms why this gospel alone is worthy dying for.

Audio narrated by Duane Disalvo.

files.author: James A. Haldane
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Gospel: What Is It?, The
sourceMetadata.description: In this tract, James Haldane elaborates on five major points concerning the gospel. First, the gospel is good news of pardon to the guilty. Second, the gospel is misunderstood by many who profess to believe, who view it as a “scheme for making up their deficiencies through the merits of Christ,” but this, he says, is “another gospel.” Third, to many who hear the gospel, it is foolishness and a stumbling block, an offense to their pride and they reject it. Fourth, while the gospel is a “proclamation of pardon addressed to sinners without exception…it is the power of God unto salvation only to those who believe,” whose hearts are purified by faith. Fifth, he warns that all who claim to be saved, but do not live soberly and righteously in this present world, and show no fruit, prove their salvation is a delusion.

files.author: Charles Lukesh
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Greasy the Robber: A Story of Gospel's Power
sourceMetadata.description:
Greasy the Robber is the true story of a thief and murderer in Siberia of the late 1800s. It is a story of the power of the Gospel: Jesus Christ saves sinners for the glory of His Name!

“When Pasha saw that these men were not from the barracks, he told them freely what he had passed through and where he wanted to go. The men listened attentively; the clever and daring boy appealed to them. After a short consultation, they decided to take him along with them, ‘that he may not perish,’ they said. Pasha dared not contradict them, because he feared these armed men. He went with them into the interior of the woods—now it became clear to Pasha that he had landed in a robbers’ den.”—from Chapter 4, “Discovered”

children.title: Grasoso, el Ladrón
children.description: Greasy el ladrón es la verdadera historia de un ladrón y asesino en Siberia de finales del siglo XIX. Es una historia del poder del Evangelio: ¡Jesucristo salva a los pecadores para la gloria de Su Nombre! “Cuando Pasha vio que estos hombres no eran del cuartel, les contó con libertad lo que había pasado y hacia dónde quería ir. Los hombres escucharon atentamente; El chico inteligente y atrevido los atraía. Después de una breve consulta, decidieron llevarlo con ellos, "para que no perezca", dijeron. Pasha no se atrevió a contradecirlos, porque temía a estos hombres armados. Se fue con ellos al interior del bosque, ahora a Pasha le quedó claro que había aterrizado en una guarida de ladrones ". - Del Capítulo 4," Descubierto ".

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained

sourceMetadata.title: Heart of the Gospel, The
sourceMetadata.description: Preaching in July 1886, Charles Spurgeon begins by stating his theme taken from 2 Corinthians 5:20-21—“The heart of the Gospel is redemption, and the essence of redemption is the substitutionary sacrifice of Christ.” He goes on to identify and elaborate on the central truth of this great doctrine: God has made Christ—who knew no sin—to be sin for us that we might be made the righteousness of God in Him. Spurgeon winds up with a plea to sinners, “I humbly play the part of an ambassador for Christ, and I beseech you believe in Him and live.”

sourceMetadata.title: Heroes of Faith
sourceMetadata.description: The Heroes of Faith, as only A. W. Pink can, presents the persons and events of Hebrews chapter eleven both in understandable terms and with deep spiritual insight. The reader will agree that this is both an immensely practical devotional study and a doctrinally clear biblical exposition. The author skillfully develops the character of Abel, Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Rahab, and the Judges. Faith itself is expounded in chapters on its excellence, perseverance, reward, achievements, and pinnacle. In all, Christ is glorified as the great Object of faith in the whole of the Scriptures.

files.author: I. C. Herendeen
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Holiness: Is It Necessary for Salvation?
sourceMetadata.description:
Holiness: Is It Necessary for Salvation? shows the vital place holiness holds in God’s plan for His people. We are saved by grace, and not by works, but we are saved “unto good works”! Holiness is the result of being born again, by the Holy Spirit as a gift of God’s grace. This transformation makes its possessor truly happy as it makes the heart and life reflect the glory of God more and more.

So, is this life of holy obedience essential? Herendeen reminds us that God is a holy God, and that he demands a holy life of His blood-bought people. J. C. Ryle said, "We must be saints on earth if ever we are to be saints in heaven. He leads none to heaven but those whom He sanctifies on earth."

children.title: Santidad: ¿es necesaria para la salvación?
children.description: Santidad: ¿Es necesaria para la salvación? muestra el lugar vital que ocupa la santidad en el plan de Dios para su pueblo. Somos salvos por gracia, no por obras, sino para buenas obras. La santidad es el resultado de nacer de nuevo, por el Espíritu Santo, como don de la gracia de Dios. Esta transformación hace verdaderamente feliz a quien la posee, pues hace que su corazón y su vida reflejen cada vez más la gloria de Dios.

sourceMetadata.title: Holy Spirit - Holy Music: Contemporary Christian Music Exposed to Truth
sourceMetadata.description: 1 Timothy 4:1 reads, “Now the Spirit expressly says that in the latter times some will depart from the faith giving heed to deceiving spirits and doctrines of demons.” We are indeed living in the times that the Spirit describes. The departing from the faith has come as a consequence for not believing the Word of God is the “voice of the Lord your God” (Deu 8:20). Jesus said of these times that “because lawlessness will abound, the love of many will grow cold” (Mat 24:12). The coldness is a lack of real love for His Word, lacking any serious desire to obey it and to be conformed by it. Many claim to passionately ‘love the Lord,’ but without a manifest love for what He says. This effort is not to propose that I have the last word on music, but to take it out of the darkness of subjective reasonings and traditions of men, and place it in the light of the Word of God.—from the Forward

files.title: Holy Spirit's Work In Salvation, The
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Holy Spirit's Work In Salvation, The
sourceMetadata.description: In this booklet A. W. Pink examines the following aspects of the Holy Spirit’s work in salvation: regenerating, quickening, enlightening, convicting, comforting, drawing, and working faith. His biblical insights regarding the first (regeneration) and the last (faith) are particularly valuable today because these two areas are frequently misunderstood by modern evangelicals. Regeneration, for example, is believed by many to be the result of one’s “decision for Christ.” But as Pink shows, regeneration precedes repentance and belief. Likewise—and also unlike what many believe today—faith is not something that can be produced at will, but is a gift of God given by the Holy Spirit. It is sometimes lamented that the Holy Spirit is the “forgotten” member of the Trinity; but forgotten or not, it is always profitable to study the Spirit’s work, especially His role in salvation as presented in this booklet.

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Hopeful's Conversion
sourceMetadata.description: This is an excerpt from The Pilgrim’s Progress, and shows Christian and Hopeful speaking about salvation in Christ as they journey. The vanity of worldly pleasures was Hopeful’s entire lot. Ignorant of God’s redeeming work, loving sin and sinful friends, hating any reminder of his sinful condition or the coming of deserved judgment, Hopeful continued on as best he could, until he could no longer ignore the testimony of Faithful that continually came before his mind, and the power of salvation was made known to him. Were sinners in all ages honest with themselves, they would likely describe feelings and thoughts similar to Hopeful. Bunyan captures in honest and touching fashion the experience of many in coming to salvation.

files.title: Return to the Gospel: Introductory Essay to the Death of Death
files.author: James Innell Packer
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Return to the Gospel: Introductory Essay to the Death of Death
sourceMetadata.description: This Introductory Essay was written for the modern reprinting of John Owen’s The Death of Death in the Death of Christ (available from The Banner of Truth Trust), which first appeared in 1684. But the essay is much more; it is a direct refutation of what has become a watered-down man-centered gospel, and a step in the recovery of the God-centered Gospel contained in the Scriptures. There is no doubt that Evangelicalism today is in a state of perplexity and unsettlement. In such matters as the practice of evangelism, the teaching of holiness, the building up of local church life, the pastor’s dealing with souls and the exercise of discipline, there is evidence of widespread dissatisfaction with things as they are and of equally widespread uncertainty as to the road ahead. Without realizing it, we have during the past century bartered that Gospel for a substitute product which, though it looks similar enough in points of detail, is as a whole a decidedly different thing. The essay will help us in one of the most urgent tasks facing Evangelical Christendom today: the recovery of the Gospel.

files.title: Justification by Faith Alone
files.author: Martin Luther
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Justification by Faith Alone
sourceMetadata.description: Justification by Faith Alone is Martin Luther’s commentary on the essential truth of how we are declared right with God from Galatians 2:16. This truth was the catalyst for the Reformation, which restored biblical Christianity to Western civilization. By nature we are prone to run to the error of law-keeping in order to earn God’s favor—that is, to seek salvation by doing good works. Luther explains how false teachers deceive many with this error, and clearly proclaims the beauty of how Jesus Christ achieved a perfect righteousness for His people at the cross. Luther champions the true role of God’s free grace in justification by faith alone.

sourceMetadata.title: London Baptist Confession of Faith - 1689
sourceMetadata.description:
The London Baptist Confession of 1677/89 played an important role in Baptist history. The Act of Uniformity of 1662 made the new Anglican Prayer Book mandatory for use in all Anglican, Presbyterian, Congregationalist, and Baptist churches in England. Moreover, the Anglican church abandoned the Westminster Confession and returned to the Thirty-Nine Articles as its official confession of faith. Consequently, with the restoration of the Monarchy, the English Baptists suffered persecution for their faith. In 1677, a group of Particular Baptists met for the purpose of producing a more expansive confession than the previous Baptist confession of 1644. They modeled the Second London Confession on the Westminster Confession, but with significant theological differences regarding church government and baptism. Persecution kept the 1677 document from being officially endorsed by Particular Baptists until 1689, when the Toleration Act was passed. This act enabled religious freedom to co-exist alongside the established churches in England and Scotland. As a result, representatives from over 100 Particular Baptist churches met in London from July 3-11 to discuss and endorse the 1677 document. Though the confession was published in 1677, the General Assembly of Particular Baptist Churches adopted it in 1689; hence it is commonly known as “the 1689.” The Westminster Confession, the Savoy Declaration, and the London Baptist Confession of 1677/89 are considered the most important Reformed confessions arising from the English-speaking world.

"This little volume is not issued as an authoritative rule, or code of faith, whereby you are to be fettered, but as an assistance to you in controversy, a confirmation in faith, and a means of edification in righteousness. Here the younger members of our church will have a body of divinity in small compass, and by means of the Scriptural proofs, will be ready to give a reason for the hope that is in them. Be not ashamed of your faith; remember it is the ancient gospel of martyrs, confessors, reformers, and saints. Above all, it is the truth of God, against which the gates of Hell cannot prevail. Let your lives adorn your faith; let your example adorn your creed. Above all live in Christ Jesus, and walk in Him, giving credence to no teaching but that which is manifestly approved of Him and owned by the Holy Spirit. Cleave fast to the Word of God which is here mapped out for you.” —Charles Haddon Spurgeon to his own congregation in 1865

children.title: Esto creemos - confesión de fe de 1689
children.description:
“Este pequeño tomo no se presenta como una regla autoritativa ni como un código de fe, sino como una ayuda en casos de controversia, una confirmación en la fe y un medio para edificación en justicia. En él los miembros más jóvenes de nuestra iglesia tendrán un conjunto resumido de enseñanzas divinas, y por medio de pruebas bíblicas, estarán preparados para dar razón de la esperanza que hay en ellos. No te avergüences de tu fe; recuerda que es el antiguo evangelio de los mártires, confesores, reformadores y santos. Sobre todo, es la verdad de Dios, contra la que las puertas del infierno no pueden prevalecer. Haz que tu vida adorne tu fe, haz que tu ejemplo adorne tus creencias. Sobre todo, vive en Cristo Jesús, y permanece en él, no creyendo ninguna enseñanza que no haya sido manifiestamente aprobada por él y sea propia del Espíritu Santo. Aférrate a la Palabra de Dios que aquí es explicada para ti.”
– Charles Haddon Spurgeon (1834-1892)

children.title: TELUGU Edition: London Baptist Confession of 1689
AMAHAME Y’UKWEMERA Y’ABABATISITA BAVUGURUYE YO MU WA 1689
children.description:
IJAMBO RY’IBANZE

Mu gihe u Rwanda ari kimwe mu bihugu bishyirwa mu ibarurishamibare ko umubare munini w’ababituye ari abakristo, ndetse kugeza ubu imibare igaragaza ko 94% by’abanyarwanda ari abakristo, muri bo 38% akaba ari aba protestanti, ukuri ni uko ikigero cy’ubukristo bwa Bibiliya kikiri hasi cyane.  Nubwo imibare itangwa n’ibigo by’ibarura igaragaza ubukristo bungana butya mu gihugu, mu byukuri uko siko kuri k’ubukristo nyakuri mu Rwanda. Kuva mu mateka y'aho ubukristo bwagereye mu Rwanda, hagiye habaho akenshi ibwirizwa ry’ubutumwa buvanze, ndetse henshi budahuza n’ijambo ry’Imana, haba no mu matorero yitwa ko ari ayagi Protestanti. Ubutumwa bwiza bukiza, buvuga iby’Umwana w’Imana Yesu Kristo, n’umurimo yaje gukora wo gukiza abanyabyaha, no kubaha ubugingo buhoraho binyuze mu rupfu rwe n’izuka rye; ndetse n’uburyo umunyabyaha yakira uwo murimo binyuze mu kwihana no kwizera Kristo n’umurimo yakoze byonyine, si byo bibwirizwa. Ahubwo no mu nsengero zabayeho mbere, guhera mu myaka ya 1907 ndetse na nyuma yaho, usanga ubutumwa bwiza bwaragiye busimbuzwa agakiza gaheshwa n’imirimo, ndetse ahenshi imigenzo y’idini yagiye ipfukirana ubutumwa bwiza ku buryo uyu munsi amadini menshi yumva ubutumwa bwiza bw’ubuntu bw’Imana nk’inyigisho z’inzaduka. Muri iki gihe bwo, uretse n’agakiza k’imirimo, insengero nyinshi zahinduye ubutumwa bubwirizwa, aho bivugira gusa ibikora ku marangamutima ya muntu, nko kubwira abantu ko Imana igiye kubaha ubukire, ubuzima bwiza, kujya mu mahanga n’ibindi by'ubu bugingo ariko bitabasha kugira icyo bimarira umuntu mu gihe cy’iteka ryose.

Nyamara Imana mu buntu n’ubugabe bwayo, yakomeje kujya yisigariza bake bakomeje kumva no kwizera ubutumwa bwiza, nk'uko amateka agenda abigaragaza, ndetse na zimwe mu ndirimbo zo mu gitabo cy’indirimbo cy’ikinyarwanda zigaragaza ko hariho abera bagiye baba muri ayo madini nubwo ukuri bizeraga kutakomeje guhabwa intebe. Guhera mu myaka ya 2000 kuzamura, ndetse cyane cyane muri za 2008 nibwo bamwe mu banyeshuri ba Kaminuza, ndetse n’abandi bagiye bizera ubutumwa bwiza mu bihe bitandukanye, batangiye kwamamaza ubutumwa bwiza bw’ukuri, buvuga iby’agakiza k’ubuntu bw’Imana. Bamwe muri bo bakomeje kwamamaza inkuru nziza, ndetse abandi benshi bagenda bizera binyuze ku mbuga nkoranyambaga.

Uko niko baje no kumenya inyandiko z’abera babayeho mbere, harimo nk’iz'abatangije ivugurura mu Burayi (Martin Luther, Ulrich Zwingli, John Calvin, n'abandi) ndetse n’Abasukuzi bo mu Bwongereza (English Puritans). Muri ubwo bumenyi ndetse no gusoma ibyanditswe, niho havuye ko bamwe muri abo bizera bo mu Rwanda, basanze inyandiko z’amahame y’ukwemera zanditswe n’abo bahuje ukwemera kwa Bibiliya zakozwe mu kinyejana cya 17 mu Bwongereza, zihuza n’ukwemera babona mu ijambo ry’Imana. Kubw’iyo mpamvu, iyi nyandiko y’Amahame y’Ukwemera kw’Ababatisita Bavuguruye yanditswe mu 1677 ikaza gushyirwa ahagaragara mu 1689 yahinduwe mu Kinyarwanda, kugira ngo ibe kimwe mu bikoresho byo kwigisha ukuri kwahawe abera rimwe kugeza iteka, guhamya ingingo z’ingenzi z’ukwemera gatolika (kw’Itorero rusange), amahame y’ukwemera kw’abagorozi cyangwa se abazanye ivugurura rya gi protestanti, ndetse n’umwihariko w’Ababatisita bavuguruye batandukaniyeho na benedata b' Abaperesebuteriyeni ndetse n’Abakongresiyonisite. Iyi nyandiko rero ntabwo ari isimbura Bibiliya, cyangwa ngo ibe kurwego rwayo ku rugero urwo ari rwo rwose, ahubwo ni imfashanyigisho izafasha abera kumenya, kwiga, kwigisha, guhamya no kunezererwa ukuri kw’ibyanditswe byera, ndetse n’ubumwe bw’abera bizera ukuri kuva kera kose kugeza uyu munsi.

Umwami akomeze gukoresha iyi nyandiko mu gukuza no gushimangira ukuri kw’ijambo rye mu mitima y’abera bose bazayikoresha.

Icyubahiro cyibe icye Iteka ryose. Amen

Emmanuel MASENGESHO, 2021

Jean de Dieu Ntwari

files.title: Luther's Conversion
files.author: Horatius Bonar
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Luther's Conversion
sourceMetadata.description: To those around him, the monk Martin Luther seemed to be the holiest man alive. But the light of God’s Law showed him that all within him was vile. Horatius Bonar describes the terrors Luther went through, knowing himself to be a sinner who would one day stand, inexcusable and defenseless, before a holy God. He tells of the only hope and comfort Luther found was in the death of Christ, and the forgiving love of Him who first loved us. “The just shall live by faith.” The conversion of Luther was one of the catalysts of the Reformation, bringing light to the nations of Europe benighted under Roman Catholic errors.

files.title: Marks of True Repentance and Saving Faith
files.author: Jonathan Dickinson
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Marks of True Repentance and Saving Faith
sourceMetadata.description: What is true repentance and faith like? Jonathan Dickinson answers this question with penetrating care. He reminds us that there is a form of repentance and faith that falls far short of salvation. Evangelical repentance shows itself in mourning over sin, love for God and His Law, and trust in His mercy. It is a daily exercise and results in a total change of life. Saving faith includes a sensible impression of gospel truth, an embrace of the terms of the gospel, a humble trust in Christ alone, submission to His Lordship, love to God and men, and real heart humility.

files.title: Must We Be Born Again?
files.author: Thomas Boston
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Must We Be Born Again?
sourceMetadata.description: “Ye must be born again.” Boston shows that regeneration is absolutely necessary to qualify one to do something really good and acceptable to God. Without faith, the best works are but glittery sins. All reformation Is nothing in God’s sight, prayers are an abomination, and struggles against sin are nothing. Regeneration is the key to communion with God, and the one qualification for heaven. The unregenerate would find no pleasure in heaven, as it is filled with everything, they find distasteful. Boston shows the path to regeneration: receive the testimony of God’s Word concerning the misery of an unregenerate state, view the corruption in your nature, and fix your thoughts upon Christ and hope offered in the Gospel.

sourceMetadata.title: My Homegoing
sourceMetadata.description: What is the Christian response to death? The Bible shows us that we have hope beyond the grave. Death has lost its sting for the believer. This message provides a clear Christian testimony of joy and peace in the face of death. This message was first delivered over the Voice of Truth radio broadcast May 21st, 1967, shortly after the author's conversion when he was associate pastor in his father's church. It was first printed in 2003, shortly after L. R. Shelton, Jr.'s death.

children.title: Mi viaje a casa
children.description: De la Introducción: Quiero hablarles un poco esta mañana sobre un tema que me toca muy de cerca, y es: mi viaje a casa. Como hijo de Dios, la muerte no me causa temor ni preocupación, porque para mí la muerte es solamente la puerta que conduce a la casa de mi Padre celestial; ¿y quién teme o se preocupa por ir a casa? Puedo decir como el salmista: «Aunque ande en valle de sombra de muerte, no temeré mal alguno, porque tú estarás conmigo; tu vara y tu cayado me infundirán aliento» (Sal 23:4). Puedo decir con el apóstol Pablo en Filipenses 1:21: «Porque para mí el vivir es Cristo, y el morir es ganancia». De nuevo, en Apocalipsis, oigo estas palabras: «Bienaventurados… los muertos que mueren en el Señor» (Ap 14:13), y luego: «Bienaventurado y santo el que tiene parte en la primera resurrección; la segunda muerte no tiene potestad sobre estos» (Ap 20:6). También leí estas palabras en Números 23:10: «Muera yo la muerte de los rectos, y mi postrimería sea como la suya». ¿Por qué? porque la muerte de los justos es una muerte llena de bondad, gloria y misericordia, ya que nos conduce a la presencia del Señor Dios de gloria. También encuentro en Filipenses 3:20 que mi ciudadanía está en los cielos, desde donde espero a mi Salvador, el Señor Jesucristo, el cual transformará este cuerpo de mi humillación, para que sea semejante al cuerpo de Su gloria. El apóstol Juan también me dice en su carta: «Amados, ahora somos hijos de Dios, y aún no se ha manifestado lo que hemos de ser; pero sabemos que cuando él se manifieste, seremos semejantes a él, porque le veremos tal como él es. Y todo aquel que tiene esta esperanza en él, se purifica a sí mismo, así como él es puro»  (1Jn 3:2-3).

files.title: Neglecting the Gospel
files.author: Thomas Shaw B. Reade
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Neglecting the Gospel
sourceMetadata.description:
In the introduction to this tract, Thomas Reade asks the same question that the author of Hebrews asked, "How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation?" (Heb. 2:3).
He first points out the obvious: that those who hold infidel principles and who live in a total disregard of religious ordinances, despise the salvation of God. But there are others that, while they do not despise God’s salvation, are simply “neglecters of salvation.”
According to Reade, this neglect can take three forms:
  1. Living in the allowed indulgence of one known sin.
  2. Building on any other foundation than Jesus Christ and Him crucified.
  3. Preferring an earthly object rather than Jesus Christ.
Reade warns that any of these should excite alarm and call for strict self-examination.

files.title: Not Faith But Christ
files.author: Horatius Bonar
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Not Faith But Christ
sourceMetadata.description: Justification is the direct result of believing the gospel, but faith is not equal to righteousness. If faith was righteousness, that it would be a work like any other doing of man. Faith is not our physician, but brings us to Him. Bonar rather shows that faith connects us with righteousness. Faith is the acknowledgment of the absence of all goodness in us, and the recognition of the cross as a substitute of all lack on our part. God sees the believer as having done all righteousness in Christ. As the paschal Lamb, Christ is our protection, pardon, righteousness, strength, and peace.

sourceMetadata.title: Obedience
sourceMetadata.description:
In our day, modern American religion has such a flimsy, worldly, and perverted view of grace, one is not surprised that many professing believers think they are hearing the unbearable clanking of legalistic chains when some preacher is witless enough—or maybe even has the Christlike love for their souls enough—to tell them that the Word of God commands them obey the Lord Jesus Christ. The truth of the matter is that Jesus Himself says that obeying Him is our expression of love for Him; in fact, He goes on to say that we positively do not love Him if we do not obey Him. This is sobering, but biblical truth.

With this is mind, we present the latest Free Grace Broadcaster: Obedience.

Pastors—when was the last time you taught Christ's blood-bought people the importance of obedience to Christ? Parents—does your life of obedience to Christ fill your home, your family worship, your daily lives with the fragrance of Christ's grace? How we pray that this issue of the FGB will stir your heart to love Christ Jesus by keeping His commandments! His precious blood, spilled on Calvary's cross, not only cleanses us, but sanctifies as well. May our hearts pour out our love to Christ by fervent, humble, joyful obedience to Him. Obey is a four-letter word that blood-bought believers should love.

articles.title: God's Word and Obedience
articles.description: Professing Christians agree that all who bear the name of Christ must honor and glorify Him in this world—but how? This introduction answers with clarity.

articles.title: God's Gospel and Obedience
articles.description: The author presents what may be for many, a truly startling thought: the gospel is to be obeyed. The Christian life begins with obedience.

articles.title: God's Grace and Obedience
articles.description: How does God’s salvation by grace work with the believer’s responsibility to obey Him and to do good works? This exposition presents a detailed, helpful discussion.

articles.title: God's Law and Obedience
articles.description: Sinners are saved by grace alone through faith alone in Christ alone: does God’s Law, then, have any place in the lives of blood-bought, grace-redeemed believers?

articles.title: Our Faith and Obedience
articles.description: Abraham’s great faith was the root of his remarkable obedience: he is a pattern for disciples.

articles.title: Our Love and Obedience
articles.description: Jesus taught that love for Him and obedience are inseparable: what should this look like in the daily lives of professing Christians?

articles.title: Christ's Friends Obey Him
articles.description: How does the Lord Jesus Christ view those who submit to His authority? If salvation is all of grace, does obedience really matter to Him? How should we pursue it?

articles.title: Christ's Obedience Saves Us
articles.description: Are sinners saved by works? The Bible says, “Yes,” emphatically—but not their own works: the incarnate Son of God accomplished full, free pardon of sin and eternal life by His obedience to His heavenly Father.

sourceMetadata.title: Obeying the Gospel
sourceMetadata.description: Faith and obedience are tightly related. We should find real comfort in the fact that God has designed that His people should be saved by faith in the saving work of Jesus Christ, the Son of God. However, I. C. Herendeen's little tract urges us to check the reality of our faith by this vital test: Is my faith producing obedience? Not perfection, but genuine childlike obedience? Without faith it is impossible to please God. And without a lifestyle of obedient submission to God's Word, a professing Christian should question whether his faith is healthy--or present at all.

sourceMetadata.title: On the Faith of the Gospel
sourceMetadata.description: Haldane considers two kinds of faith: saving faith and speculative faith. This speculative faith is held by anyone who goes about to establish their own righteousness, those who trust to their faith, and not Christ. True faith in Christ is made evident by a life lived close to God, depending on Christ for everything. Faith unaccompanied by the power of godliness is dead. True faith is shown by the life it produces. Haldane reminds the reader of the known deceit of man’s heart, which makes it necessary to examine what is the basis of faith.

sourceMetadata.title: Ordained Gospel, The
sourceMetadata.description: “I have ordained a lamp for mine anointed” (Psalm 132:17). This is the Gospel, a light given to sinners in darkness, and carried by Christ. God has appointed the places where the Gospel lamp will be set up and shine. God ordains that His Word will always reach His elect, wherever they are. God appoints how long the Gospel lamp will remain in a place, and who will be converted by it. The servant of God does not know who of his hearers are of the elect. His business is to preach, and leave the Holy Spirit to work as He pleases. Pink makes clear that it is not by chance or coincidence that anyone is privileged to sit under Gospel preaching. God works both on the minister to preach His gospel and the hearer to accept it and repent and be converted.

sourceMetadata.title: Parents' Groans Over Their Ungodly Children
sourceMetadata.description:
Parents’ Groans over Their Ungodly Children was written by Edward Lawrence (1623-1695) for his own unsaved children. This 17th century Puritan pastor shares the burden of all such parents and encourages them to bear it in the strength of the Lord.

The following is from his preface:

To All Christian Parents:  “It is not only for the sake of myself and children, but also for the sake of you and yours that I have published this little book; but especially out of respect to the glory of God, that we may leave a seed to bless him in this world, when we are glorifying him in the better world…Give to every one of your children one of these books, and do likewise bestow some of them upon the children of the poor…I am a lover of children and have often lifted up my heart in prayer to God for them…Pray that we may leave that religion, which came originally from the Father of Jesus Christ and is revealed to us in the Scriptures, to our posterity and that they may have hearts to live according to the rules and principles of it more than we have done.”                                                    —Edward Lawrence, 1681

sourceMetadata.title: Pathway to Christian Marriage
sourceMetadata.description:
The Pathway to Christian Marriage is a Biblical guide for the journey from singleness to marriage. It describes the dangers associated with “recreational romance,” while explaining Scriptural guidelines for establishing a Christ-honoring marriage. The timeless truths contained in this booklet will help one arrive at the altar in purity.

Prayerfully applying these principles will prove helpful for older teens and their parents, as well as for parents of toddlers and preteens, for young people before they are attracted to the opposite sex, and for Christians of every age who desire to glorify the Lord Jesus Christ in every aspect of their lives. On this pathway, families as well as individuals will prepare for entering the joy that God has designed for Christian marriage.

Las verdades eternas contenidas en este folleto lo ayudarán a llegar al altar en pureza.
La aplicación en oración de estos principios será útil para los adolescentes mayores y sus padres, así como para los padres de niños pequeños y preadolescentes, para los jóvenes antes de sentirse atraídos por el sexo opuesto, y para los cristianos de todas las edades que desean glorificar al Señor Jesucristo en todos los aspectos de sus vidas. En este camino, tanto las familias como los individuos se prepararán para entrar en el gozo que Dios ha diseñado para el matrimonio cristiano.

files.title: Problem of a Suffering Christian, The
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained

sourceMetadata.title: Problem of a Suffering Christian, The
sourceMetadata.description:
In this tract, A. W. Pink describes several heart-wrenching examples of a suffering Christian, a situation that puzzles many. According to Pink, Paul casts light on this perplexing problem in Romans Chapter 8 when he shows that the sufferings of this present time (v. 18) “are not inconsistent with the special favor and infinite love which God bears to His people.” He then gives four ways this is true.

  1. We are brought into fellowship with the sufferings of Christ;
  2. There is a vast disproportion between our present sufferings and future glory;
  3. Our very sufferings provide for the development of hope and patience;
  4. Divine help is given by the Holy Spirit so that we are able to endure our afflictions.

Thus, God does not abandon us in our sufferings, but uses them for our good and His glory.

sourceMetadata.title: Professing Christians Warned
sourceMetadata.description: In light of the current widespread practice of equating salvation with a mere profession of faith, Pastor Gary Hendrix encourages every professor of faith in Christ to “give diligence to make your calling and election sure" (2 Pet 1:10). If this is not done, the result could be catastrophic. “Many who are confident of their relationship to Christ and make this profession with all boldness will spend eternity under the wrath of God.” So what is the evidence of salvation? Pastor Hendrix answers with 1 John 3:1-10. The apostle John’s major contention in this passage is simply this: “The child of God will strive after holiness and will in fact maintain a pattern of righteousness.” Hendrix ends with the penetrating question, “Now I must inquire, how do you view yourself in light of 1 John chapter three?”

sourceMetadata.description: The Rare Jewel of Christian Contentment first appeared in 1648, and is now available in a quality, abridged format. An exposition of Philippians 4:11, it describes the inner satisfaction enjoyed by true Christians who look up to Christ as their life, and not down at this world’s many problems. It is happiness without having everything we want. It is joy even when we feel sad. It is true contentment in the will of God, and not just because there is nothing else we can do. Every Christian will benefit from reading, meditating on, and applying this precious book.

sourceMetadata.title: Read the Christian's Reasonable Service
sourceMetadata.description:
Use this reading plan to read Wilhelmus à Brakel’s The Christian’s Reasonable Service (4 volumes), available through Reformation Heritage Books (heritagebooks.org). 

"In my opinion, this is one of the most valuable set of books available in English today. I don’t say this because I had the privilege of organizing the task, raising the funds for its translation and printing, and serving as its final editor a quarter of a century ago, but I believe this is true because of the rich doctrinal, experiential, practical, pastoral, and ethical content this classic conveys. When one reads Brakel, one is not surprised to learn that for centuries this set of books was as popular in the Netherlands as John Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress was in English-speaking countries. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, most Dutch farmers who were of Reformed persuasion would typically read a few pages of “Father Brakel,” as he was fondly called, every evening to his family as an important part of their family worship. When he completed the entire work, he would start over!" -from the Introduction by Joel Beeke

sourceMetadata.title: Real Faith
sourceMetadata.description: In this tract, George Mueller asks and answers the questions: What is faith and how may it be increased? As founder of a number of orphanages and other ministries in 19th century England, he had much experience in exercising his faith by trusting God daily, and even hourly, for the resources to keep them running. According to Mueller, our faith must be based on the Word of God and is almost always exercised and developed through trials, losses, and troubles. His advice? “Begin in a little way.” And your faith, based solidly on the promises of God, will increase step by step.
