files.title: Repent or Perish
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Repent or Perish
sourceMetadata.description: “Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish” (Luke 13:3). Sadly, this Biblical truth is seldom heard in our modern churches. But as A. W. Pink points out, “Repentance is absolutely necessary if the sinner is to make peace with God.” He goes on to describe repentance as, “A holy hatred and horror of sin, a deep sorrow for it, and acknowledgement of it before God, and a complete heart forsaking of it.” Pink ends this short tract with a chilling statement and a question, “Turn from your course of self-will; turn with full purpose of heart to please and serve HIM: or be tormented day and night, forever and ever, in the Lake of Fire. Which shall it be?”

children.title: Arrepiéntete o perecerás
children.description: "Antes si no os arrepentís, todos pereceréis igualmente." (Lucas 13: 3). Lamentablemente, esta verdad bíblica rara vez se escucha en nuestras iglesias modernas. Pero como señala AW Pink, "el arrepentimiento es absolutamente necesario si el pecador debe hacer las paces con Dios". Continúa describiendo el arrepentimiento como "Un odio santo y el horror del pecado, un profundo dolor por él y su reconocimiento ante Dios, y un corazón completo para abandonarlo ". Pink termina este breve tramo con una declaración escalofriante y una pregunta, “Cambia de tu curso de voluntad propia; Gire con todo el propósito del corazón para complacerlo y servirle: o ser atormentado día y noche, por los siglos de los siglos, en el Lago de Fuego. ¿Cuál será? ”

children.title: Repentez-vous ou périssez
children.description: « Si vous ne vous repentez, vous périrez tous de même » (Luc 13.3). Malheureusement, cette vérité biblique est rarement entendue dans nos églises modernes. Mais, comme A.W. Pink le fait remarquer, « la repentance est absolument nécessaire si le pécheur veut être réconcilié avec Dieu. » Il continue en décrivant la repentance comme : « une sainte haine et une sainte horreur du péché, une profonde douleur de l'avoir commis ; elle consiste à reconnaître notre péché devant Dieu et à y renoncer totalement du fond du cœur ». Pink conclut ce court traité par une déclaration effrayante et une question : « Détournez-vous de votre voie de volonté personnelle et d'égocentrisme ; tournez-vous vers Dieu avec un cœur brisé, cherchant sa miséricorde en Christ ; tournez-vous avec un cœur pleinement décidé à LUI plaire et à LE servir ; ou bien vous serez tourmenté jour et nuit, aux siècles des siècles, dans l'étang de feu ». Qu'en sera-t-il pour vous ?

children.title: Magsisi o Mapahamak?
children.description: “Sinasabi ko sa inyo, Hindi! Subalit malibang kayo’y magsisi, mapapahamak din kayong lahat tulad nila.” (Lucas 13:3). Nakalulungkot, ang katotohanang ito sa Bibliya ay bihirang marinig sa ating mga modernong simbahan. Ngunit gaya ng itinuturo ni A. W. Pink, “Ang pagsisisi ay lubos na kailangan kung ang makasalanan ay nakipagpayapaan sa Diyos.” Ipinagpatuloy niya na ilarawan ang pagsisisi bilang, “Isang banal na poot at kakila-kilabot sa kasalanan, isang matinding kalungkutan para dito, at pagkilala nito sa harap ng Diyos, at isang buong pusong pagtalikod dito.” Tinatapos ni Pink ang maikling tract na ito sa isang nakakatakot na pahayag at isang tanong, “Talikod sa iyong sariling pagnanais; bumaling sa buong layunin ng puso upang bigyang kasiyahan at paglingkuran SIYA: o pahirapan araw at gabi, magpakailanman at magpakailanman, sa Lawa ng Apoy. Alin kaya ito? ”

sourceMetadata.title: Repentance
sourceMetadata.description: What does the Bible say about repentance?  Is it necessary for salvation?  Where does repentance come from?  These and many more questions are answered in this edition of the Free Grace Broadcaster.  Arm yourself with wisdom to be able to examine yourself for fruits of repentance.

articles.title: Christ Commanded Repentance
articles.description: The first word of Christ’s preaching was repent: His disciples are to do the same.

articles.title: Examining Our Repentance
articles.description: How do we know if our repentance is genuine? Here is a brief scriptural test.

articles.title: Fruits of Repentance, The
articles.description: True repentance is a manifestation of the new birth. What should it look like in our lives?

articles.title: Heaven's Joy and Repentance
articles.description: answers the question, Why do God, the Son of God, and the angels rejoice over repenting sinners?

articles.title: Necessity of Repentance, The
articles.description: explains that without repentance there is no forgiveness of sins and no abiding happiness in this life or in the world to come.

articles.title: Repentance and Universal Judgment
articles.description: a breathtaking, panoramic glimpse of Christ and the Day of Judgment as a sobering persuasion for all people to repent and believe on the Lord Jesus.

articles.title: Repentance or Faith: Which Comes First?
articles.description: a thoughtful, careful look at a theological and practical controversy.

articles.title: Sin, Sinners, and Repentance
articles.description: Of what should we repent? And who should repent? Brief, but biblical answers to these questions.

articles.title: Six Ingredients of Repentance
articles.description: a detailed discussion of the nature of saving repentance: sight of sin, sorrow for sin, confession of sin, shame for sin, hatred of sin, and turning from sin.

articles.title: The Greatest Motive to Repentance
articles.description: argues that the revelation of Christ crucified is the most effective means of producing repentance in the sinner’s heart.

articles.title: What Is Repentance?
articles.description: a clear definition of repentance from Scripture and summarized in the confessional standards.

children.title: Arrepentimiento
children.description: ¿Qué dice la Biblia acerca del arrepentimiento? ¿Es necesario para la salvación? ¿De dónde viene el arrepentimiento? Estas y muchas más preguntas se responden en esta edición de Free Grace Broadcaster. Ármate con sabiduría para poder examinarte en busca de frutos del arrepentimiento.

files.title: Repentance--Legal vs. True
files.author: James Heard
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Repentance--Legal vs. True
sourceMetadata.description: According to James Heard, true repentance and true faith are products of regeneration by the Holy Spirit. He notes that there is also a false (or legal) repentance. This repentance arises from a fear of punishment, but is not accompanied by hatred of sin and self. So what does true repentance look like? It is a gift of God wrought in the heart so that a sinner is humbled by godly sorrow and abhors himself and his sin, crying out for forgiveness. It consists of three elements—a change of mind, a change of feeling, and a change of purpose. Heard uses the story of the prodigal son to illustrate these and then quotes Acts 3:19 to show the glorious results of repentance, “Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out…”

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained

sourceMetadata.title: Salvation from the Pleasures of Sin
sourceMetadata.description: Every person is born into this world in love with sin. Pink shows us that God’s Word does not deny that there is delight to be found in sin, but warns that those pleasures are but “for a season”, and the consequences that will follow are painful and unpleasant. God saves from the love of sin by giving each believer a new, holy nature which fears and loves the Lord and hates evil. Pink addresses the struggle believers often face: knowing if he has been delivered from the love of sin. He shows how believers may be assured that have been saved from the pleasure they formerly had in their sin.

files.author: Edward Griffin
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Salvation Taken into God's Own Hands
sourceMetadata.description: In this tract, Edward Griffin (1770-1837) speaks of God’s plan of salvation conceived before the dawn of time. According to Griffin, every aspect of this plan was taken into God’s own hands, motivated by nothing but His own glory and compassion for a ruined world. Included was sending His Son to bear the sins of many, enlightening the world by gospel preaching, insuring the salvation of His elect and their sanctification, and creating and preserving His Church. Furthermore, every part of this was brought about independently of His creatures. Indeed, had God not taken salvation into His own hands, not a single fallen creature would ever have reached the kingdom of heaven. Griffin concludes by urging believers to leave all of their concerns to God, and entreating impenitent men to “seek ye the Lord while He may be found.”

files.title: Satan and His Gospel
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Satan and His Gospel
sourceMetadata.description: A. W. Pink provides a thoroughly biblical description of Satan including his existence as a personal being, his origin, his fall, and his position since he fell. Pink then concentrates on Satan’s counterfeit gospel which so closely resembles the real gospel that multitudes are deceived. It is not revolutionary nor is it obviously heretical, but aims at “peace and unity.” Toning down the true gospel’s offensive doctrines and smoothing its rough edges, Satan’s gospel has great appeal to the carnal mind. Sadly, many who are deluded by it will in the end hear the most terrifying words, “I never knew you; depart from me, ye that work iniquity.” Pink concludes with timely advice for us all, “How necessary it is then to find out where we really are; to examine ourselves and see whether we be in the faith.”

files.title: Eight Lies You Hear on Campus and in the World
files.author: Richard Ochs
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Eight Lies You Hear on Campus and in the World
sourceMetadata.description:
This tract deals with some major objections to the Bible and Christianity that are found in our modern secular society.

There are many lies told today about Christianity. Not everything we are told, however, agrees with the Bible. Ochs addresses and debunks eight common lies:

1) In order to believe the Bible, one must commit intellectual suicide.

2) Evolution is a reasonable explanation of the origin and present makeup of the universe.

3) Christianity is basically the same as other religions of the world.

4) Money, power, pleasure, and prestige are the things that give real meaning and purpose to life.

5) Jesus never claimed to be God.

6) The accounts of Christ are not reliable since they were written long after His death.

7) Man is basically good.

8) God saves good people.

children.title: Ocho mentiras que oyes
children.description:
Este folleto aborda algunas de las principales objeciones a la Biblia y al cristianismo que se encuentran en nuestra sociedad secular moderna.

Hoy en día se dicen muchas mentiras sobre el cristianismo. Sin embargo, no todo lo que se nos dice concuerda con la Biblia. Ochs analiza y refuta ocho mentiras comunes:

1) Para creer en la Biblia, uno debe cometer un suicidio intelectual.

2) La evolución es una explicación razonable del origen y la constitución actual del universo.

3) El cristianismo es básicamente igual a otras religiones del mundo.

4) El dinero, el poder, el placer y el prestigio son las cosas que dan verdadero sentido y propósito a la vida.

5) Jesús nunca afirmó ser Dios.

6) Los relatos sobre Cristo no son fiables, ya que fueron escritos mucho tiempo después de su muerte.

7) El ser humano es básicamente bueno.

8) Dios salva a las personas buenas.

files.author: George Whitefield
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Saul's Conversion
sourceMetadata.description: In this booklet George Whitefield gives an exposition of the biblical account of the conversion of Saul, who would later become the Apostle Paul. He focuses the attention of the reader on the grace of Jesus Christ to a persecutor of His church, Saul. This redeemed man who would be brought to conversion by Christ, who preached the very gospel which he had formerly persecuted, is a testimony to the truth that, in the words of Whitefield, "For all that we know to the contrary, some of those very persons, who are now persecuting, may be chosen from all eternity by God, and hereafter called in time, to edify and build up the church of Christ."

files.author: Joel Beeke
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Escape For Your Life
sourceMetadata.description:
Comparing God’s September 11, 2001, judgment on America to His ancient judgment on Sodom, Joel Beeke examines heaven’s somber message to our sinful nation and, more personal, to those who have ignored or rejected the gospel. He addresses the latter in words spoken by the angel just prior to Sodom’s devastation, “Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain; escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed” (Gen. 19:17). From this passage he admonishes unbelievers:

  1. Realize your danger (you are under the wrath of God, just like Sodom).
  2. Forsake all (you must give up everything to follow Christ).
  3. Run for your life (you must flee this wicked world).

Beeke sums it up this way, “Oh, I beseech you, run for your life; run straight to Christ. Don’t run to ceremonies, feelings, ministers, works, orthodoxies—but run straight to Christ.”

files.title: Eternal Destiny of the Unsaved
files.author: I. C. Herendeen
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Eternal Destiny of the Unsaved
sourceMetadata.description: I. C. Herendeen examines the somber—and by today’s standards very unpopular—question of what happens to the unsaved after death. Why did he write on such a subject? Because an offended God is righteous, holy, and just. Because natural man is an incorrigible sinner with the wrath of a sin-hating God abiding on him. Because the sinner is in alarming danger; the punishment that awaits him is awful, hopeless, unendurable, and endless. In a word, Herendeen wrote to give sinners a solemn warning. He does this by expounding on the nature of hell, the sinner’s great folly, and the ferocity of God’s wrath. He concludes by explaining who goes to hell and why, and showing the only way of escape—“Flee to the blessed Saviour.”

files.title: Saving Faith: Its Meaning & Object
files.author: Lee Roy Shelton, Jr.
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Saving Faith: Its Meaning & Object
sourceMetadata.description: What is saving faith? The essential elements of saving faith include yielding to the authority of God, a genuine coming to Christ, a complete surrender of my whole life to God, and believing on Christ with all my heart, affections, and will. Who does saving faith look to? The only object of true saving faith is Christ as the surety of the new covenant. We must look to Christ in His willingness to save sinners. "There is no salvation in Christ apart from faith, and no instrumental means other than faith."

files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Scriptures and Obedience, The
sourceMetadata.description: "Reality in life, not glowing words from the lips, is what Christ requires. What a searching and solemn word is that in James 1:22. 'Be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves'...God has given us His Word not only with the design of instructing us, but for the purpose of directing us: to make known what He requires us to do." Pink looks at God's demands upon man and man's failure to meet God's demands before he brings us to God's full provision for meeting His demands. We are called to love God's commandments and yield ourselves to them.

files.title: Eternal Punishment
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Eternal Punishment
sourceMetadata.description: This booklet addresses an exceedingly weighty matter worthy of serious contemplation by persons of all spiritual states. God’s just judgment of the wicked is terrible and eternal. The reality of eternal punishment demonstrates that God is holy and just in His response to sin, and that He demonstrates glorious mercy and grace upon His people. Pink concludes his exposition of the judgment of God by giving an earnest warning to the unsaved reader to come into God’s eternal mercy and grace in Christ and be saved from the coming wrath of eternal punishment.

children.title: Le châtiment éternel
children.description: Ce livret aborde un sujet absolument crucial qui mérite l’attention de tous, quelle que soit leur condition spirituelle. Le juste jugement de Dieu sur le méchant est terrible et éternel. Le châtiment éternel est réel, et il manifeste la sainteté et la justice de Dieu lorsque celui-ci traite le péché, ainsi que sa glorieuse miséricorde et sa grâce envers son peuple. Pink conclut cette exposition sur le jugement de Dieu en adressant au lecteur perdu un fervent avertissement de venir à Christ, pour être sauvé de la colère à venir et du châtiment éternel par la miséricorde et la grâce éternelles de Dieu.

files.title: Eternity - The Dying Man
files.author: J.J.S.
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Eternity - The Dying Man
sourceMetadata.description: In this short tract, the author confronts his readers with the reality of their temporary stay on this earth, reminding them that they are on a journey in which every step takes them closer to eternity. Even though many people will have nothing to do with God now, how many consider that they will certainly face Him then? The author challenges his unregenerate readers to contemplate the gravity of their vulnerable state, “Your sin will find you out,” he says, and pointedly asks “Where will you spend eternity?” Softening his tone, he urges them to “Listen to the glad tidings of God, against whom you have sinned.” In the end, he quotes John 3:16, explaining, “My dear friend, this is God’s salvation.” And poses the crucial question, “Will you take it?”

files.title: Sorrow In Christian Homes
files.author: J. R. Miller
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Sorrow In Christian Homes
sourceMetadata.description: Sorrow and loss will eventually come to every home, despite wealth, culture, social standing, or religion. Times of sorrow can be a critical, dangerous point when wise and loving guidance is required. Miller shows us that God uses sorrow to purify the lives of His people. However, sorrow may produce only desolation in the life. The difference between the two results lies in the relation of the sufferer to Christ. In the Christian who is near to Christ, though there are tears and pain, sorrow leaves a blessing of peace and submission to the will of God. Miller urges each person to prepare for the inevitable day of sorrow by maintaining a living, personal relationship with Christ.

files.title: Everlasting Righteousness
files.author: Horatius Bonar
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Everlasting Righteousness
sourceMetadata.description: The Everlasting Righteousness gets right to the heart of the gospel of Jesus Christ. How can sinful people be right before a holy God? God’s inflexible justice demands a perfect righteousness in His creatures; only the everlasting righteousness of the Son of God will suffice! His is sufficient because it is that of God Himself. When a sinner believes on Christ the Savior, his record of sins is erased on the basis of the substitutionary work of Christ on the cross, and Christ’s righteousness is freely reckoned to his account. This priceless gift is granted freely to the one who places his faith in the Person of Christ, not in his own merits, graces, or even faith itself. The sufficient righteousness of Christ is the safe ground of peace and joy for the believer, as he looks not at anything in himself but the all-sufficient Lamb of God!

sourceMetadata.title: Spiritual Faith and Outward Profession
sourceMetadata.description: In this brief tract, A. W. Pink examines the difference between a mere outward profession of faith and the true faith that is given by a sovereign act of God. According to Pink, “The natural man, no matter how religious or orthodox he be” does not possess this true faith and no labor or decision on his part will cause him to acquire it. He continues by showing how this difference is evident in several spheres of Christian living which include reading the Scriptures, listening to the Word preached, prayer, conversing about the things of God, living a godly life, and passing out of this present world. Pink ends by showing in a few words what distinguishes a genuine Christian from one who is Christian in name only—not mere head knowledge, but a “God-given, Spirit-wrought faith in the heart.”

sourceMetadata.title: Spurgeon's Catechism
sourceMetadata.description:
Spurgeon edited the Baptist Catechism for his own congregation in 1855, when he was 21 years old. On October 14, 1855, Charles Spurgeon preached Sermon No. 46 to several thousand gathered to hear him at New Park Street Chapel. The sermon publication contained an announcement of this Catechism. The text that morning was: “Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations” (Psa 90:1).

“I am persuaded that the use of a good Catechism in all our families will be a great safeguard against the increasing errors of the times, and therefore I have compiled this little manual...for the use of my own church and congregation. Those who use it in their families or classes must labor to explain the sense; but the words should be carefully learned by heart, for they will be understood better as years pass. May the Lord bless my dear friends and their families evermore…”—C. H. Spurgeon

The Baptist Catechism was written in 1693 by William Collins and Benjamin Keach for teaching the doctrines of the London Baptist Confession of 1689. By 1738, this catechism was adopted by the Philadelphia Association of Baptists in America, the spiritual parent of all Baptist churches in the USA. Spurgeon edited and reprinted it in 1855, shortening the expositions of the Ten Commandments and the Lord’s Prayer. Thus, the catechism you hold in your hand is in essence the one used by Baptists in English-speaking countries to train their families for the last 300 years!

sourceMetadata.title: Exchange Between the Sinful and the Sinless, The
sourceMetadata.description: Horatius Bonar here considers how God can show favor to His children. A just ruler may not show favor to a criminal unless he can do so without loss of character, without breach of law, without encouragement to crime, and without infringement or compromise of government. Bonar shows that God’s plan of pardon accomplishes this perfectly, by making the Sinless One to bear the sin of the sinful. Christ lived a perfect sinless life, yet died the death of the worst criminal, being “made sin” for the sinner. As Christ died the death of the unrighteous, the unrighteous is made righteous through the virtuous life of Christ.

sourceMetadata.title: Television and the Christian Home
sourceMetadata.description: Many dangers threaten the spiritual well-being of the believer in these last days. Television is one of the most well-hidden dangers to a Christian, but is exploited by Satan to accomplish his own sinister ends. Rather than seeking to encroach upon personal liberties, Duff seeks to lovingly warn those who are tempted to follow worldly trends. He shows that watching television programs can be harmful to the spiritual prosperity of adults and children alike. Because the Lord has redeemed us with His precious blood, let us not allow the world to steal our affections away from Him.

sourceMetadata.title: Experiential Union
sourceMetadata.description:
This booklet deals with our practical oneness with Christ. He shows how we maintain this relationship and how to restore this relationship after backsliding.

Arthur Pink discusses the mystical saving union of the believer with Christ. In order to have close communion with Christ, He must be known to us, we must have free access to Him, and there must be mutual affection and esteem. “Walking together” with Christ is to live in agreement with His revealed will. The believer’s experience of communion with Christ is exercised in happy, willing subjection to Him as Lord. Pink describes the nature and characteristics of the believer’s union with Christ, and describes what is needed to maintain it. At times, however, believers fail and communion with Christ is broken for a time. Pink shows what is necessary to restore the fellowship once enjoyed with Christ: confession and repentance.

sourceMetadata.title: Ten Commandments from the Westminster Larger Catechism
sourceMetadata.description:
During the early 1600s, Presbyterians, Congregationalists, and Baptists suffered repeated cycles of persecution at the hands of the Church of England and the crown. The Puritans arose to defend Biblical worship. During the resulting civil war (1642-1649), hierarchical parishes and bishops were abolished by the then Puritan Parliament. A special assembly was appointed to draft a new structure; it met at the historic Westminster Abbey (adjoining the Houses of Parliament) in London. The Westminster Assembly held 1,163 sessions between July 1, 1643, and February 22, 1649.

This Westminster Confession was drafted for the Church of England, and has become the most important of the great Protestant creeds of the Reformation era. It is a summary of major Christian beliefs in thirty-three chapters. Classic reformed biblical theology permeates the confession, with emphasis on the covenant relationships between God and man. A Larger Catechism was prepared by the Westminster Assembly, to be used by ministers in the pulpit for public teaching (1648). A Shorter Catechism was published for instructing children.

sourceMetadata.title: Fatherhood
sourceMetadata.description:
Matthew Henry said, “Masters of families, who preside in the other affairs of the house, must go before their households in the things of God. They must be as prophets, priests, and kings in their own families; and as such they must keep up family-doctrine, family-worship, and family-discipline.” The master of a family in Henry’s time was the male head of a household—usually a husband or father. The Reformers and Puritans often spoke of fathers this way. The biblical vision of fatherhood that arises from the pages of Scripture is beautiful, majestic, and holy. It is also foreign to the day in which we live.

As Henry points out, fathers “must go before their households in the things of God.” The biblical picture of a father is of one who leads his family according to the Word of God. He is a representative of God and Christ. This means that he must be a man of prayer, of the Word, and of humble holiness. By faith in Christ, trusting in His grace, empowered by His Spirit, and informed by the Word, a father must keep up “family doctrine.” This means he should be able to teach his family the truths of God’s Word. He must keep up “family worship.” His home must be a place where he leads his loved ones in the worship of the thrice-holy Triune God, in prayer, in the reading of Scripture, and in song. And he must keep up “family discipline.” That is, he must govern his home under Christ, blessing the obedient and chastening the disobedient—all under the grace, mercy, and love of Jesus Christ the Lord. He must learn from Christ, walk with Christ, and model Christ’s truth in his home.

Do we understand fatherhood this way? Along with many other biblical doctrines, the biblical doctrine of fatherhood has fallen on hard times. Our decaying and perverse culture needs a mighty generation of biblical fathers to rise up from the ashes of authoritarianism, abdicationism, selfism, feminism, and same-sex-ism to follow Christ, whatever the cost.

With this in mind, we offer the latest issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster, Fatherhood. William Gurnall briefly introduces us to this subject by describing a father’s roles as a prophet to instruct the family, a king to govern the family, and a priest to lead the family in the worship of God. Arthur W. Pink then helps us understand that fatherhood is a responsibility and a privilege, as a father instructs his children, models the Christian life for them, disciplines them, and prays for them. John Calvin explains a father’s main responsibility. Richard Baxter writes that, in order to properly lead a family for Christ, a father must understand and maintain biblical authority in his home, skill in governing, and holiness of life. We then learn from Nicholas Byfield that a father must be godly. What does this look like? Byfield tells us by giving us a list of signs by which fathers may identify Christ’s work in their hearts. To be a “prophet” in his home, a father must teach the Word of God, says Thomas Doolittle; and to be effectual in that good work, he, as a “priest,” must be a man of prayer. Every father knows that bringing up children in the nurture and admonition of the Lord is a difficult task; for this reason, William Gouge discusses the loving discipline that a father must exercise as “king” in his home. However, Thomas Watson makes abundantly clear that fathers must act prudently toward their children: otherwise, they can provoke them to wrath. Having considered all this, what practical steps can a man take to accomplish it? Richard Baxter gives clear, helpful, biblical counsel to fathers who would reform their families in the name of Jesus Christ. Finally, George Swinnock concludes this subject with an earnest, heartfelt prayer to be the father that Christ has saved him to be.

children.title: Paternidad
children.description:
Matthew Henry dijo: “Los jefes de familia, que dirigen los otros asuntos de la casa, deben también hacerlo con las cosas de Dios. Tienen que ser como profetas, sacerdotes y reyes en sus propias familias; y como tales, mantener el adoctrinamiento familiar, la adoración familiar y la disciplina familiar”. El jefe de la familia, en la época de Henry, realmente actuaba como cabeza del hogar, ya fuera como padre o como esposo. Los reformadores y puritanos se referían, a menudo, a los padres de familia como tales. La visión bíblica de la paternidad que surge de las páginas de las Escrituras es hermosa, majestuosa y santa. Es también muy extraña para la época en que vivimos.

Como destaca Henry, los padres deben dirigir su hogar en lo que respecta a las cosas de Dios. El perfil bíblico de un padre lo define como aquel que lidera a su familia de acuerdo con la Palabra de Dios. Él es el representante de Dios y Cristo. Esto significa que tiene que ser un hombre de oración, estudioso asiduo de la Palabra y de humilde santidad. Por su fe en Cristo, confiando en su gracia, dotado de poder por el Espíritu de Dios e informado por la Palabra, el padre debe inculcar y mantener la “doctrina familiar”. Esto significa que debiera ser capaz de enseñar a su familia las verdades de la Palabra de Dios. Debe practicar el “culto familiar”. Su hogar tiene que ser un lugar donde dirige a sus seres queridos en la adoración, del Trino Dios tres veces santo, en la oración, en la lectura de la Escrituras y en el canto. Y debe mantener la “disciplina familiar”. Esto significa que debe gobernar su hogar bajo Cristo, bendiciendo al obediente y castigando al desobediente; todo bajo la gracia, misericordia y el amor de Jesucristo el Señor. Debe aprender de Cristo, andar con Cristo y ser un modelo de la verdad de Cristo en su hogar.

¿Entendemos la paternidad de esta manera? Al igual que muchas otras doctrinas bíblicas, la de la paternidad está atravesando tiempos difíciles. Nuestra cultura decadente y perversa necesita una generación poderosa de padres de familia que se levante de las cenizas de autoritarismo, egocentrismo, feminismo y  toda clase de “ismos” que van en contra de los valores bíblicos necesarios para seguir a Cristo, cueste lo que cueste.

Con esto en mente, ofrecemos este número de Portavoz de la Gracia sobre la paternidad. William Gurnall nos presenta este tema brevemente, describiendo las funciones de un padre como profeta para instruir a la familia, un rey para gobernarla y un sacerdote para dirigir a la familia en la adoración a Dios. Arthur W. Pink luego nos ayuda a comprender que la paternidad es una responsabilidad y un privilegio. El padre cumple su papel al instruir a sus hijos, serles un modelo de la vida cristiana; disciplinándolos y orando por ellos. Juan Calvino explica la responsabilidad principal del padre. Richard Baxter escribe que, a fin de guiar correctamente a la familia para Cristo, el padre necesita la habilidad para gobernar, comprender lo que es la autoridad bíblica en su hogar y tener como un estilo de vida la santidad. Luego aprendemos de Nicholas Byfield que el padre tiene que ser piadoso. ¿Cómo se manifiesta esto? El autor nos lo dice dándonos una lista de señales que nos ayudan a identificar la obra de Cristo en sus corazones. Para ser “profeta” en su hogar, el padre tiene que enseñar la Palabra de Dios, dice Thomas Doolittle, y para ser eficaz en esa buena obra, él, como “sacerdote”, tiene que ser un hombre de oración. Cada padre de familia sabe que criar a los hijos en las enseñanzas de la Palabra, el amor y los consejos del Señor es una tarea difícil; por esta razón William Gouge escribe sobre la disciplina amorosa que el padre debe practicar como “rey” en su hogar. No obstante, Thomas Watson hace ver muy claro que los padres deben actuar con prudencia con sus hijos: de otra manera, pueden provocarlos a ira. Habiendo considerado todo esto, ¿qué pasos prácticos puede tomar el hombre para cumplir su papel? Richard Baxter comparte consejos claros, provechosos y bíblicos a los padres para que puedan reformar a sus familias en el nombre de Jesucristo. Por último, George Swinnock concluye este tema con una oración sincera y de corazón pidiendo al Señor que lo salvó que le ayude a ser el padre que ha sido llamado a ser.  

Si encuentra usted, bíblicos y provechosos estos artículos, por favor súmese a nosotros en orar que Dios el Padre quiera, por medio de la persona y obra de su Hijo y el poder de su Espíritu Santo, levantar a una generación poderosa de padres piadosos: Hombres que aman a Cristo, estudian su Palabra y están llenos de su Espíritu. Necesitamos hombres que amen a su esposa como Cristo ama a la Iglesia y que formen a sus hijos basados en las enseñanzas y los consejos del Señor. Padres comprados por sangre, llenos del Espíritu; nuestras familias los necesitan, nuestras iglesias los necesitan y nuestras comunidades los necesitan. Cuando nuestro bendito Padre celestial se propuso salvar a su pueblo perdonándoles sus pecados, cuando Cristo el Hijo vivió, murió y resucitó para salvarlos, y cuando el Espíritu Santo aplica su gran poder regenerador a sus vidas, no es que Dios esté solo redimiendo a pecadores, sino que estaba y está redimiendo también la paternidad. Quiera Dios que la visión hermosa y bíblica que tuvo Matthew Henry de la paternidad se convierta en una realidad en la actualidad.

sourceMetadata.title: The London Baptist Confession of Faith of 1689 with Preface, Baptist Catechism, and Appendix on Baptism
sourceMetadata.description: The London Baptist Confession of 1677/89 played an important role in Baptist history. The Act of Uniformity of 1662 made the new Anglican Prayer Book mandatory for use in all Anglican, Presbyterian, Congregationalist, and Baptist churches in England. Moreover, the Anglican church abandoned the Westminster Confession and returned to the Thirty-Nine Articles as its official confession of faith. Consequently, with the restoration of the Monarchy, the English Baptists suffered persecution for their faith. In 1677, a group of Particular Baptists met for the purpose of producing a more expansive confession than the previous Baptist confession of 1644. They modeled the Second London Confession on the Westminster Confession, but with significant theological differences regarding church government and baptism. Persecution kept the 1677 document from being officially endorsed by Particular Baptists until 1689, when the Toleration Act was passed. This act enabled religious freedom to co-exist alongside the established churches in England and Scotland. As a result, representatives from over 100 Particular Baptist churches met in London from July 3-11 to discuss and endorse the 1677 document. Though the confession was published in 1677, the General Assembly of Particular Baptist Churches adopted it in 1689; hence it is commonly known as “the 1689.” The Westminster Confession, the Savoy Declaration, and the London Baptist Confession of 1677/89 are considered the most important Reformed confessions arising from the English-speaking world.

sourceMetadata.title: Fellowship with the Trinity
sourceMetadata.description: As believers in the Lord Jesus Christ, we should have conscious fellowship with God our Father, Christ our Savior and the Holy Spirit our Sanctifier. John Owen wrote Of Communion with God the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost in 1657. For many readers, it has become their favorite devotional work of the Puritans and perhaps of all time. It was certainly so for Erroll Hulse. In writing Fellowship with the Trinity, he sought to capture Owen’s main ideas in order to make the work more accessible to everyone.

sourceMetadata.title: Thoughts for Young Men
sourceMetadata.description:
About Thoughts for Young Men:  “When St. Paul wrote his Epistle to Titus about his duty as a minister, he mentioned young men as a class requiring peculiar attention. After speaking of aged men and aged women, and young women, he adds this pithy advice—“Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded” (Tit 2:6). I am going to follow the Apostle’s advice. I propose to offer a few words of friendly exhortation to young men.

“I am growing old myself, but there are few things I remember so well as the days of my youth. I have a most distinct recollection of the joys and the sorrows, the hopes and the fears, the temptations and the difficulties, the mistaken judgments and the misplaced affections, the errors and the aspirations, which surround and accompany a young man’s life. If I can only say something to keep some young man in the right way, and preserve him from faults and sins, which may mar his prospects both for time and eternity, I shall be very thankful.” —J. C. Ryle

children.title: Pensamientos para hombres jóvenes
children.description: Reflexiones para los hombres jóvenes: “Cuando San Pablo escribió su Epístola a Tito acerca de su deber como ministro, mencionó a los jóvenes como una clase que requiere atención especial. Después de hablar de hombres ancianos y mujeres ancianas, y de mujeres jóvenes, agrega este consejo conciso: "Exhorta asimismo a los jóvenes a que sean prudentes" (Tit. 2: 6). Voy a seguir el consejo del apóstol. Propongo ofrecer algunas palabras de exhortación amistosa a los jóvenes. “Yo también estoy envejeciendo, pero hay pocas cosas que recuerdo tan bien como los días de mi juventud. Recuerdo claramente las alegrías y las tristezas, las esperanzas y los miedos, las tentaciones y las dificultades, los juicios equivocados y los afectos equivocados, los errores y las aspiraciones que rodean y acompañan la vida de un joven. Si solo puedo decir algo para mantener a un joven en el camino correcto y preservarlo de las faltas y los pecados, lo que puede arruinar sus perspectivas tanto en el tiempo como en la eternidad, estaré muy agradecido ". —J. C. Ryle

files.description:
About Thoughts for Young Men:  “When St. Paul wrote his Epistle to Titus about his duty as a minister, he mentioned young men as a class requiring peculiar attention. After speaking of aged men and aged women, and young women, he adds this pithy advice—“Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded” (Tit 2:6). I am going to follow the Apostle’s advice. I propose to offer a few words of friendly exhortation to young men.

“I am growing old myself, but there are few things I remember so well as the days of my youth. I have a most distinct recollection of the joys and the sorrows, the hopes and the fears, the temptations and the difficulties, the mistaken judgments and the misplaced affections, the errors and the aspirations, which surround and accompany a young man’s life. If I can only say something to keep some young man in the right way, and preserve him from faults and sins, which may mar his prospects both for time and eternity, I shall be very thankful.” —J. C. Ryle

files.title: Fleeing Out of Sodom
files.author: Jonathan Edwards
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Fleeing Out of Sodom
sourceMetadata.description: In this sermon, Jonathan Edwards gives a number of reasons why the story of Lot’s fleeing out of Sodom is a picture of fleeing to Christ from the state of sin and misery. He notes that those who flee ought not to look back. Sodom is a city full of filthiness and abominations with nothing worth looking back upon, and it is a city appointed to swift and sudden destruction—a destruction that will be exceedingly dreadful, universal, and everlasting. Edwards solemnly warns those who are in a “natural condition” to flee, pointing out that the world is divided into two cities—the holy and beloved city of Zion, and the polluted and accursed city of Sodom. He underscores the gravity of his warning with this chilling truth: He who is out of Christ is in Sodom.

children.title: Fuir Sodome
children.description: Dans ce sermon, Jonathan Edwards donne un certain nombre de raisons pour lesquelles la fuite de Lot hors de Sodome est une image de notre fuite vers Christ, hors de notre état de péché et de misère. Il observe que ceux qui fuient ne doivent pas regarder en arrière. Sodome est une ville remplie de souillures et d’abominations qui ne mérite pas un seul regard en arrière. C’est une ville destinée à une destruction rapide et soudaine—une destruction qui sera infiniment épouvantable, universelle et éternelle. Edwards appelle solennellement ceux qui se trouvent dans leur « condition naturelle » à fuir, faisant remarquer que ce monde est divisé en deux cités : la sainte et bien-aimée Sion, et la souillée et maudite cité de Sodome. Il souligne la gravité de son avertissement par cette vérité effrayante : Celui qui est hors de Christ demeure en réalité en Sodome.

children.title: Pensamientos para los jóvenes
children.description:
En este número del Portavoz de la Gracia, Archibald Alexander presenta nuestro tema con un excelente consejo bíblico para los jóvenes. Plantea una importante colección de pensamientos desde la necesidad de un carácter consistente hasta la preparación para la muerte. Después de esto, J. C. Ryle da otra colección de exhortaciones reflexivas y provocativas, enfocándose en la necesidad de una persona joven de entender el pecado, el Salvador, la oración y la Palabra de Dios, además de ser cautelosos en la elección de amigos. John Angell James advierte a los jóvenes acerca de los pecados de su época, que no son diferentes de los pecados de los jóvenes de nuestros días. El apóstol Pablo instruyó a Tito a exhortar a los jóvenes a ser sobrios (Tito 2:6). A la luz de esto, Matthew Henry brinda persuasiones bíblicas, aleccionadoras y alentadoras para que los hombres y mujeres jóvenes cultiven la sobriedad. ¿Qué casa puede soportar peleas constantes entre hermanos y hermanas? ¿Cómo deben tratarse los hermanos? John Angell James brinda una discusión útil sobre este asunto. El puritano Tomás Vicente exhorta con fervor a los jóvenes que profesan la fe en Cristo a ser firmes y no desviarse. Explica sabiamente los motivos y da instrucciones para evitar la declinación y la apostasía. Con una prédica característica centrada en Cristo, Charles Spurgeon exhorta a los jóvenes a que dejen de poner excusas y crean en Cristo Jesús para vida eterna.

'In  Thy  presence  is  fullness  of  joy,  at  Thy  right  hand  are  pleasures  forevermore.' "

sourceMetadata.title: True Gospel, The
sourceMetadata.description: The gospel is a marvelous display of mercy to sinners, having its beginning in the sovereign, free grace of God, and proclaimed to mankind solely through the merits of the righteousness, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. The gospel considers all men as lost and helpless in the accomplishment of their own salvation. Not only this, but Hawker points out that each person is utterly undeserving of the divine favor shown in salvation. Having received the gospel, the believer ought to seek to imitate Christ by inviting sinners to come to Him for life and salvation as he himself has received it. Let every believer’s heart echo the heavenly invitation “Return, thou backslider, and I will heal your backsliding.”

files.title: For Whom Did Christ Die?
files.author: Charles H. Spurgeon
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: For Whom Did Christ Die?
sourceMetadata.description: Charles Spurgeon asks a very important question: for whom did Christ die? The straight-forward answer is given in Romans 5:6—for the ungodly. Expanding on this truth, he first lays out the hopeless condition of the ungodly, moving from there to the truth that Christ died for sinners just like them, and on to the plain inferences that may be drawn from this. For the ungodly these inferences are twofold. First, they are already under God’s wrath and in great danger. Second, only Christ can deliver them out of this danger and only through His death. Spurgeon concludes by addressing the believers in his congregation, urging them to make the truth of Romans 5:6 the central message of their lives. Turning to the unsaved, his plea is simple: “There is life in a look at the crucified One…look to Him now and live.”

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained

sourceMetadata.title: True vs. False Gospel
sourceMetadata.description: The True Gospel of Christ versus the False Gospel of Carnal Christianity examines in detail the common modern message sometimes called “easy-believism,” where justification in Christ is presented without mention of one’s responsibility to forsake sin and live set apart from the world. This gospel holds that one may “make a decision” to “receive Christ,” without bowing to His authority over one’s life. The problem is that many conclude: “a little sin won’t hurt—I’m just carnal, and God has saved me any way.” This false gospel leaves the professing Christian without any power over sin and a false confidence in heaven, even to the point of resisting calls to repent because “I don’t need to; I’m already saved.” Romans 6 is used to develop a Biblical understanding of self-denial, and passages in 1 and 2 Timothy are used to explain the deceitful nature of selfish sin. Finally, the book explores the rich new life provided in the true Gospel of Scripture.

children.title: El verdadero evangelio... versus evangelio falso
children.description: El Verdadero Evangelio de Cristo contra el Falso Evangelio del cristianismo carnal examina en detalle el mensaje moderno común a veces llamado "fácil de creer", donde se presenta la justificación en Cristo sin mencionar la responsabilidad de uno de abandonar el pecado y vivir separado del mundo. Este evangelio sostiene que uno puede "tomar una decisión" de "recibir a Cristo", sin inclinarse ante su autoridad sobre la vida de uno. El problema es que muchos concluyen: "un pequeño pecado no dolerá; solo soy carnal, y Dios me ha salvado de cualquier manera". Este falso evangelio deja al cristiano que profesa sin poder sobre el pecado y una falsa confianza en el cielo, incluso hasta el punto de resistir los llamados a arrepentirse porque “no necesito hacerlo; Ya estoy salvado ”. Romanos 6 se usa para desarrollar una comprensión bíblica de la negación propia, y los pasajes en 1 y 2 Timoteo se usan para explicar la naturaleza engañosa del pecado egoísta. Finalmente, el libro explora la nueva y rica vida provista en el verdadero Evangelio de las Escrituras.

sourceMetadata.title: Forgiveness
sourceMetadata.description: Who needs forgiveness and why? According to J. C. Ryle, the short answer is that all men need forgiveness because all are sinners. He elaborates on this at some length and then offers a concise summary, “The first step towards heaven is to see clearly that we deserve hell. There are but two alternatives before us: we must either be forgiven, or be miserable forever.” He next addresses the question of how we are forgiven. Speaking directly to the unsaved, he implores them, “Cast your soul, with all its sins, unreservedly on Christ; cease completely from any dependence on your own works.” After describing several characteristics of those who have been forgiven—they hate sin, they love Christ, they are humble, holy, and forgiving—Ryle ends with a solemn warning to those who know they are not forgiven, and a word of exhortation to those who are.

sourceMetadata.description: Intellectual faith can neither save nor sanctify: it is not faith, but unbelief. The only saving faith links us with a living Savior. Faith is the gift of God, the result of the Holy Spirit’s direct quickening power. Bonar warns us to beware of new theology which simplifies faith to bring it within reach of the unregenerate, thus making man the initiator of his salvation. This is a denial of the Spirit’s work, an impassable obstacle to true salvation.

sourceMetadata.title: Formality
sourceMetadata.description: J. C. Ryle here presents a comparison of “formal religion” and true religion. Based on 2 Timothy 3:5 and Romans 2:28-29, he indicates that we may learn three basic lessons as we study these two texts. In the first place, we learn that formal religion (that which is based on outward manifestations only) is not true religion and that a formal Christian is not a Christian in God’s sight. Secondly, we learn that the heart is the seat of true religion and that the true Christian is the Christian in heart. Thirdly, we learn that true religion must never expect to be popular—it will not have the “praise of man, but of God.” Ryle ends by addressing three types of people—formal Christians, those under conviction of sin, and true believers—offering wise counsel to each.

sourceMetadata.title: Fury Not In God
sourceMetadata.description: In Fury Not in God, Thomas Chalmers contrasts God's present merciful entreaties to His judgment day fury. Today men may have salvation from God's just fury despite their sin. The Judgment Day is coming; "the burning up of this earth and the passing away of these heavens is an event in the history of God's administration to which we are continually drawing nearer." But fury is not yet in God; it is not yet to be unleashed. God in His mercy has stretched forth "mighty strength that had to be put forth in the work of a sinner's justification."

sourceMetadata.title: Warrant of Faith, The
sourceMetadata.description: Spurgeon deals with two questions about faith in this sermon. What is it that a man is to believe in order to eternal life? The faith which saves is a belief in a person, depending upon Jesus for eternal life. What is our warrant for coming to Christ? The gospel command is a sufficient warrant for a sinner to believe in Jesus Christ. This is the commandment, that ye “believe on his Son Jesus Christ.”

sourceMetadata.title: What Is a Biblical Christian?
sourceMetadata.description:
What Is a Biblical Christian? is a pointed and extremely helpful inquiry into the true state of the soul. The author asks: “According to the Scriptures, when does a man, woman, boy or girl have the right to the name Christian? One must not make the assumption lightly that he or she is a true Christian. A false conclusion at this point is tragic and fatal. Therefore I want to set before you four strands of the Bible’s answer to the question: What is a Biblical Christian? ”

Albert N. Martin served for forty-six years from 1962 to 2008 as pastor of Trinity Baptist Church of Montville, New Jersey. His teaching ministry is known for thorough and powerful exposition of God’s Word. Today he serves in writing and conference ministry from his home in Michigan.

children.title: ¿Qué es un cristiano bíblico?
children.description:
¿Qué es un cristiano bíblico? es una investigación puntual y extremadamente útil sobre el verdadero estado del alma. El autor se pregunta: “De acuerdo a las Escrituras, ¿Cuándo tiene un hombre, mujer, niño o niña derecho al nombre de cristiano? Uno no debe asumir a la ligera que él o ella es un verdadero cristiano. Una conclusión falsa en este punto es trágica y fatal. Por lo tanto, quiero presentarles cuatro líneas de la respuesta de la Biblia a la pregunta: ¿Qué es un cristiano bíblico?

Albert N. Martin servido durante cuarenta y seis años, de 1962 a 2008, como pastor de la Iglesia Bautista Trinity de Montville, New Jersey. Su ministerio de enseñanza es conocido por la exposición completa y poderosa de la Palabra de Dios. Hoy sirve en el ministerio de escribir y conferencias desde su casa en Michigan.

children.title: Mkhristu ndi ndani?
children.description:
Pa umoyo wathu pali zinthu zambiri zimene munthu utakhala osazidziwa kapena osazilabadira sizingakubweretsere tsoka kapena ngozi. Ndi ochepa mwa ife amene tingathe kufotokoza njira imene ng’ombe yokuda imadya udzu wobiriwira kuti ipange mkaka woyera—koma tonsefe mkakawo timawukonda ndithu. Ambiri a ife sitidziwa mfundo zozama zaukachenjede wa nyengo ndi dziko ndipo wina atatipanikiza kuti tipereke yankho, zikhoza kutivuta zedi. Koma kusadziwa zonsezi sikutibweretsera tsoka kapena ngozi pamoyo wathu.
Komatu zilipo zinthu zina zoti kusazidziwa kapena kusazilabadira kungakhale tsoka ndi ngozi angakhale imfa imene. Chimodzi mwa zinthuzi ndi yankho la funso lakuti, “Mkhristu ndi ndani?” Kapena kuti, “Kodi Mau a Mulungu anena kuti pachitike chiyani kuti munthu atchulidwe Mkhristu”?
Munthu payekha asangoganizira mwachisawawa kuti iye ndi Mkhristu woona. Kutsimikiza mosalondola pa mfundo iyi ndi ngozi komanso tsoka. N’chifukwa chake ndikufuna ndikupatseni mfundo zinayi zochokera mu Baibulo zomwe zili mayankho a funso lakuti, “Mkhristu ndi ndani?”

sourceMetadata.title: What Is Christianity?
sourceMetadata.description: Mackintosh discusses Philippians 3, which gives us the model of a true Christian: his standing, his object, and his hope. In light of the gospel, the legalist must cast aside his own righteousness, having found a better righteousness in Christ. Sins may drive the sinner to Christ, but more importantly, Christ’s excellencies draw us to Him. Mackintosh shows the object is to know Christ, to fix our gaze on Him. With Christ as our righteousness, we long to know Him, and more ardently seek to be like Him.

children.title: ¿Qué es el cristianismo?
children.description:
El tercer capitulo de Filipenses nos da el modelo de un cristiano verdadero.

  1. La posición del cristiano
  2. El objetivo del cristiano
  3. La esperanza del cristiano

Mackintosh analiza Filipenses 3, pasaje que nos presenta el modelo del verdadero cristiano: su posición, su objetivo y su esperanza. A la luz del evangelio, el legalista debe dejar de lado su propia justicia, tras haber hallado una justicia superior en Cristo. Si bien los pecados pueden llevar al pecador hacia Cristo, lo más importante es que las excelencias de Cristo nos atraen hacia Él. Mackintosh señala que el objetivo es conocer a Cristo y fijar la mirada en Él. Al tener a Cristo como nuestra justicia, anhelamos conocerle y procuramos con mayor fervor ser como Él.

files.title: What Is It to Preach the Gospel?
files.author: Henry Mahan
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: What Is It to Preach the Gospel?
sourceMetadata.description: The apostle Paul was perhaps the greatest preacher we are told of in Scripture, doing everything, throughout his life, good or bad, with all of his heart. When it came to preaching the gospel, he preached seriously, simply, sincerely, and boldly in the power of the Holy Spirit. But what is it to truly preach the gospel? Mahan answers that preaching the gospel is to tell the truth about God, His character, and His attributes. Preaching the gospel requires the truth to be told about man and his condition before God, as well as the truth about Christ and His work to accomplish our salvation. A true preacher cannot glory in his preaching, for he is conscious of his own guilt, and his message is not his own. Woe is pronounced against the preacher who will not preach the gospel, and the sinner who will not hear it.

sourceMetadata.title: What It Means to Be Really "Born Again"
sourceMetadata.description: Many people today claim to be saved and on the way to heaven but have never truly submitted themselves to the authority of Christ. However, Scripture commands that we “give all diligence” to God’s warning to examine ourselves, “search and try our ways”, and “make our calling and election sure”. Herendeen examines the actions, thoughts and desires that regenerate Christians will pursue. Self-examination, controlling the tongue, and forsaking sins, among many other things, are all things true Christians will do. He encourages every reader to examine his heart, and make sure his profession is not a lie. It is not enough to be outwardly religious. To be truly acceptable to God, all we do and say and think must come from a hear that loves and delights in doing God’s will cheerfully.

sourceMetadata.title: Godly Manhood
sourceMetadata.description:
We need godly men. And they only appear by the miraculous work of God's Holy Spirit known as "the new birth." The "power of God unto salvation" transforms lives: it mightily changes those who are unclean, impure, deceitful, and degenerate and gives them new hearts. The Holy Spirit can blow upon the "valley of dry bones"—our culturized, impotent, religious males to create a generation of godly men who look like Jesus Christ.

Within the pages of this Free Grace Broadcaster lies a wealth of practical, Biblical application for the transformation of men into the image of the greatest Man, Jesus Christ. Godly Manhood begins as Benjamin Keach describes true godliness as an allegorical character similar to Pilgrim in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress. Richard Steele follows with a wonderful summary of the "upright man." Thomas Watson then uses his "Scripture pencil" to draw a portrait of the signs and character of a godly man. Few treatises on husbands loving their wives can compare with William Gouge's wonderful biblical directives on this subject. While Samuel Lee is not well-known, his discourse on the conversion of family members shimmers with rays of Biblical instruction. John Gill warns us of the tragic consequences of a father's sinful anger. Then John Angell James warns young men of many dangers that threaten their growth in godliness. And finally, Charles Spurgeon points us to the only hope for a restoration of godly manhood, the Man Christ Jesus.

children.title: Hombres piadosos
children.description:
Necesitamos hombres piadosos. Y estos solo surgen mediante la obra milagrosa del Espíritu Santo de Dios, conocida como «el nuevo nacimiento». El «poder de Dios para salvación» transforma vidas: cambia poderosamente a aquellos que son inmundos, impuros, engañosos y degenerados, y les otorga corazones nuevos. El Espíritu Santo puede soplar sobre el «valle de los huesos secos» —nuestros varones religiosos, impotentes y moldeados por la cultura— para crear una generación de hombres piadosos que se asemejen a Jesucristo.

Entre las páginas de este Portavoz de la Gracia se halla una riqueza de aplicaciones prácticas y bíblicas para la transformación de los hombres a la imagen del Hombre por excelencia: Jesucristo. El tema de la «Hombres piadosos» comienza con Benjamin Keach, quien describe la verdadera piedad mediante un personaje alegórico, similar al Peregrino de la obra El progreso del peregrino, de Bunyan. A continuación, Richard Steele ofrece un maravilloso resumen sobre el «hombre íntegro». Luego, Thomas Watson utiliza su «lápiz de las Escrituras» para trazar un retrato de las señales y el carácter de un hombre piadoso. Pocos tratados sobre el amor de los esposos hacia sus esposas pueden compararse con las maravillosas directrices bíblicas que William Gouge ofrece sobre este tema. Aunque Samuel Lee no sea muy conocido, su disertación sobre la conversión de los miembros de la familia resplandece con los rayos de la instrucción bíblica. John Gill nos advierte sobre las trágicas consecuencias de la ira pecaminosa de un padre. Seguidamente, John Angell James alerta a los jóvenes sobre los muchos peligros que amenazan su crecimiento en la piedad. Y, por último, Charles Spurgeon nos señala la única esperanza para la restauración de la masculinidad piadosa: el Hombre Cristo Jesús.

files.description:
We need godly men. And they only appear by the miraculous work of God's Holy Spirit known as "the new birth." The "power of God unto salvation" transforms lives: it mightily changes those who are unclean, impure, deceitful, and degenerate and gives them new hearts. The Holy Spirit can blow upon the "valley of dry bones"—our culturized, impotent, religious males to create a generation of godly men who look like Jesus Christ.

Within the pages of this Free Grace Broadcaster lies a wealth of practical, Biblical application for the transformation of men into the image of the greatest Man, Jesus Christ. Godly Manhood begins as Benjamin Keach describes true godliness as an allegorical character similar to Pilgrim in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress. Richard Steele follows with a wonderful summary of the "upright man." Thomas Watson then uses his "Scripture pencil" to draw a portrait of the signs and character of a godly man. Few treatises on husbands loving their wives can compare with William Gouge's wonderful biblical directives on this subject. While Samuel Lee is not well-known, his discourse on the conversion of family members shimmers with rays of Biblical instruction. John Gill warns us of the tragic consequences of a father's sinful anger. Then John Angell James warns young men of many dangers that threaten their growth in godliness. And finally, Charles Spurgeon points us to the only hope for a restoration of godly manhood, the Man Christ Jesus.

files.title: God's Grace in Justifying the Sinner
files.author: Robert Traill
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: God's Grace in Justifying the Sinner
sourceMetadata.description:
Traill shows the how the glory of God's grace abounds in the free and full justification of the sinner on the basis of the work of Christ and through faith alone.

Paul’s epistle to the Galatians is a reproof to them for their great and sudden apostasy from the gospel he had helped them to know. They were guilty of mixing works of the law with faith in justification. Traill’s text contains two of the greatest errors men can make: “frustrating the grace of God”, and “making the death of Christ to be in vain.” These come very near to the description of the unpardonable sin in Hebrews 10:29—"Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden underfoot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite to the Spirit of grace?" Using these points, Traill begins to examine what the grace of God in justification is, and what it means to frustrate this grace.

files.title: Why Are We Saved through Faith?
files.author: Charles H. Spurgeon
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Why Are We Saved through Faith?
sourceMetadata.description: The hand which receives charity does not expect to be thanked for accepting the gift. The hand doesn’t take glory for what it has done that benefits the whole body. So faith also excludes all boasting. Faith has been chosen by God to be the receiver of salvation. It is a sure method, linking man with God. Faith brings us into connection with Him. Spurgeon shows the purpose of faith in believing, and discusses several reasons why no other method will bring salvation.

children.title: ¿Por qué somos salvos por medio de la fe?
children.description: ¿Por qué es la fe el medio escogido para la salvación? Sin duda surge esta pregunta con frecuencia. “Por gracia sois salvos por medio de la fe” es por cierto una de las doctrinas de las Sagradas Escrituras y el plan de Dios; pero ¿por qué es así? ¿Por qué escogió la fe y no más bien la esperanza, el amor o la paciencia? Nos conviene responder a esta pregunta con humildad, porque los caminos de Dios no son siempre comprensibles, ni nos permite él ponerlos, arrogantemente, en telas de juicio.

files.title: Word of Salvation Sent to Sinners, The
files.author: Ralph Erskine
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Word of Salvation Sent to Sinners, The
sourceMetadata.description: Erskine preaches here on the subject of the gospel, its nature, and its intended recipient. The gospel is the word of salvation, and it is sent to every sinner who hears it. Every sinner is alienated and estranged from God by the misery of his sin. Through the work of Christ, complete redemption has been purchased and is offered freely. This word has been sent by God, but is delivered by men. “We are ambassadors for Christ.” It is sent as a healing remedy for a deadly malady. Erskine discusses the antidotes against many doctrinal errors that distort this message of salvation for sinners.

files.title: God's Purpose of Grace
files.author: Horatius Bonar
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: God's Purpose of Grace
sourceMetadata.description: God’s Purpose of Grace magnifies the grace of God in its fullness and blessedness, for both the seasoned saint and the seeker. Grace is all the more glorious in light of man’s tremendous need, without hope and without God in this world. But this need, with no merit in ourselves, is but the opening for God to pour forth His grace freely and abundantly. God’s love and justice in shedding the lifeblood of His only Son and His holiness in honoring His law are but aspects of the beauty of His grace. Bonar concludes with a clear presentation of gospel grace and how those without Christ may be joined to Him by grace through faith alone.

files.title: Word to Parents, A
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.audience: children; new believers; parents; teachers; youth
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Word to Parents, A
sourceMetadata.description: A most tragic feature of our modern civilization is the prevalence of disobedience of children to their parents in childhood, and their lack of respect for them when they grow up. Spoiled, self-willed children bring themselves into sorrow, and inflict great unhappiness on all around them. Quite often, parents are more to blame for this than children. When parents depart from the scriptural pattern, this is the result. Pink shows at least part of the problem: parents have not learned to govern themselves so cannot hope to govern their children well. Pink lays out the four principal duties of parents: instruction, leading by example, discipline, and prayer. By heeding this advice, parents may hope to raise obedient, helpful, respectful children.

children.title: Una palabra para los padres
children.description: "Una de las características más tristes y trágicas de nuestra 'civilización' del siglo XX es la terrible prevalencia de desobediencia de los hijos hacia sus padres durante los días de la niñez, y su falta de reverencia y respeto cuando crecen. Esto se evidencia de muchas maneras, y es general, lamentablemente, incluso en las familias de los que profesan ser cristianos. En sus extensos viajes durante los últimos treinta años, el escritor ha residido en un gran número de hogares: la piedad y la belleza de algunos de ellos siguen siendo recuerdos sagrados y fragantes, pero otros de ellos han dejado las impresiones más dolorosas. Los hijos que son obstinados o mimados no solo se conducen a sí mismos a la infelicidad perpetua, sino que infligen incomodidad a todos los que tienen contacto con ellos, y anuncian cosas malas para los días venideros."

children.title: Uma Palavra aos Pais
children.description: Deus confiou aos pais um mui solene, e ainda assim, um mui precioso privilégio. Não é demais dizer que em suas mãos estão depositadas a esperança e bênção, ou então a maldição e praga da próxima geração. As suas famílias são os berçários tanto da Igreja e do Estado, e de acordo com o cultivo deles agora, tal será a sua futura fecundidade. Como com oração e cuidado eles devem cumprir o que lhes está confiado. Em verdade, Deus exigirá uma prestação de contas dos filhos das mãos dos pais, pois eles são Seus, e apenas emprestados ao cuidado e manutenção deles. A tarefa atribuída a vocês não é fácil, especialmente nestes dias superlativamente maus. No entanto, se com confiança e sinceridade buscarem, a graça de Deus será encontrada suficiente aqui, como em outros casos. As Escrituras nos fornecem regras para agir, com promessas a serem apropriadas e, nós podemos acrescentar, com alertas temerosos para que não tratemos a questão com ânimo leve.

files.title: God's Way of Holiness
files.author: Horatius Bonar
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: God's Way of Holiness
sourceMetadata.description: “The way of peace and the way of holiness lie side by side, or rather, they are one. That which bestows the one imparts the other; and he who takes the one takes the other also. The Spirit of peace is the Spirit of holiness. The God of peace is the God of holiness. If at any time these paths seem to go asunder, there must be something wrong—wrong in the teaching that makes them seem to part company, or wrong in the state of the man in whose life they have done so. They start together, or at least so nearly together that no eye, save the divine, can mark a difference…The two are not independent. There is fellowship between them, vital fellowship, each being the helpmeet of the other…A spurious holiness there may be, founded upon a spurious peace, or upon no peace at all; but true holiness must start from a true and authentic peace.”                                                —from the Preface, 1864

files.title: Ye Must Be Born Again!
files.author: Thomas Boston
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Ye Must Be Born Again!
sourceMetadata.description:
In this tract, Thomas Boston challenges the reader with several pointed truths concerning regeneration.

  • Regeneration is absolutely necessary for you to do anything acceptable to God.
  • Without generation there is no faith; without faith it is impossible to please God.
  • If you are not born again, all attempts at reformation are nothing in God’s sight.
  • Prayers of the unregenerate are an abomination to the Lord.

If this is you, what should you do? According to Boston, you should “fix your thoughts upon Him offered to you in the gospel as fully suited to your case.” That is, Jesus’ death on the cross perfectly satisfied the justice of God, bringing in everlasting righteousness for repentant sinners. He ends with a stark warning, plainly stating that if one is not born again and continues in that state until death, it would have been better had he never been born at all.

children.title: Os es necesario nacer de nuevo
children.description:
En este tratado, Thomas Boston desafía al lector con varias verdades punzantes sobre la regeneración.

  • La regeneración es absolutamente necesaria para que hagas cualquier cosa aceptable para Dios.
  • Sin regeneración no hay fe; sin fe es imposible agradar a Dios.
  • Si no has nacido de nuevo, todos los intentos de reforma no son nada a los ojos de Dios.
  • Las oraciones de los no regenerados son una abominación para el Señor. Si este eres tú, ¿qué deberías hacer?
De acuerdo con Boston, debes "fijar tus pensamientos en Él tal como el evangelio lo ofrece completamente en tu caso". Es decir, la muerte de Jesús en la cruz satisfizo perfectamente la justicia de Dios, trayendo justicia eterna para los pecadores arrepentidos. Termina con una advertencia severa, declarando claramente que si uno no nace de nuevo y continúa en ese estado hasta la muerte, hubiera sido mejor que nunca hubiera nacido.

sourceMetadata.title: Young Cottager
sourceMetadata.description:
This booklet from the pen of the gifted and honoured Rev. Legh Richmond, gives a clear and sweet account of the Lord’s mercy manifested in rescuing one of His tender lambs out of the “paw of the lion.”

“Direct its course, Oh my God. May the eye that reads, and the ear that hears the record of little Jane, through the power of the Spirit of the Most Highest, each become a witness for the truth as it is in Jesus,” was his prayer.

May the Lord fulfill this petition, and use this abridged reprint for the good of many and for the glory of His Name.

children.title: La niña de la humilde cabaña
children.description: Este folleto de la pluma del dotado y honrado Reverendo Legh Richmond, da un relato claro y dulce de la misericordia del Señor manifestada en el rescate de uno de Sus tiernos corderos de la “garra del león”. “Dirije su curso, Oh mi Dios. Que el ojo que lee y el oído que escucha el registro de la pequeña Jane, a través del poder del Espíritu del Altísimo, se conviertan en testigos de la verdad tal como está en Jesús ", fue su oración. Que el Señor cumpla esta petición y use esta reimpresión abreviada para el bien de muchos y para la gloria de Su Nombre.

Then it is that sinners are converted, as the Lord Himself said, ‘I, if I be lifted up, will draw all men unto me’ (John 12:32).”

sourceMetadata.title: Young Women and Discretion
sourceMetadata.description: Walter Isenhour paints a beautiful picture of what a godly young woman looks like. Not surprisingly, this portrait directly opposes modern views of the roles and behavior of women. Isenhour comments on Titus 2:3-5 which describes older women teaching young women to “love their husbands, to love their children, to be discreet, chaste, homemakers, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God may not be blasphemed.” Throughout this tract, Isenhour expands on the admonition to be discreet, which he defines as “judicious, cautious; wise in conduct and management, especially as to matters of propriety and self-control.” He concludes with two observations: 1) a young woman who lives up to these qualities, lives a life of “nobility, beauty, usefulness and sublimity” and 2) to be a discreet woman “is more to be desired than education, fame, honor, and earthly glory.”

sourceMetadata.title: Great Judgment, The
sourceMetadata.description: The final judgment is a foundational doctrine of Christianity, and one of the most solemn. In this booklet, Charles Spurgeon sheds scriptural light on several of its aspects. Introducing his subject, he shows that the great judgment follows immediately after the resurrection of the dead so that they may be judged in their bodies. He goes on to indicate in the first place that no one escapes this final accounting, for every person who has ever lived will be judged; secondly, that the judge is none other than Jesus Christ Himself; thirdly, that the basis of judgment consists of those things done in the body; and finally, he describes the outcome—“the Lord will grant unto His people an abundant reward for all that they have done” and unto the ungodly the eternal punishment due to their sinful deeds. Spurgeon is quick to point out that the righteous do not deserve any reward, but that “God first gave them grace to do good works, then took their good works as evidence of a renewed heart, and then gave them a reward for what they had done.” He sums it all up this way, “…sin is hell and holiness is heaven.” And ends with an impassioned plea, “Oh, that we may have grace, every one of us, to flee to Christ. There is our only safety.”
