children.title: Juicio final, El
children.description: El juicio final es una doctrina fundamental del cristianismo, y una de las más solemnes. En este folleto, Charles Spurgeon arroja luz bíblica sobre varios de sus aspectos. Al presentar su tema, muestra que el gran juicio sigue inmediatamente después de la resurrección de los muertos para que puedan ser juzgados en sus cuerpos. Continúa indicando, en primer lugar, que nadie escapa a esta contabilidad final, ya que cada persona que haya vivido será juzgada; en segundo lugar, que el juez no es otro que Jesucristo mismo; en tercer lugar, que la base del juicio consiste en aquellas cosas que se hacen en el cuerpo; y finalmente, describe el resultado: "el Señor otorgará a su pueblo una recompensa abundante por todo lo que hayan hecho" y al impío el castigo eterno debido a sus acciones pecaminosas. Spurgeon señala rápidamente que los justos no merecen ninguna recompensa, sino que "Dios les dio gracia para hacer buenas obras, luego tomaron sus buenas obras como evidencia de un corazón renovado y luego les dió una recompensa por lo que habían hecho ". Lo resume todo de esta manera," ... pecado es infierno y santidad es cielo ". Y termina con una súplica apasionada:" Oh, que tengamos gracia, cada uno de nosotros, para correr a Cristo. Ahí está nuestra única seguridad".

children.title: Le jugement dernier
children.description: Le Jugement Dernier est une doctrine fondamentale du Christianisme, et une des plus solennelles. Dans ce livret, Charles Spurgeon examine à la lumière des Écritures plusieurs de ses aspects. Pour introduire le sujet, il nous montre que le Jugement Dernier suit directement la résurrection des morts, afin qu’ils soient jugés dans leurs corps. Il continue en indiquant premièrement que personne n’échappera à cet arrêté, car toute personne ayant vécu sur cette terre sera jugée. Deuxièmement, il montre que le juge sera Jésus-Christ, et aucun autre. Troisièmement, que ce jugement sera basé sur les actions faites dans ce corps. Pour finir, il en décrit le dénouement : « le Seigneur accordera à son peuple une généreuse récompense pour tout ce qu’il a accompli, et le châtiment éternel pour l’impie selon ses mauvaises œuvres  ». Spurgeon nous fait remarquer que le juste ne mérite aucune récompense mais que « Dieu lui donne premièrement la grâce d’accomplir toute œuvre bonne ; ses œuvres bonnes sont ensuite acceptées comme preuve d’un cœur renouvelé ; alors enfin Dieu lui donne une récompense pour ce qu’il a accompli ». Il résume tout cela ainsi : « …l’enfer, c’est le péché ; le ciel, la sainteté. » Il termine par un appel passionné : « Oh que nous recevions la grâce, pour chacun d’entre nous, de fuir vers Christ. Il est notre seul refuge ».

sourceMetadata.title: Catecismo de Spurgeon
sourceMetadata.description:
Spurgeon editó el Catecismo Bautista para su propia congregación en 1855, cuando tenía 21 años. En el 14 de octubre de 1855, Charles Spurgeon predicó sermón N º 46 a varios miles que se reunieron para escucharlo en Capilla New Park Street. La publicación sermón contenía un anuncio de este Catecismo. El texto que mañana era: "Señor, tú has sido nuestro refugio de generación en generación" (Sal 90, 1).

 "Estoy convencido de que el uso de un buen catecismo en todas nuestras familias será una gran salvaguardia contra las crecientes errores de los tiempos, y por lo tanto he compilado este pequeño manual de Catecismos de la Asamblea Westminster y Catecismos Bautistas, para el uso de mi propia iglesia y congregación. Aquellos que lo utilizan en sus familias o en leciones deben de esfuerzarse  para explicar el sentido; pero las palabras deben ser aprendidas cuidadosamente de corazón, porque ellas serán comprendidas mejor como años pase. Que el Señor bendiga mis queridos amigos y sus familias cada vez más ... "-C. H. Spurgeon

parent.title: Spurgeon's Catechism
parent.description:
Spurgeon edited the Baptist Catechism for his own congregation in 1855, when he was 21 years old. On October 14, 1855, Charles Spurgeon preached Sermon No. 46 to several thousand gathered to hear him at New Park Street Chapel. The sermon publication contained an announcement of this Catechism. The text that morning was: “Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations” (Psa 90:1).

“I am persuaded that the use of a good Catechism in all our families will be a great safeguard against the increasing errors of the times, and therefore I have compiled this little manual...for the use of my own church and congregation. Those who use it in their families or classes must labor to explain the sense; but the words should be carefully learned by heart, for they will be understood better as years pass. May the Lord bless my dear friends and their families evermore…”—C. H. Spurgeon

The Baptist Catechism was written in 1693 by William Collins and Benjamin Keach for teaching the doctrines of the London Baptist Confession of 1689. By 1738, this catechism was adopted by the Philadelphia Association of Baptists in America, the spiritual parent of all Baptist churches in the USA. Spurgeon edited and reprinted it in 1855, shortening the expositions of the Ten Commandments and the Lord’s Prayer. Thus, the catechism you hold in your hand is in essence the one used by Baptists in English-speaking countries to train their families for the last 300 years!

sourceMetadata.title: Have You Truly Come to Christ?
sourceMetadata.description: Pink examines 7 different stages of coming to Christ, shown in Scripture, asking the reader to examine himself to know where he stands with his Creator. Every soul at some point refuses to acknowledge his need of a Savior, yet Christ extends a gracious invitation. “Coming to Christ” is not the easy matter that so many imagine it to be, or the simple thing some preachers represent it as; it must begin with the drawing of God. This requires a humbling of the proud, depraved nature of man because he cannot begin the work. He must be willing to completely renounce all that stands in competition of Christ being crowned Lord of all his life for He will allow no rival of our affection. Having once been shown our need, we see the necessity of continually coming to Him daily for strength and cleansing. We are assured of the security we have in Christ, being “saved to the uttermost.”

sourceMetadata.title: Hearing the Rod
sourceMetadata.description: “Man is born unto trouble as the sparks fly upward.” With this quote from Job 5:7, A. W. Pink considers that there are two lines of truth concerning trouble and suffering in a Christian’s life. First, there are times when God chastens His children because of their sin. Second, trouble can be sent by God for benefits besides reproof of sin—for example, His purpose can be to make His people more like Christ, or fit them for greater usefulness in Christian service. The suffering believer should seek Divine consolation in the midst of all his trouble, confessing and forsaking every known sin. Whatever God does, it is for His glory and His people’s good.

sourceMetadata.title: Heart of the Saint, The
sourceMetadata.description: The outward, upright, moral lives of professing Christians may be a cover for a heart “overcharged with surfeiting, drunkenness and cares of this life”. Saints are commanded to guard their hearts, to live to the glory of God in every respect. The supreme desire of a believer is to know, love, and serve God. This requires that we “cleanse first that which is within.” Satan wants to persuade people that they are not responsible for the state of their hearts and it is impossible to change them. Pink examines what it means to “keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.”

sourceMetadata.title: Heavenly Birth and Its Earthly Counterfeits
sourceMetadata.description: In this 1843 sermon based on John 1:11-13, J. C. Philpot examines why some reject Christ and others receive Him. He further describes those who become sons of God and those who only profess to be sons of God. Explaining that the primary cause underlying all of this is found in the sovereign will of God, Philpot points out that there are also a number of secondary causes. For example, those who reject Christ do so because of blindness of heart, self-righteousness, worldliness of mind, or unbelief. In addition, he explores the motives of those who falsely profess a heavenly birth under three headings taken from John 1:13—born of blood, born of the will of the flesh, and born of the will of man. Philpot concludes with a description of those who are truly born of God.

files.author: John Bunyan
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Heavenly Footman, The
sourceMetadata.description: The Heavenly Footman is a fast-paced and direct challenge to every Christian to “run the race to win”! Footman is no reference to an infantryman or an aristocrat’s servant, but refers to those who are travelling on foot to a distant country, engaged in a pilgrimage from earth to heaven.  John Bunyan uses the allegory of the runner to picture the Christian’s race through this world to win the heavenly prize. Indeed, they that will have heaven must run for it. “They which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize…so run, that ye may obtain” (1Co 9:24). He understands that most are too casual in their approach to the Christian life. Their vigilance looks more like sloth too much of the time! Instead, Bunyan encourages us to “press toward the mark,” to “continue in the faith” in spite of all adversity, to remove hindrances, to beware of by-paths, to know the cross and mortification, to deny self, and to persevere. While this race is mentioned in most works on holiness, Bunyan’s focus is on the personal vigilance needed to complete the race, starting now, starting today.

sourceMetadata.title: True Christian's Love to the Unseen Christ, The
sourceMetadata.description: The True Christian’s Love to the Unseen Christ is a stirring exhortation to live a life of fervent love for our Savior fueled by the wonder of His love for us. An early edition states about this book, “It everywhere breathes the very spirit of the gospel and, while it unfolds the nature of sincere love to the Lord Jesus, it points the believer to those heavens where sits that Savior, ‘Whom, having not seen, ye love; in whom, though now ye see him not, yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory’ (1Pe 1:8).” The author exalts the beauties of Christ and expounds the believer’s duty and privilege to love such a Savior. It will both support the seeker in coming to Christ and renew the Christian’s genuine love for Christ.

children.title: Amor del verdadero cristiano al Cristo invisible, El
children.description: El amor del verdadero cristiano al Cristo invisible es una exhortación conmovedora a vivir una vida de amor ferviente por nuestro Salvador, impulsada por la maravilla de su amor por nosotros. Una de las primeras ediciones dice acerca de este libro: “En todas partes se respira el espíritu mismo del evangelio y, mientras revela la naturaleza del amor sincero al Señor Jesús, señala al creyente hacia esos cielos donde se sienta el Salvador, ‘a quien amáis sin haberle visto, en quien creyendo, aunque ahora no lo veáis, os alegráis con gozo inefable y glorioso’ (1 Pedro 1:8)”. El autor exalta las bellezas de Cristo y expone el deber y el privilegio del creyente de amar a tal Salvador. Apoyará al buscador a venir a Cristo y renovará el amor genuino del cristiano por Cristo.

sourceMetadata.title: Heir of Heaven - Heir of Hell
sourceMetadata.description: J. C. Philpot comparese grievous, yet forgiven, sins in the Christian, to the religious works of the unbeliever, which are but defiling hypocrisies. God sees the true state of the soul. Though the regenerate soul may falter into sin, by faith he is destined to eternal salvation. Though the unconverted may continually strive after the duties of religion, because of his unbelief he is headed for condemnation. Philpot closes with this admonition: "I have drawn two opposite characters—their beginning, progress and end. Which are you? If an empty professor, unless grace prevent, your sentence is recorded, that you shall lie down in sorrow. If a living soul, though now you are walking in darkness, and have no light, you shall one day behold the face of God with joy."

sourceMetadata.title: Repentez-vous ou périssez
sourceMetadata.description: « Si vous ne vous repentez, vous périrez tous de même » (Luc 13.3). Malheureusement, cette vérité biblique est rarement entendue dans nos églises modernes. Mais, comme A.W. Pink le fait remarquer, « la repentance est absolument nécessaire si le pécheur veut être réconcilié avec Dieu. » Il continue en décrivant la repentance comme : « une sainte haine et une sainte horreur du péché, une profonde douleur de l'avoir commis ; elle consiste à reconnaître notre péché devant Dieu et à y renoncer totalement du fond du cœur ». Pink conclut ce court traité par une déclaration effrayante et une question : « Détournez-vous de votre voie de volonté personnelle et d'égocentrisme ; tournez-vous vers Dieu avec un cœur brisé, cherchant sa miséricorde en Christ ; tournez-vous avec un cœur pleinement décidé à LUI plaire et à LE servir ; ou bien vous serez tourmenté jour et nuit, aux siècles des siècles, dans l'étang de feu ». Qu'en sera-t-il pour vous ?

parent.title: Repent or Perish
parent.description: “Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish” (Luke 13:3). Sadly, this Biblical truth is seldom heard in our modern churches. But as A. W. Pink points out, “Repentance is absolutely necessary if the sinner is to make peace with God.” He goes on to describe repentance as, “A holy hatred and horror of sin, a deep sorrow for it, and acknowledgement of it before God, and a complete heart forsaking of it.” Pink ends this short tract with a chilling statement and a question, “Turn from your course of self-will; turn with full purpose of heart to please and serve HIM: or be tormented day and night, forever and ever, in the Lake of Fire. Which shall it be?”

sourceMetadata.title: His Own Special People
sourceMetadata.description: In this exposition of 1 Peter 2:9, Philpot makes it clear that the saved and regenerate people of God are distinctly different from the people of this world. Philpot first addresses the spiritual exercises distinct to the people of God, followed by the special deliverances of God to His people. He then remarks on the special external marks of believers, in which, "They will be separate from the world." In his closing words, he observes "the marks visible to the Church of God", the marks of true and saving salvation in Christ by which these souls are found to be "His Own Special People."

parent.title: London Baptist Confession of Faith - 1689
parent.description:
The London Baptist Confession of 1677/89 played an important role in Baptist history. The Act of Uniformity of 1662 made the new Anglican Prayer Book mandatory for use in all Anglican, Presbyterian, Congregationalist, and Baptist churches in England. Moreover, the Anglican church abandoned the Westminster Confession and returned to the Thirty-Nine Articles as its official confession of faith. Consequently, with the restoration of the Monarchy, the English Baptists suffered persecution for their faith. In 1677, a group of Particular Baptists met for the purpose of producing a more expansive confession than the previous Baptist confession of 1644. They modeled the Second London Confession on the Westminster Confession, but with significant theological differences regarding church government and baptism. Persecution kept the 1677 document from being officially endorsed by Particular Baptists until 1689, when the Toleration Act was passed. This act enabled religious freedom to co-exist alongside the established churches in England and Scotland. As a result, representatives from over 100 Particular Baptist churches met in London from July 3-11 to discuss and endorse the 1677 document. Though the confession was published in 1677, the General Assembly of Particular Baptist Churches adopted it in 1689; hence it is commonly known as “the 1689.” The Westminster Confession, the Savoy Declaration, and the London Baptist Confession of 1677/89 are considered the most important Reformed confessions arising from the English-speaking world.

"This little volume is not issued as an authoritative rule, or code of faith, whereby you are to be fettered, but as an assistance to you in controversy, a confirmation in faith, and a means of edification in righteousness. Here the younger members of our church will have a body of divinity in small compass, and by means of the Scriptural proofs, will be ready to give a reason for the hope that is in them. Be not ashamed of your faith; remember it is the ancient gospel of martyrs, confessors, reformers, and saints. Above all, it is the truth of God, against which the gates of Hell cannot prevail. Let your lives adorn your faith; let your example adorn your creed. Above all live in Christ Jesus, and walk in Him, giving credence to no teaching but that which is manifestly approved of Him and owned by the Holy Spirit. Cleave fast to the Word of God which is here mapped out for you.” —Charles Haddon Spurgeon to his own congregation in 1865

sourceMetadata.title: Holiness
sourceMetadata.description: Holiness – from the Introduction: “There is a simple yet profound word which occurs nine hundred times in the Bible. You see it first in Genesis, as we are informed how God created heaven and earth. You see it last in the Bible's final chapter, where we are told about God's creation of a new heaven and a new earth. One entire book, Leviticus, is devoted to the subject of this word. Yet this word is strangely overlooked today. Though it describes the uniqueness of God and the calling of all His children, it is largely ignored. This short yet awesome word is holy. Among other words, saint, sanctify, and sanctification are obtained from its root. What does holy, holiness mean? What is the scriptural call to holiness? How must holiness be practiced? Why does the church so desperately need holiness in our day?” Joel Beeke effectively answers these questions, using the Scriptures as authority and guide.

sourceMetadata.title: Un mot aux parents

parent.title: Word to Parents, A
parent.description: A most tragic feature of our modern civilization is the prevalence of disobedience of children to their parents in childhood, and their lack of respect for them when they grow up. Spoiled, self-willed children bring themselves into sorrow, and inflict great unhappiness on all around them. Quite often, parents are more to blame for this than children. When parents depart from the scriptural pattern, this is the result. Pink shows at least part of the problem: parents have not learned to govern themselves so cannot hope to govern their children well. Pink lays out the four principal duties of parents: instruction, leading by example, discipline, and prayer. By heeding this advice, parents may hope to raise obedient, helpful, respectful children.

files.author: Andrew Murray
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Holiness and Humility
sourceMetadata.description: In this tract, Andrew Murray explains how we can determine if the holiness we profess or seek is genuine. He gives his conclusion in the first paragraph. “The one infallible test of our holiness will be the humility before God and men that marks us. Humility is the bloom and the beauty of holiness.” On the other hand, “The chief mark of counterfeit holiness is its lack of humility.” Murray goes on to illustrate the point using the parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector. Finally, he warns all who seek or teach holiness that “There is no pride so dangerous, because none is so subtle or insidious, as the pride of holiness.” He ends with this plea, “Come let us flee to Jesus, and hide ourselves in Him until we be clothed upon with His humility. That alone is our holiness.”

sourceMetadata.title: Honey Out of the Rock
sourceMetadata.description: Honey Out of the Rock is mentioned in 1740 by Thomas Crosby in his History of the English Baptists, where he wrote of Willcox: “He writ a small piece, which was printed before the Fire of London, entitled: A Drop of Honey from the Rock Christ, a piece that was very well esteemed, and has done much good and been oft reprinted.” It was also translated into numerous languages. Now entitled Honey Out of the Rock, it continues to encourage God’s people wherever Christ is served.

files.author: Chapel Library contributors
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Chibvomerezo cha London Baptist cha 1689

parent.title: London Baptist Confession of Faith - 1689
parent.description:
The London Baptist Confession of 1677/89 played an important role in Baptist history. The Act of Uniformity of 1662 made the new Anglican Prayer Book mandatory for use in all Anglican, Presbyterian, Congregationalist, and Baptist churches in England. Moreover, the Anglican church abandoned the Westminster Confession and returned to the Thirty-Nine Articles as its official confession of faith. Consequently, with the restoration of the Monarchy, the English Baptists suffered persecution for their faith. In 1677, a group of Particular Baptists met for the purpose of producing a more expansive confession than the previous Baptist confession of 1644. They modeled the Second London Confession on the Westminster Confession, but with significant theological differences regarding church government and baptism. Persecution kept the 1677 document from being officially endorsed by Particular Baptists until 1689, when the Toleration Act was passed. This act enabled religious freedom to co-exist alongside the established churches in England and Scotland. As a result, representatives from over 100 Particular Baptist churches met in London from July 3-11 to discuss and endorse the 1677 document. Though the confession was published in 1677, the General Assembly of Particular Baptist Churches adopted it in 1689; hence it is commonly known as “the 1689.” The Westminster Confession, the Savoy Declaration, and the London Baptist Confession of 1677/89 are considered the most important Reformed confessions arising from the English-speaking world.

"This little volume is not issued as an authoritative rule, or code of faith, whereby you are to be fettered, but as an assistance to you in controversy, a confirmation in faith, and a means of edification in righteousness. Here the younger members of our church will have a body of divinity in small compass, and by means of the Scriptural proofs, will be ready to give a reason for the hope that is in them. Be not ashamed of your faith; remember it is the ancient gospel of martyrs, confessors, reformers, and saints. Above all, it is the truth of God, against which the gates of Hell cannot prevail. Let your lives adorn your faith; let your example adorn your creed. Above all live in Christ Jesus, and walk in Him, giving credence to no teaching but that which is manifestly approved of Him and owned by the Holy Spirit. Cleave fast to the Word of God which is here mapped out for you.” —Charles Haddon Spurgeon to his own congregation in 1865

sourceMetadata.title: Hour with George Mueller, An
sourceMetadata.description:
An interview with George Mueller of Bristol.

“He received me with a cordial handshake and bade me welcome. It is something merely to see a man by whom God has accomplished a mighty work: it is more to hear the tones of his voice; far greater than either is the privilege of being brought into immediate contact with his spirit and of feeling the warm breath of his soul breathed into one’s own. The communion of that hour will be graven on my memory while life shall last. This servant of the Most High opened his heart to me, counseled me, prayed with me, and gave me his blessing. In that hour the source of George Mueller’s great spiritual strength was clearly made manifest. The aged saint with all his faculties unimpaired, was eloquent the whole time on one theme, the praise of Jehovah, the great Hearer and Answerer of His people’s prayers. My own words were few.

“You have always found the Lord faithful to His promise, Mr. Mueller?

“Always! He has never failed me!...”

La comunión de esa hora quedará grabada en mi memoria mientras la vida durará. Este siervo del Altísimo me abrió su corazón, me aconsejó, oró conmigo y me dio su bendición. En esa hora, la fuente de la gran fuerza espiritual de George Mueller se manifestó claramente. El anciano santo con todas sus facultades intactas, fue elocuente todo el tiempo sobre un tema, la alabanza de Jehová, el gran oyente y el que responde a las oraciones de su pueblo. Mis propias palabras fueron pocas. "¿Siempre ha encontrado al Señor fiel a Su promesa, Sr. Mueller? "¡Siempre! ¡Nunca me ha fallado! ...

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained

sourceMetadata.title: Gospel in a Single Verse, The
sourceMetadata.description: The Gospel in a Single Verse considers each part of 1 Timothy 1:15 to bring the gospel to today’s reader in Spurgeon’s straightforward style. As “sinners” we need to be “saved,” “Christ Jesus” came as Savior, and He willingly came “into the world” in order to save His people from their sins. Lastly, realizing that Paul considered himself as “chief” of all sinners brings us to deal realistically with our own sin. Spurgeon exhorts us to take this “gospel-in-a-verse” to heart, and to live our lives for this wonderful Lord!

files.title: How Men Come to Christ
files.author: Charles H. Spurgeon
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: How Men Come to Christ
sourceMetadata.description: In this tract Charles Spurgeon explains the truth Christ declares in John 6:44: no man can come to Christ unless the Father draw him. First, he refutes a common Arminian view that suggests God uses preaching alone to draw men to Christ, leaving the rest up to man. He also repudiates the assertion that Spurgeon, and those like him, teach that God drags men to Christ against their will. But since all men are naturally resistant, how does the Father draw them? According to Spurgeon, He sends the Holy Spirit to change men’s hearts so that they come willingly to the Savior without any compulsion whatever. How is this accomplished? Only God knows, but if the Holy Spirit’s influence is not brought to bear, “there never has been and there never will be any man who either can or will come to the Lord Jesus Christ.”

children.title: Como vienen los hombres a Cristo
children.description: En este tratado, Charles Spurgeon explica la verdad que Cristo declara en Juan 6:44: ningún hombre puede venir a Cristo a menos que el Padre lo atraiga. Primero, refuta un punto de vista arminiano común que sugiere que Dios usa la predicación solo para atraer a los hombres a Cristo, dejando el resto a los hombres. También repudia la afirmación de que Spurgeon, y aquellos como él, enseñan que Dios arrastra a los hombres a Cristo en contra de su voluntad. Pero como todos los hombres son naturalmente resistentes, ¿cómo los atrae el Padre? Según Spurgeon, Él envía al Espíritu Santo para cambiar los corazones de los hombres para que vengan voluntariamente al Salvador sin ninguna obligación. ¿Cómo se logra esto? Solo Dios sabe, pero si la influencia del Espíritu Santo no se ejerce, "nunca ha habido y nunca habrá un hombre que pueda venir o que vendrá al Señor Jesucristo".

sourceMetadata.title: TELUGU Edition: London Baptist Confession of 1689

parent.title: London Baptist Confession of Faith - 1689
parent.description:
The London Baptist Confession of 1677/89 played an important role in Baptist history. The Act of Uniformity of 1662 made the new Anglican Prayer Book mandatory for use in all Anglican, Presbyterian, Congregationalist, and Baptist churches in England. Moreover, the Anglican church abandoned the Westminster Confession and returned to the Thirty-Nine Articles as its official confession of faith. Consequently, with the restoration of the Monarchy, the English Baptists suffered persecution for their faith. In 1677, a group of Particular Baptists met for the purpose of producing a more expansive confession than the previous Baptist confession of 1644. They modeled the Second London Confession on the Westminster Confession, but with significant theological differences regarding church government and baptism. Persecution kept the 1677 document from being officially endorsed by Particular Baptists until 1689, when the Toleration Act was passed. This act enabled religious freedom to co-exist alongside the established churches in England and Scotland. As a result, representatives from over 100 Particular Baptist churches met in London from July 3-11 to discuss and endorse the 1677 document. Though the confession was published in 1677, the General Assembly of Particular Baptist Churches adopted it in 1689; hence it is commonly known as “the 1689.” The Westminster Confession, the Savoy Declaration, and the London Baptist Confession of 1677/89 are considered the most important Reformed confessions arising from the English-speaking world.

"This little volume is not issued as an authoritative rule, or code of faith, whereby you are to be fettered, but as an assistance to you in controversy, a confirmation in faith, and a means of edification in righteousness. Here the younger members of our church will have a body of divinity in small compass, and by means of the Scriptural proofs, will be ready to give a reason for the hope that is in them. Be not ashamed of your faith; remember it is the ancient gospel of martyrs, confessors, reformers, and saints. Above all, it is the truth of God, against which the gates of Hell cannot prevail. Let your lives adorn your faith; let your example adorn your creed. Above all live in Christ Jesus, and walk in Him, giving credence to no teaching but that which is manifestly approved of Him and owned by the Holy Spirit. Cleave fast to the Word of God which is here mapped out for you.” —Charles Haddon Spurgeon to his own congregation in 1865

sourceMetadata.title: How Shall I Approach God?
sourceMetadata.description: How Shall I Approach God? brings the good news of the Gospel of Jesus Christ in nine short messages, each from a different perspective, inviting those in this world to carefully consider the claims of God upon their lives. These were not originally spoken sermons, as is much of the current literature from prior centuries; rather, each short message was written specifically as a tract to command the attention of readers across time and cultures.

children.title: ¿Cómo ir a Dios?
children.description: ¿Cómo ir a Dios? trae las buenas nuevas del Evangelio de Jesucristo en nueve mensajes cortos, cada uno desde una perspectiva diferente, invitando a los que están en este mundo a considerar cuidadosamente las afirmaciones de Dios sobre sus vidas. Estos no fueron sermones originalmente hablados, como lo es gran parte de la literatura actual de siglos anteriores; más bien, cada mensaje corto fue escrito específicamente como un tramo para captar la atención de los lectores a través del tiempo y las culturas.

files.author: Horatius Bonar
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: How Shall I Go to God?
sourceMetadata.description: We have nothing we can claim as our own, but our sins. This difficult, humbling lesson is the first right step in pursuing a religious life. The only place of true happiness is to rest secure in the favor of God. Our first step in going to God must be to humbly admit our great need of a Savior. Bonar shows that all else we need is found in God. Using the example of the great Reformer Martin Luther, even the gift of repentance is wrought by the goodness of God. At the cross, we meet God in peace and receive His favor. All we must do is ask! “If thou knewest the gift of God…thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.” In this message, Bonar shows the simplicity of the gospel.

children.title: ¿Cómo iré a Dios?
children.description: No tenemos nada que podamos reclamar como propio, salvo nuestros pecados. Esta lección, difícil y que nos humilla, es el primer paso correcto para emprender una vida religiosa. El único lugar de verdadera felicidad es descansar seguros en el favor de Dios. Nuestro primer paso al acercarnos a Dios debe ser admitir humildemente nuestra gran necesidad de un Salvador. Bonar demuestra que todo lo demás que necesitamos se encuentra en Dios. Tomando como ejemplo al gran reformador Martín Lutero, vemos que incluso el don del arrepentimiento es obra de la bondad de Dios. En la cruz, nos encontramos con Dios en paz y recibimos su favor. ¡Lo único que debemos hacer es pedir! «Si conocieras el don de Dios... le habrías pedido, y él te habría dado agua viva». En este mensaje, Bonar muestra la sencillez del evangelio.

sourceMetadata.title: The Ordinance of Baptism
sourceMetadata.description: The Ordinance of Baptism is a concise yet thorough biblical examination of Christian baptism: how it was ordained by God, its Old Testament precedents, and most importantly, who are to be its subjects. Gill carefully examines the New Testament incidents of baptism to determine if the subjects are repentant believers in the atoning sacrifice of Christ, or infant covenant children of believers. This thread continues through the remainder of the treatise as Gill considers baptism’s manner of administration (immersion or sprinkling), form (in the names of the Trinity), and purposes and uses. The latter brings encouragement to every believer as we anticipate obedient fellowship with our Lord among His people.

sourceMetadata.title: How to Be Free from Bitterness
sourceMetadata.description: How to Be Free From Bitterness helps the reader break the chains of one of the most terrible masters—the sin of bitterness. Through this booklet explore what bitterness is, its cause, and how to solve it. The root of bitterness in a person’s life can only be extracted by the power of God’s grace in the gospel, honestly facing their sin, and coming to God to fill their heart with the sweet water of His love.

children.title: Como estar libre de la amargura
children.description: Cómo Estar Libre de la Amargura ayuda al lector a romper las cadenas de uno de los señores más terribles: el pecado de la amargura. A través de este folleto, se expone qué es la amargura, su causa y cómo resolverla. La raíz de la amargura en la vida de una persona solo puede ser extraída por el poder de la gracia de Dios en el evangelio, enfrentando honestamente su pecado y acercándose a Dios para llenar su corazón con el agua dulce de su amor.

sourceMetadata.title: Ten Commandments and the Christian, The
sourceMetadata.description: The Ten Commandments and the Christian is an important and very relevant topic. Is the believer in Christ to obey laws revealed in the Bible prior to the giving of the New Testament? Specifically, is he to obey the Ten Commandments? If so, on what basis? The lawless condition of both the professing church of Christ and the world that surrounds it demands that we find biblical answers to these questions. This booklet explores the significance of the Ten Commandments through their place in the Old Covenant and New Covenant,  through their function as reflecting the moral law, and through their treatment in the London Baptist Confession of Faith of 1689.

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Hypocrisy
sourceMetadata.description: In this issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster, we learn of the great sin of hypocrisy. Andrew Bromhall shows us the danger of this sin. The hypocrite's two-faced character is declared by Charles H. Spurgeon. Thomas Brooks reminds us that no hypocrite makes God or Christ his ultimate reason for existence. Jonathan Edwards describes a hypocrite as a prayerless man. How far may hypocrites go? This compelling question is answered by David Clarkson, who shows that some can seem to be so close, yet be so very far away from heaven. Jonathan Edwards brings a stirring reminder that fear will overtake the hypocrite at the last Day. As Thomas Boston shows, a true Christian can be discerned by his heart religion. Lastly, Charles Spurgeon applies these truths, as he considers, "What if I find hypocrisy in me?"

sourceMetadata.title: I Can't Let Go
sourceMetadata.description: A young lad dangled by a rope from a sinking ship over a lifeboat full of strong men ready to catch him. Yet he trusted more to his own strength and to the rope than to the boat below full of those ready and waiting to rescue him. Bonar uses this example to admonish those who complain, “I can’t believe in Christ.” This is a rejection of His finished work. Self-righteousness and depravity make man unwilling to give up self. He blames his unbelief on God. Bonar shows that God’s plan of redemption has been finished; all that remains for man is to let go of himself, and fully trust in Christ as Savior.

children.title: No puedo soltarme
children.description: Un joven colgaba de una cuerda desde un barco que se hundía, justo encima de un bote salvavidas lleno de hombres robustos listos para recibirlo. Sin embargo, confiaba más en su propia fuerza y ​​en la cuerda que en el bote que estaba abajo, lleno de personas dispuestas y a la espera de rescatarlo. Bonar utiliza este ejemplo para exhortar a quienes se quejan diciendo: «No puedo creer en Cristo». Tal actitud constituye un rechazo a la obra consumada de Él. La justicia propia y la depravación hacen que el hombre se resista a renunciar a sí mismo; así, atribuye a Dios la culpa de su incredulidad. Bonar demuestra que el plan de redención de Dios ya se ha consumado; lo único que le queda al hombre por hacer es soltarse de sí mismo y confiar plenamente en Cristo como Salvador.

sourceMetadata.title: Un catecismo para niños y niñas
sourceMetadata.description: A lo largo de los siglos, la iglesia cristiana ha valorado el catecismo como una herramienta importante para la formación en la doctrina básica. Esta variación del catecismo bautista ha sido cuidadosamente actualizada para los niños de hoy.

parent.title: Catechism for Boys and Girls, A
parent.description:
This simple catechism is very helpful for teaching young children to understand and remember the basic truths of the Christian faith.

The Westminster Assembly produced not only its well-known Confession of Faith, but also the Longer Catechism (for pastors’ use in teaching their congregations) and Shorter Catechism (for parents’ use in teaching their children). Soon thereafter, Benjamin Keach (1640-1704) tailored the Westminster Shorter Catechism to the London Baptist Confession of 1677/89 (which is based on the Westminster except in its chapters on church government, the covenants, and baptism). Later, Charles Spurgeon (1834-1892) updated Keach’s catechism for his own congregation.

More recently, Erroll Hulse knew that a more simplified Baptist catechism was needed so that parents could train their young children at home. The 134 short questions and answers encompass all the key doctrines of the faith, including sections on God-Man-Sin, Salvation, The Ten Commandments, Prayer, The Word, The Church and Ordinances, and Last Things.

sourceMetadata.title: Imminent Danger and Only Sure Resource of Our Nation, The
sourceMetadata.description: In this sermon from February 1794, John Newton lays out the plight of his beloved England in the late 18th century. Describing the danger as imminent and the impending judgment as deserved, his comments could just as easily apply to 21st century America. He goes on to point squarely to the only real solution—humbling ourselves before God, our true and only means of deliverance. Newton ends with a heartfelt prayer for his nation. As Christians in America, we would do well to imitate his example as we find it in this sermon.

sourceMetadata.title: Christian Unity
sourceMetadata.description: In this issue of the FGB on Christian Unity, Arthur W. Pink introduces Christian unity as the fruit of regeneration. Matthew Henry then explains from Scripture that this unity has its origin in the oneness of the members of the Godhead. Charles Spurgeon describes the unity that Christ prayed for, contrasting it with man-made movements and denominations. David Martyn Lloyd-Jones then beautifully describes the spiritual nature of unity in Christ’s body. Following that, Anthony Burgess discusses the difference between visible and invisible unity. A second article by Lloyd-Jones lists helpful steps for guarding the Spirit’s unity among Christ’s people. Thomas Smyth offers us twelve rules for promoting harmony among church members, and another article by Anthony Burgess exhorts ministers to seek unity among themselves. The unity of pastors and members of Christ’s churches is important; Andrew Fuller guides in securing it. In his third article, Burgess expounds the excellence of unity and how it brings the world to believe the truth of Christ’s saving mercies. Spurgeon’s second article calls us to the crucial work needed in accomplishing Christian unity. We conclude with Jeremiah Burroughs explaining the excellence and beauty of peace, love, and harmony among the blood-bought people of God. May the Lord help us to see and pursue it.

articles.title: Even as We Are One
articles.description: The Christian unity that Jesus prayed for flows from the unity of the Godhead.

articles.title: Guarding the Spirit’s Unity
articles.description: a helpful guide for God’s people in guarding the gift of the Holy Spirit’s unity.

articles.description: useful steps for promoting and preserving unity among the members of Christ’s congregations.

articles.title: The Unity of Ministers
articles.description: explains the vital role and benefits that unity among ministers of the gospel plays in the church’s life.

articles.title: The Unity of Pastors & Members
articles.description: a two-part exhortation explaining how pastors and members may preserve peace in a church.

articles.title: That the World May Believe
articles.description: Christian unity testifies that Jesus Christ came into the world to save sinners.

articles.title: The Work to Be Done
articles.description: Preaching Christ to the world and loving one another with a pure heart is the work that brings peace.

articles.title: The Excellence of Unity
articles.description: God loves brotherly love, and He blesses it for the good of His people and for His eternal glory.

sourceMetadata.title: Inspired Logic
sourceMetadata.description: Horatius Bonar elaborates on the inescapable logic of Romans 8:32—“He that spared not His own Son, but delivered Him up for us all, how shall He not with Him also freely give us all things?” He breaks it down into two parts: the one gift and the many gifts. The one gift is “the unspeakable gift” where God spared not his Son so he could spare us. While the gift is one, it is infinite, the gift of all gifts. Furthermore, this one gift was given not for righteous men, but for sinners whose portion was condemnation. So the question comes—if God Is willing to give the ultimate gift to such as us, will He deny us any other needful thing? Clearly, the answer is no. He will “freely give us all things,”—that is, the many gifts.

sourceMetadata.title: The Christian's Love for Christ
sourceMetadata.description: In this issue of the FGB, The Christian’s Love for Christ, J. C. Ryle introduces this crucial subject with Christ’s question to Peter: “Lovest Thou Me?” Thomas Vincent explains why true Christians love the unseen Christ. Following that, Jonathan Edwards lists biblical motives to love Christ. Charles Spurgeon declares that love for Christ is the great test for confirming that we are children of God. Ryle, in his second article, identifies the marks of love for our precious Savior. In Spurgeon’s second article, he asserts reasons to love Christ and the consequences of being without love for Him. Edwards follows with a second article that describes God’s dreadful curse on those who do not love Christ. Vincent then helpfully gives an overview of how to examine and prove our love for Jesus. In his third and final article, Ryle asks a heartfelt, probing, and personal question that we must all answer: Do you love Jesus Christ?

articles.title: Lovest Thou Me?
articles.description: After Peter had denied Jesus three times, the resurrected Lord asked him this question. How do you answer that simple but profound question?

articles.title: Why True Christians Love the Unseen Christ
articles.description: True Christians love Christ because of the need they have of Him, because of His loveliness, and because He loves them.

articles.title: Motives to Love Christ
articles.description: What motivates true believers to love Christ? His loveliness, the excellent effects of His love, the pleasantness of living life in His love, and the pleasantness of His love over any other.

articles.title: The Great Test of Sonship
articles.description: Loving Jesus Christ is the great test of the true believer’s sonship.

articles.title: Marks of Love to Christ
articles.description: What marks of love to Christ can true believers identify in their lives? This survey offers  biblical and common-sense marks for the consideration of Christ’s blood-bought people.

articles.title: Without Love to Christ
articles.description: The absence of love to Christ is the loss of one of the greatest spiritual pleasures in human experience.

articles.title: Cursed for Not Loving Christ
articles.description: The absence of love to Christ is a great crime against God, which brings His eternal curse.

articles.title: The Trial of Our Love
articles.description: How do we know if we are true Christians? The questions in this article will help us measure our true spiritual condition.

articles.title: Do You Love Jesus Christ?
articles.description: This is the question that all human beings must answer: eternity in heaven or hell awaits our answer.

files.title: Instead of Me
files.author: Horatius Bonar
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Instead of Me
sourceMetadata.description: In the guise of two personal encounters, Horatius Bonar gives an easy-to-understand explanation of the atonement. In these conversations we learn that atonement for sins is not based on anything we do, it is only because of Christ’s sacrifice on the cross. Jesus pays the debt and God forgives the sins of those who believe. In a simple description of this astonishing exchange, Bonar brings it down to a personal level when he declares the good news that God is willing to put Christ in my place—that is, Christ “instead of me.” There is no better news than this.

children.title: En mi lugar
children.description: Bajo la apariencia de dos encuentros personales, Horatius Bonar da una explicación fácil de entender de la expiación. En estas conversaciones aprendemos que la expiación por los pecados no se basa en nada en lo que hacemos, es solo por el sacrificio de Cristo en la cruz. Jesús paga la deuda y Dios perdona los pecados de los que creen. En una descripción simple de este intercambio sorprendente, Bonar lo lleva a un nivel personal cuando declara la buena noticia de que Dios está dispuesto a poner a Cristo en mi lugar —es decir, Cristo "en lugar de mí". No hay mejores noticias que esta.

sourceMetadata.title: Is Abortion Really So Bad?
sourceMetadata.description: Over 53 million unborn children have been killed in legal abortions committed in the United States and Canada. We certainly should have a strong ethical basis to legally sanction the ending of so many lives in our nations, plus over a million more each year. We therefore examine the arguments used by those who promote abortion to determine on how strong of a foundation this practice is based. Then we turn to a higher court of authority than human reasoning to set forth the truths of God’s Word that are involved in the issue of abortion.

children.title: ¿Es realmente tan malo el aborto?
children.description: Más de 53 millones de niños no nacidos han sido asesinados en abortos legales cometidos en los Estados Unidos y Canadá. Ciertamente, deberíamos tener una base ética sólida para sancionar legalmente el final de tantas vidas en nuestras naciones, más más de un millón cada año. Por lo tanto, examinamos los argumentos utilizados por aquellos que promueven el aborto para determinar en qué medida se basa esta práctica. Luego nos dirigimos a un tribunal de autoridad más alto que el razonamiento humano para exponer las verdades de la Palabra de Dios que están involucradas en el tema del aborto.

files.description: Over 53 million unborn children have been killed in legal abortions committed in the United States and Canada. We certainly should have a strong ethical basis to legally sanction the ending of so many lives in our nations, plus over a million more each year. We therefore examine the arguments used by those who promote abortion to determine on how strong of a foundation this practice is based. Then we turn to a higher court of authority than human reasoning to set forth the truths of God’s Word that are involved in the issue of abortion.

sourceMetadata.title: Depression and the Christian
sourceMetadata.description:
In this small but helpful tract on depression, Pink goes to the Psalms and looks at how David dealt with his own soul when struggling with inner and outer burdens and conflicts.

When it seems that God’s face frowns, most of us are apt to be depressed. While some temperaments seem to fluctuate as wildly as a barometer, even the most stable personalities are likely to be cast down in trying situations. Pink examines the question “Is it wrong to be cast down?” The answer depends on the cause, duration, and effects of the despondency. God does not require His children to live emotionless lives, unaffected by circumstances within or without us. Christians should be deeply concerned over their sins, and over souls hurtling headlong into hell. However, if the source of gloom is the crossing of the will or the foiling of cherished plans, this is shameful. Pink examines several passages from Psalms, noting the causes and cures of the psalmist’s despair. The creature may fail, but the Creator will not, if we wholly and truly trust Him. “Hope thou in God.”

children.title: El cristiano y la depresión
children.description: Cuando la providencia parece ser adversa, la mayoría de nosotros tendemos a desanimarnos. Es cierto que algunas personas tienen un temperamento más voluble que otras: sus emociones cambian con la misma frecuencia que el barómetro en un clima inestable; un día están en la cima de la montaña, y al siguiente, en el abismo de la desesperación. Sin embargo, incluso quienes son más estables y equilibrados pueden verse abatidos en el espíritu al enfrentar situaciones difíciles, cuando todo parece ir en contra de ellos.

sourceMetadata.title: Is Christ Your Lord?
sourceMetadata.description: The saving Christ of the Bible is not only the Savior of His people, but also their Lord! Is He your Lord? If He is not your Lord, then He is not your Savior as well.

children.title: ¿Es Cristo tu Señor?
children.description: Muchas personas esperan ser salvadas por Jesucristo, el único Salvador de los pecadores. Pero las Escrituras declaran que debemos creer en Jesucristo el Señor para ser salvos del pecado. Si Jesucristo no es tu Señor, no es tu Salvador. El arrepentimiento del pecado contra el Salvador debe acompañar la fe en el Salvador.

children.title: Христ Чиний Эзэн Мөн Үү?

children.title: SI KRISTO BA ANG IYONG PANGINOON?
children.description: Ang nagliligtas na Kristo ng Bibliya ay hindi lamang ang Tagapagligtas ng Kanyang mga tao, kundi pati na rin ang kanilang Panginoon! Siya ba ang iyong Panginoon? Kung hindi Siya ang iyong Panginoon, hindi rin Siya ang iyong Tagapagligtas.

sourceMetadata.title: Is It Settled?
sourceMetadata.description: Every soul is traveling to an eternal heaven or an endless hell. In the affairs of life, men like to have things settled, but, oddly enough, many continue on through life without having their eternal affairs settled. At peace in this condition, they are lulled to sleep by Satan only to be awakened by the judgment of the Almighty when there is no hope of mercy. This tract urges every soul to seek God while there is yet time to settle the question.

sourceMetadata.title: Church Membership: Why Bother?
sourceMetadata.description:
Church Membership, Why Bother? is a call to reject Christian individualism and to embrace biblical commitment to the local church. Decided members tell the world that church is not about their personal preferences and individual needs but about the honor of Christ and His kingdom. Membership enables full participation in the body life the New Testament prescribes for Christ's disciples. Church membership must be taken seriously.

This booklet is reproduced by permission from a chapter in The Church, Why Bother? by Jeff Johnson, © 2015 Free Grace Press, Greenbrier, AR, freegracepress.com. All rights reserved. Jeff Johnson has published a new edition of his book entitled The Church: Her Nature, Authority, Purpose, and Worship, available in print and digital formats from Free Grace Press, freegracepress.com.

children.title: La membresía de la iglesia: ¿por qué importa?
children.description: La membresía de la iglesia: ¿por qué importa? es un llamado a rechazar el individualismo cristiano y a abrazar el compromiso bíblico con la iglesia local. Los miembros comprometidos demuestran al mundo que la iglesia no se trata de preferencias personales ni necesidades individuales, sino de la honra de Cristo y su reino. La membresía permite la plena participación en la vida comunitaria que el Nuevo Testamento prescribe para los discípulos de Cristo. La membresía en la iglesia debe tomarse en serio.

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: It Is Finished
sourceMetadata.description: In this short tract, A. W. Pink points out a common problem that plagues the modern church. “Many seem to think that on the cross the Lord Jesus accomplished a work which rendered it unnecessary for the beneficiaries of it to live holy lives on earth.” When Christ cried out “It is finished,” He “had now performed all that was necessary for the Holy Spirit to come and work in the hearts of His people; convincing them of their rebellion, slaying their enmity against God, and producing in them a loving and obedient heart.” Pink ends with a stern warning to those who claim to be believers but live worldly lives—Christ’s finished work avails you nothing if your heart has never been broken by an agonizing realization of your sinfulness, if you still love the world, and if you have not been saved from the power of sin.

children.title: La oración familiar no debe ser descuidada
children.description: Nueva Inglaterra ha sido un lugar famoso por la religión en general, y por la adoración familiar en particular; pero últimamente, tanto su descuido, así como de otros deberes religiosos ha ido evidentemente en aumento entre nosotros. Esto ha causado mucha tristeza a las almas piadosas, sin embargo, no he oído que se haya publicado ningún discurso sobre este tema aquí durante muchos años. Recientemente, grandes números de personas han sido notablemente despertadas en algunas partes del país, quienes crecieron sin oración familiar, y aún están en duda sobre la autoridad bíblica para su práctica diaria. Por lo tanto, humildemente ofrezco al público las siguientes consideraciones, por consejo de amigos.—Isaac Backus, pastor de una iglesia en Middleborough, Massachusetts, 6 de febrero de 1766

sourceMetadata.description: John Ploughman’s Talk is a straight-forward, no frills, common sense approach to Christian wisdom and sanctification. It is a must-read for all young people and parents. Spurgeon adopts the figure of John Ploughman, a common laborer, to write his insights in the first person about patience, gossip, flattery, business relationships, carefulness and discernment, finances, hypocrisy, hard work, and much more. His humor and expression make the immense worth of this practical wisdom enjoyable and unforgettable.

sourceMetadata.title: Just God, A
sourceMetadata.description: In this tract, Charles Spurgeon uses his own life as an example in explaining the atonement of Christ. When under conviction of sin, Spurgeon long agonized over the question: “How God could be just and yet justify me who had been so guilty.” He explains in detail the answer he came to by faith; it is in essence: “He who is the Son of God became man and, in His own blessed Person, bore my sin in His own body on the tree.” He goes on to show what it is to trust Jesus for salvation and concludes with the comforting words,“If you will have the Lord Jesus, He has you already. If you believe on Him, I tell you, you cannot go to hell, for that were to (would) make the perfect sacrifice of Christ to none effect.”

children.title: Un Dios Justo
children.description: En este tratado, Charles Spurgeon usa su propia vida como ejemplo para explicar la expiación de Cristo. Cuando estaba convencido de pecado, Spurgeon agonizaba preguntandose: "Cómo Dios puede ser justo y, sin embargo, justificarme a mí mismo por haber sido tan culpable". Explica en detalle la respuesta que recibió por fe; en esencia: "El que es el Hijo de Dios se hizo hombre y, en su propia persona bendecida, llevó mi pecado en su propio cuerpo en el madero". Continúa mostrando lo que es confiar en Jesús para la salvación y concluye con las palabras de consuelo: “Si tienes al Señor Jesús, Él ya te tiene a ti. Si crees en Él, te digo que no puedes ir al infierno, porque eso haría el sacrificio perfecto de Cristo sin efecto.

files.description: In this tract, Charles Spurgeon uses his own life as an example in explaining the atonement of Christ. When under conviction of sin, Spurgeon long agonized over the question: “How God could be just and yet justify me who had been so guilty.” He explains in detail the answer he came to by faith; it is in essence: “He who is the Son of God became man and, in His own blessed Person, bore my sin in His own body on the tree.” He goes on to show what it is to trust Jesus for salvation and concludes with the comforting words,“If you will have the Lord Jesus, He has you already. If you believe on Him, I tell you, you cannot go to hell, for that were to (would) make the perfect sacrifice of Christ to none effect.”

sourceMetadata.title: Church Membership
sourceMetadata.description: Church Membership surveys the biblical principles behind this often misunderstood and unappreciated Christian duty. It argues that church membership is indeed “in the Bible.” While it might take different forms, church membership always involves a voluntary commitment for accountability, mutual care, and spiritual union or fellowship by the Spirit of God. But who should be considered for membership and how should the process be handled? Pastor Nichols applies the biblical data and his pastoral experience to provide answers to these practical questions as well. This booklet is taken from his four volume Lectures in Systematic Theology.

El pastor Nichols aplica los datos bíblicos y su experiencia pastoral para responder también a estas preguntas prácticas.

sourceMetadata.title: Last days of Edward Payson, The
sourceMetadata.description: For the last 20 years of his life, Edward Payson (1783-1827) was the much beloved pastor of Second Church in Portland, Maine. This collection of what he saw, thought, and felt during the last month of his life—as he experienced the most severe physical suffering—are those of a humble saint at the very gates of Heaven. In a letter to his sister he wrote, “The celestial city is full in my view. Its glories beam upon me, its breezes fan me, its odors are wafted to me, its sounds strike upon my ears, and its spirit is breathed into my heart. Nothing separates me from it but the river of death, which now appears but as an insignificant rill that may be crossed at a single step, whenever God shall give permission.” Always the pastor, Payson directed that at his funeral a label be attached to his breast on which was written, “Remember the words which I spake unto you while I was yet present with you.” And thus even though dead, he still spoke.

sourceMetadata.title: Law and the Saint, The
sourceMetadata.description: The Law and the Saint is a bold exposition of the key New Testament Scriptures which speak of God’s Law. Pink himself describes the scope and importance of this study. “We are assured that the present wide-spread contempt for human law is the inevitable outgrowth of disrespect for divine Law...Christian teachers have vied with each other in denouncing the Law as a ‘yoke of bondage,’ ‘a grievous burden,’ ‘a remorseless enemy’…They have denounced as ‘Legalists’ Christians of the past, who, like Paul, ‘served the Law.’ They have affirmed that grace rules the Law out of the Christian’s life as absolutely as it did out of his salvation…And because many of our Christian leaders have publicly repudiated divine Law, God has visited us with a wave of lawlessness in our churches, homes, and social life...But we have a hope that some who have been under the influence of…antinomianism will have sufficient spiritual discernment to recognize the truth when it is presented to their notice; and it is for them we now write.”

files.title: Letters of Samuel Rutherford
files.author: Samuel Rutherford
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Letters of Samuel Rutherford
sourceMetadata.description:
Like John Bunyan in the Bedford jail, Samuel Rutherford did his best work while suffering imprisonment for the Gospel. His opponents had meant to silence him, but instead they perpetuated his ministry through the centuries: it was out of this period that most of his famous Letters came. Addressed to high and low, they were so prized by the recipients that the first collection by Robert McWard appeared in 1664, just three years after Rutherford’s death. The successive editions contained more letters until they grew to the 365 in Andrew Bonar’s classic edition.

From this, “the most remarkable series of devotional letters that the literature of the Reformed churches can show,” the great leaders in the church as well as the humblest Christians have drawn strength. It is said of Robert Murray McCheyne that “the Letters of Samuel Rutherford were often in his hand.” Richard Baxter’s view was that, apart from the Bible, “such a book as Mr. Rutherford’s Letters the world never saw the like,” while to C.H. Spurgeon they were “the nearest think to inspiration which can be found in all the writings of mere men.” This abridged edition contains thirty of these letters.

“You have heard of my trouble, I suppose. It hath pleased our sweet Lord Jesus to let loose the malice of these interdicted lords in his house to deprive me of my ministry at Anwoth, and to confine me, eight score miles from thence, to Aberdeen; and also (which was not done to any before) to inhibit me to speak at all in Jesus’ name within this kingdom, under the pain of rebellion. The cause that ripened their hatred was my book, whereof they accused me on those three days I appeared before them. But let our crowned King in Zion reign! By his grace the loss is theirs, the advantage is Christ’s and truth’s.”—Samuel Rutherford in a letter to Robert Cunningham, 1636.

sourceMetadata.title: Little Foxes
sourceMetadata.description:
According to the author of this tract, “the children of God generally do not fall into great and well-known sins,” but there are sins that they commit often which are “like little foxes which spoil the vine (of our lives)—and we become fruitless.” He lists eight of them; two are below.

  1. Not praying for others. While we often pray for ourselves, our family, and our church, we neglect to pray for the Lord’s servants, missionaries, and all who are in authority.
  2. Respect of persons or pleasing man rather than God. This sin is all too common in the churches today and takes many forms—for example, catering to the rich and educated members rather than the poor and uneducated.

The author ends by urging us to “kill these little foxes that you may not be fruitless.”

files.title: Little Sins
files.author: Charles H. Spurgeon
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Little Sins
sourceMetadata.description: In this provocative sermon, Spurgeon reminds us that the best of men have always been afraid of little sins. Little things lead to greater things, and this is true about sin as well. Little sins can multiply fast. A little sin involves a great principle. We must beware of the little foxes which spoil the vines of our hearts.

children.title: Pequeños pecados
children.description: El gran Padre de Mentira tiene multitudes de estratagemas por medio de las cuales busca arruinar las almas de los hombres. Él usa pesos falsos y balanzas falsas para engañarlos. A veces usa tiempos falsos, declarando en una hora que es demasiado pronto para buscar al Señor, y en otra que ahora es demasiado tarde. Y usa cantidades falsas, porque declarará que los grandes pecados son muy pequeños, y en cuanto a los que confiesa como pequeños pecados, después los convierte en nada en absoluto: meros pecadillos, casi dignos de perdón en sí mismos. Muchas almas, no dudo, han sido atrapadas en esta artimaña, y siendo atrapadas por ella, han sido destruidas. Se han aventurado al pecado en donde pensaban que la corriente era poco profunda, y, fatalmente engañados por su profundidad, han sido arrastrados por la fuerza de la corriente a esa catarata que es la ruina de tan vasta multitud de almas de los hombres. Será mi asunto esta mañana responder a esta tentación, y tratar de poner una espada en sus manos con la cual puedan resistir al enemigo cuando venga a ustedes con este grito: “¿No es ella pequeña?” y los tiente al pecado porque los lleva a imaginar que hay muy poco daño en ello. “¿No es ella pequeña?”

sourceMetadata.title: Long Time, The
sourceMetadata.description: This life is short and passing quickly, but at the same it is a "long time" when we consider it as the time of God's mercy and grace in calling us to repentance from sin and faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. This tract is a call to every sinner to make diligent use of the time God has graciously given--time to acquaint oneself with God and to prepare for the yet longer time, eternity!

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Look to Christ and Be Saved
sourceMetadata.description: Scripture is full of invitations from Christ to the sinner to come unto Him for salvation. Why do so few respond to this invitation? Griswold shows that by nature, man has no desire to come to Christ. He loves his sin, and therefore despises the holy God. The Holy Spirit must move upon a sinner before he can desire to come to Christ. In coming to Christ, we are made free from the power of sin and Satan, and brought into favor with God.

files.author: William Reid
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Look to Jesus
sourceMetadata.description: Look to Jesus leads the student to the Savior of sinners, Jesus of Nazareth, the Son of Man and Son of God.  Are you a sinner? You will find no security in a religion focused on yourself and your good deeds. Take personal responsibility for your sin, and come to God through Jesus the Savior for pardon and blessing. Jesus died as the substitute for His sinful people, and God is satisfied with the price His Son paid. Having risen triumphantly from the grave and being seated as the King at the Father’s right hand, He now calls you to turn from your sins and your own efforts to save yourself and to rely entirely on Him as your Savior, your Lord, your Life!

children.title: Puestos sus ojos en Jesús
children.description: Puestos sus hojos en Jesús lleva al alumno al Salvador de los pecadores, a Jesús de Nazaret, al Hijo del hombre y al Hijo de Dios. ¿Eres un pecador? No encontrarás seguridad en una religión centrada en ti y en tus buenas obras. . Asuma la responsabilidad personal por su pecado y acérquese a Dios por medio de Jesús el Salvador para obtener el perdón y la bendición. Jesús murió como sustituto de su pueblo pecador, y Dios está satisfecho con el precio que pagó Su Hijo. Habiendo resucitado triunfalmente de la tumba y habiendose sentado como el Rey a la diestra del Padre, ¡Él ahora te llama a abandonar tus pecados y tus propios esfuerzos para salvarte y confiar completamente en Él como tu Salvador, tu Señor, tu Vida!

sourceMetadata.description: The gospel message preached today often omits the simple fact that salvation is of "the Lord." Sinners not only need a "personal Savior"; they must lay down the arms of their rebellion and submit to Him as Lord. In this tract, A W Pink calls us to reconsider a shallow view of the gospel and to keep the order right: Christ is our Lord and Savior.

children.title: Señor y Salvador
children.description: El mensaje del evangelio predicado hoy a menudo omite el simple hecho de que la salvación es del "Señor". En este tratado, A W Pink nos llama a reconsiderar una visión superficial del evangelio y a mantener el orden correcto: Cristo es nuestro Señor y Salvador.

files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Lost and Found
sourceMetadata.description: Jesus said that He had come to seek and to save that which was lost. What does it mean to be lost? Pink shows that this term refers to all the tragic results of the fall. Christ has come seeking those who did not seek for Him, and His mission will be successful! Pink illustrates this in the lives of Abraham, Jacob, Moses, and Saul of Tarsus. God takes great joy in rescuing His lost sheep. "Oh, what holy satisfaction is His each time He sees of the travail of His soul! How His heart is gladdened whenever He secures another of those who were given to Him by the Father!"

children.title: Perdido y encontrado
children.description: "¡Cuántas multitudes de personas hay que no se preocupan por su lamentable condición, de hecho, no tienen conciencia de ello! Aunque no se consideran perfectos, no son conscientes de que hay algo seriamente malo en ellos. Son personas respetables, ciudadanos respetuosos de la ley y nada en particular perturba su conciencia. Consideran que ciertamente no son peores que sus vecinos religiosos; y aunque casi nunca leen la Biblia o entran en una iglesia, esperan ir al cielo cuando mueran. Algunos de ellos admitirán que son pecadores, pero imaginan que sus buenas obras superan en gran número a las malas. Una clase más pequeña de ellos fueron rociados con agua cuando eran bebés, asistieron a una clase bíblica cuando eran niños, rezaron sus oraciones cada noche y luego se unieron a la iglesia; sin embargo, hasta este momento, nunca se han dado cuenta de que son enemigos de Dios y que son una abominación ante los ojos de Su santidad y que el infierno es su justo baldío."

files.description: Jesus said that He had come to seek and to save that which was lost. What does it mean to be lost? Pink shows that this term refers to all the tragic results of the fall. Christ has come seeking those who did not seek for Him, and His mission will be successful! Pink illustrates this in the lives of Abraham, Jacob, Moses, and Saul of Tarsus. God takes great joy in rescuing His lost sheep. "Oh, what holy satisfaction is His each time He sees of the travail of His soul! How His heart is gladdened whenever He secures another of those who were given to Him by the Father!"

files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Love of God to Us, The
sourceMetadata.description: A. W. Pink declares that while “The Lord is good to all: and His tender mercies are over all His works” (Ps 145:9), His love is reserved for His elect; moreover, His love is unchangeable, like Himself. But most importantly, the love of God for His people is “in Christ Jesus” (Rom 8:39)—that is, in His person, His blood, His death, and His righteousness. Pink goes on to expand how God’s love is expressed in the lives of those He has loved from all eternity: first in election, second in redemption, third in effectual calling, and fourth in healing their backsliding. He ends with this plea, “Make God’s wondrous love to you the incentive of your obedience to Him—gratitude requires nothing less.”

sourceMetadata.title: Man's Ruin -- God's Redemption
sourceMetadata.description: Man's Ruin – God's Redemption gives detailed explanation of Romans 1:16-32 to show the depth of man’s sin and the downward spiral in which he finds himself, ending in eternal separation from God. The last chapters focus on the living hope we have in Christ, the perfect unmerited Substitute provided by God in His love for us. We see that God’s righteous justice require penalty for sin, that man is incapable of paying for it himself apart from his own death, that a perfect Substitute was provided in Christ at the cross, that man must have holiness in order to stand before God, and that this holiness is found only in Christ.

children.title: La ruina del hombre - la redención de Dios
children.description: La ruina del hombre – La redención de Dios explica en detalle el mensaje de Romanos 1:16-32 para mostrar la profundidad del pecado del hombre y el descenso vertiginoso en que se encuentra, terminando en la separación eterna de Dios. Los últimos capítulos enfocan la esperanza viva que tenemos en Cristo, el Sustituto perfecto que no merecemos y que Dios nos Dios por su amor a nosotros. Vemos que la justicia justa de Dios requiere un castigo por el pecado, que el hombre es incapaz de pagarlo él mismo si no es por su propia muerte, que un Sustituto perfecto nos fue dado en Cristo en la Cruz, que el hombre debe tener santidad a fin de poder presentarse ante Dios, y que esa santidad se encuentra sólo en Cristo.
