files.author: Chapel Library contributors
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Marriage
sourceMetadata.description:
God instituted marriage at creation, which tells us that marriage is a union of the highest order. In fact, the Spirit of God informs us that the ancient story of marriage displays the eternal purpose of God in Jesus Christ! The Apostle Paul wrote, "For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh. This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church" (Eph 5:31, 32). The Living God not only designed, established, and blessed marriage; by it He displays Jesus Christ's eternal love for and His union with His bride. Thus marriage is a mystical and beautiful picture of the union of a man in woman in the holy institution of marriage. This must be why the devil has waged a ferocious and perverse war against marriage all around us. Adultery and divorce rates astonish us, even among professing Christians.

This is why we produced this issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster on marriage. A. W. Pink begins by declaring the excellence of marriage. John Angell James then details mutual duties of husbands and wives. The Puritan preacher Richard Steeles gives us the next two articles: the first explains a husband's love for his wife, and the second describes a wife's respect for her husband. William Gouge then counsels us regarding practices that promote peace and unity between spouses. In a second article, J. A. James gives helpful and wise counsel for those seeking a marriage partner, and Charles Spurgeon ends this issue describing the glorious marriage of the Lamb.

articles.title: Duties That Preserve Marriage
articles.description: a practical discourse regarding keeping unity between husbands and wives including mutual peace, mutual prayer, mutual care, and edification.

articles.title: Excellence of Marriage, The
articles.description: an overview and introduction to the institution honored by God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit and the primary reasons for its existence.

articles.title: Husband's Love for His Wife, A
articles.description: What does love for a wife entail and how does it show itself in real life? A look at this Christlike characteristic of godly husbands.

articles.title: Marriage of the Lamb, The
articles.description: Before the foundation of the world, God the Father gave His Son a bride, a people to redeem. History now awaits the consummation of the most glorious marriage of all time. The all-important question is do you trust the Lamb?

articles.title: Mutual Duties of Husbands and Wives
articles.description: duties that husbands and wives share in their pursuit of joyful, Christ-honoring marriage.

articles.title: Thoughts on Finding a Marriage Partner
articles.description: practical wisdom for evaluating a spouse, which includes seeking wise counsel, understanding proper attraction, using rules of prudence, and mutual desire for life in Christ Jesus.

articles.title: Wife's Respect for Her Husband, A
articles.description: What does reverence for a husband include and what does it look like in real life? A look at the nature, pattern, and effects of church−like reverence.

children.title: Matrimonio
children.description:
Dios instituyó el matrimonio en la creación, lo cual nos indica que el matrimonio es una unión del más alto orden. De hecho, el Espíritu de Dios nos revela que la antigua historia del matrimonio manifiesta el propósito eterno de Dios en Jesucristo. El apóstol Pablo escribió: «Por esto dejará el hombre a su padre y a su madre, y se unirá a su mujer, y los dos serán una sola carne. Grande es este misterio; mas yo digo esto respecto de Cristo y de la iglesia» (Ef 5:31-32). El Dios viviente no solo diseñó, estableció y bendijo el matrimonio, sino que, a través de él, manifiesta el amor eterno de Jesucristo por su esposa y su unión con ella. Por consiguiente, el matrimonio constituye una imagen mística y hermosa de la unión de un hombre y una mujer dentro de la santa institución del matrimonio. Sin duda, esta debe ser la razón por la cual el diablo ha librado una guerra feroz y perversa contra el matrimonio a nuestro alrededor. Las tasas de adulterio y divorcio nos resultan asombrosas, incluso entre aquellos que se profesan cristianos.

Es por ello que hemos preparado esta edición del Portavoz de la Gracia dedicada al matrimonio. A. W. Pink comienza declarando la excelencia del matrimonio. A continuación, John Angell James detalla los deberes mutuos de esposos y esposas. El predicador puritano Richard Steeles nos ofrece los dos artículos siguientes: el primero explica el amor del esposo hacia su esposa, y el segundo describe el respeto de la esposa hacia su esposo. Posteriormente, William Gouge nos brinda consejos sobre las prácticas que fomentan la paz y la unidad entre los cónyuges. En un segundo artículo, J. A. James ofrece consejos útiles y sabios para aquellos que buscan un compañero de matrimonio, y Charles Spurgeon cierra esta edición describiendo las gloriosas bodas del Cordero.

sourceMetadata.title: Mirage Shall Become a Pool, The
sourceMetadata.description: Twentieth-century Reformed leader Martyn Lloyd-Jones takes up the text of Isaiah 35:7, using it to describe the glorious results of the coming of Christ, His gospel, and His salvation. We journey through life as ancient nomads through a desert--world-wanderers seeking peace and happiness. Some think a change of place or the people around them is all they need to be happy. Yet the real unhappiness lies not in environment or relationships to other people, but in a lack of relationship to God. Lloyd-Jones points to Christ as our perfectly satisfying hope of help and comfort in our journey through the desert of life.

sourceMetadata.title: More Than a Calvinist
sourceMetadata.description: When we come to understand truths revealed in Scripture, it is a great temptation to think too highly of ourselves. God’s sovereignty is a point often debated between Calvinists and Arminians. Both sides are so convinced by arguments from Scripture that neither will concede any possibility of error in interpretation, even to the point of accusing the other of pride and obstinacy. Newton shows why man’s reason and intellect should not be trusted when interpreting Scripture. The Lord gives strength and reason and also withdraws it when He wills. The accumulation of spiritual knowledge does not equal actual spiritual experience.

sourceMetadata.title: Mortification
sourceMetadata.description:
Do we understand what it means to "mortify our members which are upon the earth" (Col 3:5)? A. W. Pink states, "No progress can be made by you in the Christian life, until you realize the paramount importance and imperative necessity of waging a ceaseless warfare against indwelling sin." John Owen tells us, "The choicest believers, who are assuredly freed from the condemning power of sin, ought yet to make it their business all their days to mortify the indwelling power of sin." This is clear from Paul's statement in Romans: "For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die: but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live" (Rom 8:13). 

So, what is mortification, and why is it important? What place does it have in our walk with Christ? These are some of the questions dealt with in this issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster.

Our opening article by Arthur Pink introduces us to the doctrine of mortification. John Flavel follows by explaining what mortification is not and what it is. Benjamin Needler then teaches us how to search out and identify beloved lusts. Only Christians can truly mortify sin: this is the point of Horatius Bonar's article. John Owen, who wrote a penetrating, helpful book on this subject, gives us clear directions on how to mortify sin. David Martyn Lloyd-Jones shows us that we cannot accomplish this without the power of the Holy Spirit. Many great perils attend our neglect of mortification; Ezekiel Hopkins, who also wrote an important work on this, warns us of them. Ralph Erskine helps us discern the difference between legal and gospel mortification. Finally, Christopher Love explains how we may determine if we are in a state of mortification or not. May this issue of the Broadcaster encourage and help us all in this holy war against sin, which we will fight until we see Christ in all His glory!

children.title: Mortificación
children.description: El artículo inicial por Arthur Pink nos presenta la doctrina de mortificación. Le sigue John Flavel, explicando qué es y qué no es mortificación. Luego, Benjamin Needler nos enseña cómo buscar e identificar los deseos de la carne que nos son queridos. Los cristianos son los únicos que pueden realmente mortificar el pecado es el tema del artículo por Horatius Bonar. John Owen, escritor de un libro penetrante y provechoso sobre el tema, nos da directivas claras sobre cómo mortificar al pecado. David Martyn Lloyd-Jones nos muestra que no lo podemos lograr sin el poder del Espíritu Santo. Nuestra falta de atención a la mortificación acarrea muchos y grandes peligros; Ezekiel Hopkins, quien también escribió una obra importante sobre el tema, nos advierte de esos peligros. Ralph Erskine nos ayuda a discernir la diferencia entre la mortificación legal y la del evangelio. Por último, Christopher Love explica cómo podemos determinar si estamos o no en un estado de mortificación. Quizá sean necesarias varias lecturas para llegar al fondo de algunos de estos artículos, hermanos, pero las recompensas son abundantes.

files.author: Chapel Library contributors
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Motherhood
sourceMetadata.description:
In the early 1600s, a young English woman, Elizabeth Brooke Joscelin, wrote an important letter. She was pregnant and concerned that she might not live to bring up her child. She began her touching letter by addressing her husband: “To my truly loving and most dearly loved husband, Tourell Joscelin: Mine own dear love, I no sooner conceived a hope that I should be made a mother by thee, but with it entered the consideration of a mother’s duty; and shortly after followed the apprehension of danger that might prevent me from executing that care I so exceedingly desired: I mean in Christian training our child.” Throughout her letter, her burning love for her husband, her child, and her Savior shines brightly. She was delighted with this thought: “that I should be made a mother by thee.” She wanted to bear children with her husband. Nevertheless, her heart’s desire was not simply to bear children—even non-Christian women sometimes desire this. Her longing for a child was biblically focused on “that care I so exceedingly desired: I mean in Christian training our child.” She wanted to bear and bring up children for the Lord Jesus Christ. Bearing children in her day carried with it a high mortality rate for mother and child. Elizabeth was deeply concerned that she might die without the privilege of teaching her son or daughter about Christ and how to live for Him. How did she calm her realistic fears? She could have avoided this fear altogether by simply practicing birth control or by seeking an abortion (which was available then, though not as readily). But she found her comfort in God’s Word: “These fears were cured with the remembrance that all things work together for the best to those that love God (Rom 8:28) and a certain assurance that He will give me patience according to my pain.”

Strengthened with biblical truth, she then wrote an astonishing letter to her unborn child, filled with instructions, biblical thought, and earnest exhortations for how to start, spend, and end the day to God’s glory. It was her Christian legacy to her unborn baby. She wrote detailed warnings, exhortations, and promises about everything from seeking God while a child, to starting and ending the day in prayer, to pursuing humility and modesty in apparel, to studying theology! She concluded the address to her beloved Tourell, “I hope God will so give me His grace that I shall more skillfully act than apprehend a mother’s duty… Thus, humbly desiring God to give thee all comfort in this life and happiness in the life to come, I leave thee and thine to His most gracious protection.” On October 12, 1622, she gave birth to Theodora. Nine days later, Elizabeth Joscelin died. She was twenty-seven years old.

To read Elizabeth’s letter is to step into a different world of motherhood than our own. Her legacy to her unborn child brims with biblical references; in fact, her very thinking seems to be saturated with Proverbs 31, Titus 2, and biblical womanhood. While she never had the pleasure of bringing up Theodora for Christ, her mother’s heart bares itself with astonishing beauty in her humble, but firm exhortations. Her burning desire to bear this child—fully knowing the risk—and her greater desire to bring up this son or daughter for Christ is the very essence of biblical motherhood.

For this reason, the theme of this Free Grace Broadcaster is Motherhood, a complement to last quarter’s Fatherhood. Jabez Burns introduces us to the dignity of motherhood, something often lost to our culture. Thomas Boston briefly explores a mother’s main responsibility—a subject quite foreign to our post-Christian worldview. Peter Marshall develops something of a modern parable to show us our desperate need for a return to biblical motherhood. An almost forgotten Scottish Congregationalist named James Cameron gives us three articles—biblically training children, encouraging mothers, and calling mothers to Christ. articles.title: The Dignity of Motherhood
articles.description: an introduction to God’s infinite wisdom and goodness in ordaining the vital role of mothers.

articles.title: A Mother's Main Responsibility
articles.description: What is the primary responsibility that God gives to a mother for her children? Food and shelter? Education? This is an important examination of a much overlooked subject.

articles.title: Keepers of the Springs
articles.description: Our culture has lost the biblical understanding of the role of a mother; this article challenges younger women to recover the crucial and God-ordained function of motherhood.

articles.title: Biblically Training Children 1
articles.description: a survey of the necessary attitudes and practices a mother must consider as she brings up her children for the glory of God.

articles.title: Biblically Training Children 2
articles.description: further biblical counsel for training children according to God’s holy Word.

articles.title: The Mother's Legacy to Her Unborn Child
articles.description: a poignant letter from a 27 year old mother, expressing her love and spiritual counsel to her unborn child; Joscelin died shortly after giving birth.

articles.title: Loving, Wise Chastening
articles.description: A mother’s discipline should flow from love for Christ and for her children; this heart-searching and wise survey can help mothers avoid provoking their children to anger.

articles.title: A Mother's Encouragement
articles.description: practical, valuable, and Christ-centered motivation for weary and struggling mothers.

articles.title: A Gospel Call to Mothers
articles.description: an earnest call to mothers to answer the penetrating question, “Are you a child of God?”

articles.title: Church and Motherhood
articles.description: a brief comparison between a mother’s responsibilities and those of Christ’s Church.

children.title: Maternidad
children.description: El tema de este Portavoz de la Gracia es Maternidad, complemento del número anterior sobre Paternidad. Jabez Burns nos presenta la dignidad de la maternidad, algo a menudo olvidado en nuestra cultura. Thomas Benton explora la responsabilidad principal de una madre, un tema bastante extraño a la filosofía de vida pos cristiana. Peter Marshall desarrolla una especie de parábola moderna para mostrarnos nuestra necesidad desesperante de volver a una maternidad bíblica. Un congregacionalista escocés casi olvidado de nombre James Cameron, nos brinda tres artículos: instrucción bíblica de la niñez, aliento a las madres y un llamado a las madres a volver a Cristo. John Angell James nos de otra semblanza de instrucción infantil, mientras que el puritano Richard Adams aconseja a las madres sobre una disciplina cariñosa y sabia. Una versión muy editada de la carta de Elizabeth Joscelin subraya numerosos temas prácticos y espirituales para las madres. Y Charles Spurgeon tiene la última palabra, trazando un hermoso paralelo entre la maternidad y la responsabilidad de la iglesia de educar a sus niños.

files.author: Charles H. Spurgeon
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: No Compromise
sourceMetadata.description: The biblical remedy for pragmatism; a sermon preached by Charles Spurgeon in the context of the "Downgrade Controversy," the controversy surrounding the liberal views of Scripture creeping into the Baptist union of the time. Spurgeon takes Genesis 24 about Abraham's servant seeking a wife for Isaac, and reminds us that there is no room for compromise when we are on the errand of the King. We must not adulterate our doctrine, our church discipline, our standards of holiness. The true servant of God is responsible for diligence and faithfulness; but he is not responsible for success or non-success. Result are in God's hands.

files.title: Obstacles to Coming to Christ
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Obstacles to Coming to Christ
sourceMetadata.description: In this tract, A. W. Pink considers the truth of Jesus’ words in John 6:44 “No man can come to me, except the Father which has sent me draw him.” He goes on to point out that the reason this is such a “hard saying,” even to many professing Christians, is that they fail to realize the terrible havoc which the Fall has wrought. According to Pink, the inability of natural man does not spring from any physical or mental defect, but from the utter devastation which the Fall inflicted in four areas—man’s corrupt nature, the complete darkness of his understanding, the complete corruption of his affections (that is, what he loves), and the total perversity of his will. Pink ends with a quote from Charles Spurgeon, “Without the powerful, supernatural, irresistible influence of the Holy Spirit, no human being will ever be constrained toward Christ.”

sourceMetadata.title: On His Breast
sourceMetadata.description: In this sermon Charles Surgeon recalls the love between Christ and John during the last supper as he gives practical exhortations to his hearers concerning communion with Christ. Elaborating on what it means to love Christ and be loved by Christ, Spurgeon declares: "Believe me, at this moment we have, or at least we can have, such intimate enjoyment of the love of Jesus... we speak of things which we have personally enjoyed; and we know that there is an intimate communion which is one of the private privileges of those whom Jesus loves much for it has been our privilege. I hope very many of you know this choice blessing of living in the immediate enjoyment of your Saviour’s love. May you never lose it!"

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: On Walking with God
sourceMetadata.description: Introducing this tract, James laments that “so few are found who are engaged in this high Christian privilege.” He goes on to elaborate what it means to walk with God. First, one must have been regenerated and possess eternal life. Second, those who walk with God meet much opposition “for they will oppose the course of this world.” Third, they have the seal of adoption as sons and daughters of God the Father, the sovereign Ruler over heaven and earth. Fourth, they love God supremely and “cannot be satisfied without the friendship of God.” James ends with this lively encouragement: “As beggars dressed in the robes of God’s righteousness, we forget the trials of this lower land and soar and sing of Him Who ever loved us and made choice of us.”

There was one issue at Calvary: 'We will not have this man to reign over us' (Luk 19:14)."

files.title: Only Trust Him! Only Trust Him!
files.author: Charles H. Spurgeon
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Only Trust Him! Only Trust Him!
sourceMetadata.description: The healing of the ten lepers is the object lesson of this message by Baptist pastor Charles Spurgeon. This story shows that an inward work of grace and faith must precede any outward signs. The lepers had to trust Christ before they had any evidence Jesus had done anything for them. Spurgeon discusses what empty signs men may look for as reasons they should believe in Christ, what are true grounds for believing in Christ, and what fruit will come from such faith in Christ as the lepers had. As the sick trusts a physician, so a sinner must trust Christ for relief from sin. The sinner must trust Christ completely for salvation. This sermon is helpful to all who think some certain work or feeling of their own must precede any work of God upon them.

files.title: Patience of God, The
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Patience of God, The
sourceMetadata.description: This tract is an excerpt from Pink’s book The Attributes of God. God’s longsuffering is often mentioned in Scripture, often alongside His mercy and grace. Patience and mercy are difficult to distinguish. Mercy pities the sinner in his misery, while patience bears with the sin that caused the misery. Divine patience is the power of control that God exercises over Himself, causing Him to bear with the wicked and keep from punishing them for so long. Pink shows how the patience of God is shown in His dealings with sinners. Every Christian ought to marvel at the patience God had with them while they wandered in sin, and seek to imitate this Divine excellency.

children.title: 神的忍耐
children.description: 神众多的完美的属性当中，这主题比较起来似乎被忽略了。那些详细阐述了神的属性的作者，有不少对神的忍耐轻描淡写。对这现象提出适当的理由是不容易的，因为上帝不轻易发怒无疑是神圣的完美，正如祂的智慧、大能或圣洁一样，也同样值得我们钦佩和尊敬。诚然，它不会像其他属性那般频繁地出现在圣经词汇索引中，但它的荣耀几乎照耀在圣经的每一页上。我们若不经常默想神的忍耐，不诚恳地祷告我们的心和行为能更加完全地顺服神，那便是我们的损失。

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Personal Holiness
sourceMetadata.description: This short tract emphasizes the biblical truth that while we are saved by faith alone, we are not saved by a faith that is alone. God's glorious salvation not only includes justification by the imputed righteousness of Christ received by faith, but also the glorious work of the Holy Spirit in making the dead alive so that they now do good works, not for salvation, but as the genuine evidence that they are the sons of God. "The genuineness of saving faith is only proved as it bears the blossoms of experimental godliness and the fruits of true piety."

files.title: Pilgrim's Progress for Everyone
files.author: John Bunyan
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Pilgrim's Progress for Everyone
sourceMetadata.description:
The Pilgrim’s Progress traces the journey of Christian from his first conviction of sin, through his conversion, trials, suffering, and victorious joy, and ultimately across the River of Death to the Celestial City.

Pilgrim’s Progress is read with the greatest pleasure.– George Whitefield (1714-1770)

I find this book so full of matter, that I can seldom go through more than a page or half a page at a time. – John Newton (1725-1807)

Next to the Bible, the book that I value most is Pilgrim’s Progress. I believe I have read it through at least a hundred times…Prick him anywhere, and you will find that his blood is “bibline,” the very essence of the Bible flows from him. – Charles H. Spurgeon (1834-1892)

That tenderest and most theological of books is pulsating with life in every word. – J. Gresham Machen (1881-1937)

children.title: El progreso del peregrino para todos  (condensado)
children.description: El Progreso del Peregrino fue escrito durante los 12 años que Juan Bunyan pasó en la cárcel. Ha llegado a ser, después de la Biblia, el libro más leído en su original en inglés aparte de los cientos de traducciones a otros idiomas. Esta versión cuidadosamente abreviada da a conocer al lector una provechosa alegoría de la vida cristiana.

files.author: George Black
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Poor Business
sourceMetadata.description: Men are extraordinarily careful about how they conduct business in this world, but many of these same are careless and unsure of their spiritual state. Many say “I am trying to be a Christian”, or “I am trying to cultivate a Christian spirit”. Black shows the folly of this: it is like tending a garden that was never planted. He examines why some men, so careful in earthly business, are so slothful in eternal business and encourages souls to manage their business with God while there is yet time.

files.author: Chapel Library contributors
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Poor Joseph
sourceMetadata.description: This tract tells the story of a poor, simple man named Joseph, whose job was to go on errands and carry parcels through London streets. One day he heard the singing of psalms as he passed the church of Dr. Calamy. He went in and listened in rapt attention as the gospel was preached from I Corinthians 1:26, 27. Not long after this, Joseph became dangerously ill. As he tossed in his sickness, his constant language was “Joseph is the chief of sinners; but Jesus Christ came into the world to save sinners, and Joseph loves Him for this.” One of his neighbors learned where he had heard this gospel, and summoned Dr. Calamy. Soon after, Joesph died, but not before he pulled out his savings from under his pillow and put it into Dr. Calamy’s hand to divide among the poor friends of the Lord Jesus with his testimony. Dr. Calamy was deeply touched by Joseph’s faith and told this story often. This tract shows the foundation of a belief of faith: the only Savior of sinners is God “manifest in the flesh”. The gospel produces love to God and to God’s people. The gospel provides hope sufficient to support the mind, even in the immediate prospect of death. Death comes to every man. May each soul possess the hope that Joseph had in death!

As he tossed in his sickness, his constant language was “Joseph is the chief of sinners; but Jesus Christ came into the world to save sinners, and Joseph loves Him for this.” One of his neighbors learned where he had heard this gospel, and summoned Dr. Calamy. Soon after, Joesph died, but not before he pulled out his savings from under his pillow and put it into Dr. Calamy’s hand to divide among the poor friends of the Lord Jesus with his testimony. Dr. Calamy was deeply touched by Joseph’s faith and told this story often. This tract shows the foundation of a belief of faith: the only Savior of sinners is God “manifest in the flesh”. The gospel produces love to God and to God’s people. The gospel provides hope sufficient to support the mind, even in the immediate prospect of death. Death comes to every man. May each soul possess the hope that Joseph had in death!

sourceMetadata.title: Practical Godliness
sourceMetadata.description: Baptist preacher A W Pink shows that before salvation, everything in our lives is wrong, with no thought for God’s honor and glory. There is much that God must correct and reprove. The Holy Scriptures are “profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness.” After salvation, our first concern should be to order all details of our lives so as to please God. Pink discusses how the Christian uses the Scriptures to discover God’s will for his life, and what happens when God’s Word is not used correctly.

files.title: Prayer from Hell, A
files.author: Holmes Moore
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Prayer from Hell, A
sourceMetadata.description:
Taking our Savior’s story of the rich man and Lazarus, Pastor Moore gives an overview of the rich man’s prayer divided into three parts—and draws lessons for us from each. 
First, the circumstances of this prayer serve to instruct us. The rich man prayed when he saw the kingdom of God; he prayed earnestly from a sense of need and in great agony, but he prayed too late.
Second, the petitions of this prayer are intended for our correction. He prayed to the wrong person, asked for the wrong deliverer, and sought the wrong water.
Third, the mocking response to this prayer is for our solemn warning. Abraham called him “son,” asked him “to remember,” and “to consider what he has missed.” Finally, he is told that hell is forever. And this dreadful fact will mock its inhabitants eternally.

children.title: Una oración desde el infierno
children.description:
Tomando la historia de nuestro Salvador sobre el hombre rico y Lázaro, el pastor Moore ofrece una descripción general de la oración del hombre rico dividida en tres partes, y extrae lecciones para nosotros de cada una.
Primero, las circunstancias de esta oración sirven para instruirnos. El rico oró cuando vio el reino de Dios; oró fervientemente por un sentimiento de necesidad y en gran agonía, pero oró demasiado tarde.
En segundo lugar, las peticiones de esta oración están destinadas a nuestra corrección. Oró a la persona equivocada, preguntó por el libertador equivocado y buscó el agua equivocada.
En tercer lugar, la respuesta burlona a esta oración es para nuestra solemne advertencia. Abraham lo llamó "hijo", le pidió "que recuerde" y "que considere lo que se ha perdido". Finalmente, se le dice que el infierno es para siempre. Y este terrible hecho se burlará eternamente de sus habitantes.

sourceMetadata.title: Reasons Why Some Will Not Come to Christ
sourceMetadata.description: “And you will not come to me, that you may have life.” These are the most tragic words ever spoken! Jesus plainly showed that life was only found in Him, yet those who heard refused to do the one thing necessary to have eternal life. Pastor Martin here outlines four major reasons why some will not come to Christ, and shows every reason inexcusable. Some are ignorant of their desperate need of Christ. Some admit their need but remain impenitent before His demand to forsake their sin. Some disbelieve the promises of Christ, while others demand additional revelation from Christ beyond what is given in the Bible. Martin shows why each of these reasons is indefensible before God, and that simple trust is all that is needed. “Whoever believes in Him will not perish but have everlasting life.”

children.title: Razones por las cuales algunos no vendrán a Cristo
children.description: «Y no queréis venir a mí para que tengáis vida». ¡Estas son las palabras más trágicas que jamás se hayan pronunciado! Jesús demostró claramente que la vida solo se hallaba en Él; sin embargo, quienes le oían se negaron a hacer lo único necesario para obtener la vida eterna. El pastor Martin expone aquí cuatro razones principales por las que algunos no acuden a Cristo, y demuestra que ninguna de ellas tiene excusa. Algunos ignoran su desesperada necesidad de Cristo. Otros reconocen tal necesidad, pero permanecen impenitentes ante su exigencia de abandonar el pecado. Hay quienes no creen en las promesas de Cristo, mientras que otros reclaman una revelación adicional por parte de Él, más allá de la que ofrece la Biblia. Martin explica por qué cada una de estas razones es indefendible ante Dios y que lo único que se requiere es una confianza sencilla: «Todo aquel que en él cree, no se pierda, mas tenga vida eterna».

children.title: Zifukwa Zimene Ena Sabwera Kwa Khristu
children.description: Chichewa/Chinyanja translation of Reasons Why Some Will Not Come to Christ.

files.description: “And you will not come to me, that you may have life.” These are the most tragic words ever spoken! Jesus plainly showed that life was only found in Him, yet those who heard refused to do the one thing necessary to have eternal life. Pastor Martin here outlines four major reasons why some will not come to Christ, and shows every reason inexcusable. Some are ignorant of their desperate need of Christ. Some admit their need but remain impenitent before His demand to forsake their sin. Some disbelieve the promises of Christ, while others demand additional revelation from Christ beyond what is given in the Bible. Martin shows why each of these reasons is indefensible before God, and that simple trust is all that is needed. “Whoever believes in Him will not perish but have everlasting life.”

files.title: Reconciliation - Man's Greatest Need
files.author: Lee Roy Shelton, Jr.
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Reconciliation - Man's Greatest Need
sourceMetadata.description: Pastor Shelton addresses the topic of reconciliation from the whole Bible. God and man are at enmity with one another because of sin. Therefore, man lies under the just wrath of a holy and righteous God. The sinner is far distant from God, and his only hope is reconciliation. In himself, though, man has no ability or hope of being reconciled to God. But God has made gracious provision for this reconciliation by the death of His Son. Christ is the Mediator, literally, the “go-between,” of a righteously offended God and a guilty, sinful man. It is because of the “good pleasure" of God's will, and because of His love for His chosen people, that God in Christ made a way to reconcile the world to Himself. Pastor Shelton shows that through the perfect life and substitutionary sacrifice of Christ, God made a way to be just to His broken Law, and yet also to justify poor sinners.

children.title: Reconciliación: La mayor necesidad del hombre
children.description: El pastor Shelton aborda el tema de la reconciliación a la luz de toda la Biblia. Dios y el hombre se encuentran en enemistad mutua debido al pecado; por consiguiente, el hombre está bajo la justa ira de un Dios santo y justo. El pecador está muy alejado de Dios, y su única esperanza es la reconciliación. Sin embargo, por sí mismo, el hombre carece de capacidad o esperanza para reconciliarse con Dios. Pero Dios ha provisto misericordiosamente esta reconciliación mediante la muerte de su Hijo. Cristo es el Mediador —literalmente, quien intercede o media— entre un Dios justamente ofendido y un hombre culpable y pecador. Es debido al «buen beneplácito» de la voluntad de Dios, y a su amor por su pueblo escogido, que Dios abrió un camino en Cristo para reconciliar al mundo consigo mismo. El pastor Shelton demuestra que, mediante la vida perfecta y el sacrificio sustitutivo de Cristo, Dios hizo posible satisfacer la justicia de su Ley quebrantada y, al mismo tiempo, justificar a los pobres pecadores.

files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Regeneration
sourceMetadata.description:
"Regeneration is an intensely solemn thing. The new birth is the dividing line between Heaven and Hell. In God’s sight there are but two classes of people on this earth: those who are dead in sins, and those who are walking in newness of life. In the physical realm there is no such thing as being between life and death. A man is either dead or alive. The vital spark may be very dim, but while it exists, life is present. Let that spark go out altogether, and though you may dress the body in beautiful clothes, nevertheless, it is nothing more than a corpse. So it is in the spiritual realm. We are either saints or sinners, spiritually alive or spiritually dead, children of God or children of the Devil. In view of this solemn fact, how momentous is the question, Have I been born again? If not, and you die in your present state, you will wish you had never been born at all."-From the Introduction. 

Here we learn the necessity, nature, and effects of the miracle of the new birth.

files.title: Remember Lot's Wife
files.author: John C. Ryle
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Remember Lot's Wife
sourceMetadata.description: In Luke 17:32, Jesus says, “Remember Lot’s wife.” According to J. C. Ryle, there are few warnings in Scripture more solemn than this. It is solemn because of the person Jesus names—not a godly person like Abraham, or Hannah, or Ruth, but one whose soul was lost forever. As Lot’s wife, she was part of Abraham’s family and thus enjoyed the greatest exposure to true salvation in her time. But Ryle asks, “Yet what good effect had all these privileges on the heart of Lot’s wife? None at all. She lived and died graceless, godless, impenitent, and unbelieving.” This teaches us that privileges alone are not what men need; they need the grace of the Holy Ghost. Ryle ends by asking a pointed question, “Have you yet received the Holy Ghost? If not, you are no better than Lot’s wife.”

children.title: La mujer de Lot
children.description: En Lucas, Jesús dice: "Recuerda a la esposa de Lot". Según J. C. Ryle, hay pocas advertencias en las Escrituras más solemnes que esta. Es solemne debido a la persona que Jesús nombra, no una persona piadosa como Abraham o Ana, o Rut, sino una cuya alma se perdió para siempre. Como esposa de Lot, ella era parte de la familia de Abraham y, por lo tanto, disfrutó de la mayor exposición a la verdadera salvación en su época. Pero Ryle pregunta: "Sin embargo, ¿qué efecto positivo tuvieron todos estos privilegios en el corazón de la esposa de Lot? Ninguno en absoluto. Ella vivió y murió sin gracia, sin Dios, impenitente e incrédula ”. Esto nos enseña que los privilegios por sí solos no son lo que los hombres necesitan; Ellos necesitan la gracia del Espíritu Santo. Ryle termina preguntando: “¿Ya has recibido el Espíritu Santo? Si no, no eres mejor que la esposa de Lot "

sourceMetadata.title: Resisting the Devil
sourceMetadata.description: What does it mean to resist the devil? Baptist minister Arthur Pink addresses this important and often-misunderstood question biblically, including the following insights: Submit to God. Understand the limits of Satan's power toward believers. Do not listen to his suggestions. Quote the Scripture in opposition to his temptations. Claim the promise that he will flee when resisted. Be sober, watchful, zealous, and constant in resisting him, all by faith confident of his ultimate overthrow and the victory Christ has provided for us through the gospel.

sourceMetadata.title: Resolutions of Jonathan Edwards, The
sourceMetadata.description: Beginning in 1722 at age 19, Jonathan Edwards wrote 70 resolutions designed to help him live a holy life. In a short preface, he humbly entreated God’s grace for help in keeping them. He also reportedly reviewed the resolutions once a week. The first one seems to summarize his overall purpose—“Resolved, that I will do whatsoever I think to be most to God’s glory, and my own good …and most for the good and advantage of mankind in general.” Other resolutions include speaking only the truth, temperance in eating and drinking, constantly studying the Scriptures, and much more. But most remarkable for such a young man were several resolutions which, in considering his own death, he resolved to live in such a way that there would be no regrets on that day. Edwards left us a beautiful 18th century example, one we would do well to emulate today.

sourceMetadata.title: Righteousness for the Unrighteous
sourceMetadata.description: According to the author, if he had one sermon to preach to the whole world, the message would show how an unrighteous man may become righteous before God. He goes on to describe the universal unrighteousness of men and their obligation to obey all of God’s law, pointing out that without perfect obedience the sinner could only be saved at the expense of justice. If sinners are saved then, it must be through a plan where God remains just and yet justifies the ungodly. And so it was that Christ kept the law perfectly and paid its penalty fully for His people so that they might be declared righteous. The author pleads with his readers, “If you are lost, let me urge you to acknowledge before God and men that you have no righteousness of your own, and trust Christ for the righteousness God has provided in Him.”

sourceMetadata.title: Righteousness of God, The
sourceMetadata.description: Horatius Bonar examines the righteousness of God and justification by faith. On the very first page he describes mankind’s problem: “The Law cannot give a righteousness; it is merely a declaration of what righteousness is. It condemns; it cannot justify.” He goes on to declare that there is a righteousness “which meets the case of the unrighteous in every part.” How can we characterize this righteousness? Among other things, it is the righteousness of God, a righteousness without the law, a righteousness to which the Scriptures bear witness, and a righteousness perfectly suited to the unrighteous. Bonar then turns to justification by faith, pointing out that it is God who justifies the ungodly with a righteous, complete, irreversible, and divine justification. Finally, he warns that those who perish because they reject the offer of God’s righteousness have no one but themselves to blame.

sourceMetadata.title: Sanctification
sourceMetadata.description: According to J. C. Ryle, sanctification is not optional, as some believe, but absolutely critical because if we are not sanctified, “we shall not be saved.” He goes on to give a detailed definition of sanctification by expanding on the 12 Scripturally-based statements below. Sanctification is—1) the result of our union with Christ, 2) a consequence of regeneration, 3) certain evidence of the indwelling Spirit, 4) a sure mark of God’s election, 5) a thing that will always be seen, 6) a thing for which every believer is responsible, 7) a thing which grows, 8) a thing which depends on diligent use of Scriptural means, 9) a thing which does not exempt one from inward spiritual conflict, 10) a thing which cannot justify a man, yet pleases God, 11) a thing which will be absolutely necessary in the Final Judgment, and 12) a thing that is required to prepare us for heaven.

files.title: Sanctification
files.author: Chapel Library contributors
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Sanctification
sourceMetadata.description:
In his book entitled Holiness, J. C. Ryle says, "If the Bible is true, it is certain that unless we are 'sanctified,' we shall not be saved." Throughout history, confusion has surrounded the doctrine of sanctification because finding the biblical balance in this subject is not easy. Some utterly reject a place for God's Law in the life of New Covenant believers, while others love God's Law and find it a blessed rule of life. 

In this edition of the Free Grace Broadcaster, A. W. Pink introduces our subject by asking crucial questions that inevitably arise regarding sanctification. Octavius Winslow offers a useful definition of the meaning of sanctification. J. C. Ryle then discusses the nature of sanctification, giving us a survey of its important elements. Winslow gives us a second article, explaining that all sanctification begins in Christ: His cross and atoning work, His intercession, and His Mediatorial fullness all lay the foundation and secure the sanctification of every believer. John Murray discusses the vital distinction between definitive and progressive sanctification. In his second article, Pink describes the two aspects of sanctification: mortification and vivification, both inseparable in the life of God's true children. Abraham Booth sets the motive of sanctification before us. Pink shows the difference between sanctification and justification. In two articles, Horatius Bonar shows us that holiness consists of the little things of life, and urges us to shine forth in reflection of Christ's glorious holiness.

articles.title: Definitive and Progressive Sanctification
articles.description: One aspect of sanctification is its once-for-all definitive character, yet the believer also participates in a process of transformation and holiness.

articles.title: Holiness in Little Things
articles.description: Believers often discover that maturity in holiness lies most often in little matters.

articles.title: Justification and Sanctification
articles.description: A believer’s knowledge of union with Christ is a doctrine of great comfort.

articles.title: Let Us Then Shine
articles.description: a brief survey of the marks and responsibilities of those who desire to live a truly Christlike life.

articles.title: Mortification and Vivification
articles.description: Sanctification begins in regeneration and follows a two-fold process of putting sin to death and living unto God in newness of life.

articles.title: The Definition of Sanctification
articles.description: a brief, but helpful explanation of the biblical meaning of this crucial subject.

articles.title: The Importance of Sanctification
articles.description: a call for believers to consider carefully this important and often misunderstood doctrine.

articles.title: The Motive of Sanctification
articles.description: Where there is no true love for God in Christ, there can be no true life of holiness.

articles.title: The Nature of Sanctification
articles.description: a survey of the elements of sanctification so that believers may better understand this supernatural, inward work of the Holy Spirit.

children.title: La santificación
children.description: ¿Qué es “santificación”? ¿Es una cualidad o posición? ¿Es la santificación algo legal o experimental? Es decir: “¿Es algo que el creyente tiene en Cristo o en él mismo? ¿Es absoluta o relativa?”. Con lo que queremos decir: “¿Incluye niveles o no? ¿Es invariable o progresiva?”. “¿Somos santificados en el momento que somos justificados o es la santificación una bendición posterior? ¿Cómo se obtiene esta bendición? ¿Por algo hecho para nosotros o por nosotros, o ambos? ¿Cómo podemos saber que hemos sido santificados o cuáles son las características, las evidencias, los frutos?... ¿Santificación y purificación son la misma cosa? ¿Tiene la santificación relación con el alma, el cuerpo o ambos? ¿Qué posición ocupa la santificación en el orden de las bendiciones divinas? ¿Cuál es el nexo entre regeneración y santificación? ¿Cuál es la relación entre justificación y santificación?... ¿Cuál es, exactamente, el lugar de la santificación con respecto a la salvación?, ¿la precede o le sigue? ¿O es una parte integral de ella? ¿Por qué hay tanta diversidad de opiniones sobre estos puntos, tanto que, si acaso, hay dos escritores que traten este tema de la misma manera? Nuestro propósito aquí no es, simplemente, multiplicar las preguntas, sino indicar las muchas facetas de nuestro tema…

sourceMetadata.title: Satan Considering the Saints
sourceMetadata.description: Have you ever thought about how Satan sizes up the saints as he prepares a temptation? Charles Spurgeon has. In this sermon, he takes as his text Job 1:8 where the Lord questions Satan, asking if he has considered His servant Job. Spurgeon shares his thoughts about how Satan carries out his work and what he considers about his prey. Satan aims to find any vulnerability that will allow him to further his intent to injure the saint and spoil his usefulness, among other malevolent designs. He considers potential weak points including our infirmities, our state of mind, the objects of our affection, our position among men, and our condition in the world. So what is the outcome? The Lord, in His sovereignty and lovingkindness, limits how far Satan can go while sustaining and sanctifying His children in the midst of their trials.

sourceMetadata.title: Scriptures and Good Works, The
sourceMetadata.description: "Many...in their eagerness to support orthodoxy as a system, speak of salvation by grace and faith in such a manner as to under-value holiness and a life devoted to God. But there is no ground for this in the Holy Scriptures. The same Gospel that declares salvation to be freely by the grace of God through faith in the blood of Christ...also assures us, that without holiness no man shall see God" (A. Carson). Here A. W. Pink shows us the place, necessity, nature, and importance of good works in the life of a Christian.

children.description:
ஆசிரியர் A.W. பிங்க்

வேதத்தை படிப்பதற்கான நோக்கங்கள்:

கடந்த சில ஆண்டுகளாக வேதவாசிப்பு மற்றும் வேதத்தைப் பற்றி படிப்பதில் ஆர்வம் கொண்டிருப்பவர்களுக்கு, ஆவிக்குரிய எவ்வித நன்மைகளும் இல்லை என்று நம்புவதற்கு பெரும் காரணங்கள் இருக்கின்றது. ஆம், நாம் அதுப்போன்ற சூழ்நிலையை கடந்து செல்லுகிறோம். நடக்கின்ற சில நிகழ்வுகள் நமக்கு ஆசீர்வாதத்தை விட சாபமாகவே முடிகிறது. இதுப்போன்றவை பார்க்கும்போது நாம் பயப்பட வேண்டியவர்களாக இருக்கிறோம்.

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Secret Sins
sourceMetadata.description: Oh, the dreadful danger of secret sins. While scandalous sins shake the church and give occasion to the world to blaspheme, secret sins are possibly worse. They enervate the power of the stumbling Christian, they weaken the church, they call for God's chastening hand. This collection of articles from prior centuries is a wake-up call to self-examination, repentance, and sanctification by faith in Christ and the freely given power of the Holy Spirit of God.

articles.title: Examination of Secret Sins, An
articles.description: an introduction to and definition of the sobering subject of secret sins.

articles.title: Final Judgment upon Secret Sins
articles.description: a moving, powerful vision of the Day of Judgment and the final revelation of the public and private iniquities of every sinful human being.

articles.title: Folly, Misery, Guilt, and Danger of Secret Sins, The
articles.description: a penetrating description of the foolishness and the ruinous end of men, women, and children who try to hide their sins from God and from each other.

articles.title: Man's Ways and God's Way of Covering Sins
articles.description: Sinners’ attempts to cover their sins have grim and tragic consequences; God the Redeemer, however, has a perfect way to cover sin.

articles.title: Our Secret Sins in God
articles.description: an extraordinary glimpse of how vile, perverse, and corrupt our sins truly are when we see them as the holy God of heaven and earth sees them.

articles.title: Plea for Those in Secret Sin, A
articles.description: a solemn, heartfelt appeal for those in secret sin to consider both the real condition of their souls and their certain condemnation in the Day of Judgment.

articles.title: Secret Sins Hinder Secret Prayer
articles.description: a searching examination of the devastating and destructive affect that secret sin has on the prayer life of those who profess to be God’s children.

articles.title: Sight of Sin and a Sight of Jesus, A
articles.description: God’s Law can strike terror in our hearts, tell us that we have sinned, and provoke us to flee the wrath to come; but a sight of Christ crucified melts the heart and provokes sinners to deep and abiding repentance.

children.title: Pecados secretos
children.description: Para exhortar a los pecadores secretos a salir de sus tinieblas y entrar en la maravillosa luz y libertad de Cristo, ofrecemos este número del Portavoz de la Gracia. El puritano Obadiah Sedgwick introduce nuestro tema. Nos ofrece un examen de los pecados ocultos y las diferentes formas en que los seres humanos los practican. Charles Spurgeon, quien nos ofrece tres artículos en este número, comienza el primero, considerando profundamente la insensatez, la miseria, la culpa y el peligro de los pecados ocultos. Thomas Brooks ofrece una mirada penetrante sobre el modo en que los pecados secretos erosionan y destruyen la oración, nuestra arma espiritual más poderosa. Spurgeon explica luego, dos maneras de cubrir el pecado —las del hombre y la de Dios—. Edward Payson nos lleva en un impresionante viaje al trono del Dios tres veces santo en el cielo y nos da una asombrosa visión de nuestros pecados secretos desde la perspectiva de Dios. Seguidamente, Jonathan Edwards nos ofrece una aleccionadora exposición de los pecados secretos, puestos al descubierto en el Día del Juicio. A continuación, Spurgeon hace una súplica urgente y sincera para que aquellos que están en pecados secretos, huyan a Cristo Jesús, de sus prácticas condenables. Finalmente, Octavius Winslow aclara, abundantemente, que si queremos una visión honesta del horror de nuestros pecados y si deseamos un corazón verdaderamente arrepentido, una sola visión despertará, eficazmente, nuestros corazones —Cristo crucificado—. Una visión del pecado y una visión de Jesucristo muriendo en angustia por los pecados de su pueblo, nos llevarán al arrepentimiento y a la paz.

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained

sourceMetadata.title: Self or Christ: Which Is It?
sourceMetadata.description: Bonar here expounds Romans 14:7-9. Each believer once lived a life the same as every worldling. Diseased self-love is the curse of every man. Now all is changed, and every aspect of life is different. Beginning with justification before God, self begins to be set aside. This work proceeds throughout a man’s entire life. Self is replaced by Christ, who now becomes everything that self was before. Every part of life is now consecrated to God. Bonar shows the diametric difference of a life dedicated to Christ, compared to a life lived for self. He encourages every man to examine his heart and motives. Is it self or Christ?

sourceMetadata.title: Self-Deception
sourceMetadata.description: John Angell James rightly declares that the very idea of one who thinks himself a Christian, but because of self-deception ends up lost for eternity has an awfulness about it that is beyond comprehension. In this short tract, James urges all of us to examine our spiritual state, “frequently, deliberately, solemnly, and impartially.” Explaining that it is not enough to trust one’s own examination, he also implores us to beseech God about our real condition. In conclusion James writes, “If you are not converted, you may be. God is as willing to forgive the sin of a false profession as the sin of no profession. Now repent, now believe, now hope…”

sourceMetadata.title: Self-Examination
sourceMetadata.description:
According to Thomas Watson, self-examination is a spiritual inquisition, bringing one’s self to trial. The rule by which one must try himself is the Word of God. Because man naturally loves himself, this is a difficult task. Men are reluctant to look into their hearts lest they should find that which they don’t want to deal with—but it must be done. If we do not try ourselves, we can never know how it is with us. In the end, God will try us—and His trial will be according to truth.

Whether our inquiry of ourselves proves we are truly God’s children or still in our sin-cursed condition, either discovery will be to our great advantage. If we find we have not grace, then the mistake is discovered, and the danger prevented. If we find we have grace, we may take comfort from the fact that we are heirs to “all the promises and in a state of salvation.”

sourceMetadata.title: Self-Importance: An Unbiblical World-View
sourceMetadata.description: Self-importance silently creeps into men’s hearts, influencing thought, desires, and even prayers. Every person is wholly opposed to worship God, but God chooses to search out and find those whom He wills. Chantry shows us that God delights to reveal Himself to those who have had no desire to know or serve Him. This is how each believer is saved: he comes to Christ because the Father drew him. He believes on Christ when God is pleased to reveal His Son. He repents of his sin because God gives him repentance.

sourceMetadata.title: Self-losing
sourceMetadata.description: Sinners are self-destroyers: no enemy can cause harm so much as a sinner can cause harm to himself. Nothing but sin can alienate us from God and bring us under His wrath. No one else can be blamed when a soul lands in hell: he did it to himself. Only God can save a sinner from himself. Baxter exhorts every man to forget self and self-love and submit to the loving will of God, for He can care for us better than we can ourselves.

files.title: Sickness
files.author: John C. Ryle
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Sickness
sourceMetadata.description: None of us likes to be sick. But as J. C. Ryle points out, sickness, like the sin that caused it, is universal to all mankind. And while sickness is indeed a misery, Ryle shows that, at the same time, it confers general benefits on mankind. He writes, “It is a blessing quite as much as a curse. It is a rough schoolmaster, I grant. But it is a real friend to man’s soul.” He goes on to describe some of the ways that God uses sickness for good and the special duties that its prevalence requires, concluding with some words of practical application. We can do no better than to heed Ryle’s final exhortation, “In sickness and in health, in life and in death, let us lean confidently on Him.”

files.title: Sin of Adultery, The
files.author: Lee Roy Shelton, Jr.
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Sin of Adultery, The
sourceMetadata.description: Society today disregards and looks lightly upon the seventh commandment, which forbids adultery and fornication. Pastor Shelton addresses these two particular sins which Christ said proceed out of the heart of man. The sanctity of home and marriage are ridiculed and joked about daily, but God does not take these sins lightly. According to Leviticus 20:10, adultery was punishable by death, as was fornication, according to Deuteronomy 22. These sins come from a heart of lust and impurity. Pastor Shelton shows that these sins are sins against self, the family as God intended it to be, and sins against God. He shows the great need of confession and repentance for these sins, and the permanent breaking off of unlawful relationships.

files.title: Sin of Lying, The
files.author: Lee Roy Shelton, Jr.
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Sin of Lying, The
sourceMetadata.description: The sin of lying has brought nations to the brink of judgment and damnation. There is no sin committed so much and thought so little of as the sin of lying. This sin makes a person more like Satan than any other sin. The more malice enters into a lie, the more nearly it resembles the devil. Lying is a sin most contrary to God’s nature, for He is the God of truth. God’s children are to resemble Him, therefore lying should be contrary to their nature. Pastor Shelton shows how hurtful the tongue can be. He addresses not only the sin of lying, but many other ways our tongue may be used to anger God and hurt others.

children.title: El pecado de mentir
children.description: El pecado de la mentira ha llevado a las naciones al borde del juicio y de la condenación. No existe pecado que se cometa con tanta frecuencia y al que se le reste tanta importancia como a la mentira. Este pecado hace que la persona se asemeje a Satanás más que cualquier otro. Cuanta más malicia conlleva una mentira, más se asemeja esta al diablo. La mentira es un pecado totalmente opuesto a la naturaleza de Dios, pues Él es el Dios de verdad. Los hijos de Dios deben asemejarse a Él; por tanto, la mentira debería ser contraria a su propia naturaleza. El pastor Shelton muestra cuán dañina puede llegar a ser la lengua. Él aborda no solo el pecado de la mentira, sino también muchas otras formas en que nuestra lengua puede utilizarse para provocar la ira de Dios y hacer daño al prójimo.

sourceMetadata.title: Sinner's Friend, The
sourceMetadata.description:
The Sinner's Friend proclaims the divine remedy for sin found in the mercies of Christ who came to save sinners by redeeming them from the power and condemnation of sin. In this book the sinner is reminded of the desperately wicked nature of his sin, the certainty of future judgment, and the ability of Christ to save according to the sufficiency of His sacrifice. The very essence of the gospel is the salvation of sinners.

"Will He not then have mercy upon thee, thou poor polluted, self-condemned, despairing sinner? Oh, yes, He surely will—for He delighteth in mercy; it is His darling attribute; therefore it is as impossible for you to be lost, as it is impossible for God to cease to exist, if you do but come in the right way, by Jesus Christ, the Sinner’s Friend, who is now pleading your cause before the throne of God."

files.title: Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God
files.author: Jonathan Edwards
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God
sourceMetadata.description:
Preached at Enfield, Connecticut on July 8, 1741, this is perhaps the greatest sermon ever preached in America—and is certainly among the most well known. Owing to its forthright dealing with God’s wrath and His intense hatred of sin and the sinner, it is also one of the most controversial. Indeed, for more than three-quarters of the sermon Edwards lays down a relentless stream of the most vivid and horrifying descriptions of the danger facing unregenerate men. While it is difficult to read such graphic language, there is abundant hope in the sermon’s conclusion. Edwards puts it this way, “And now you have an extraordinary opportunity, a day wherein Christ has thrown the door of mercy wide open and stands calling and crying with a loud voice to poor sinners.”

While those who would rather ignore God’s justice in favor of His mercy condemn Edwards and his sermon, those who were present and actually heard him preach that day reacted in a decidedly different manner. According to the diary of Reverend Stephen Williams who attended the sermon, “Before the sermon was done there was a great moaning and crying through the whole House, ‘what shall I do to be saved; oh, I am going to hell, etc.’” The diary goes on to indicate that Edwards had to interrupt his sermon and come down to minister to those who were under such awful conviction. And so, in spite of what the scoffers might think or say, “the amazing and astonishing power of God” was manifested among the people that day—with many falling not into the hands of an angry God, but into the arms of a mighty Savior.

children.title: Pecadores en las manos de un Dios airado
children.description:
Edwards y el Gran Despertar
Según una tradición, no estaba programado que Edwards predicara en la capilla de Enfield el 8 de Julio [1741], pero lo hizo en sustitución de otro predicador. Aparentemente, el Gran Despertar no había llegado aún al distrito y reinaba allí una total indiferencia de que sucediera o no, tanto que cristianos de distritos vecinos habían dedicado casi toda la noche anterior a la oración, no fuera que “mientras las lluvias divinas sucedían todo alrededor”, no las hubiera en Enfield. Edwards tomó como su texto Deuteronomio 32:35: “A su tiempo su pie resbalará”, repitiendo un sermón que había predicado en su propia iglesia poco antes sobre el tema: “Pecadores en manos de un Dios airado”. [Eleazer] Wheelock reportó a [Benjamín] Trumbull cómo los presentes, que había caracterizado como “indiferente y presumida”, tanto habían cambiado antes de finalizado el sermón que se habían “humillado con una convicción tremenda de su pecado y peligro”. –Iain Murray, Jonathan Edwards: A New Biography (Edinburgo, Banner of Truth, 1987), 168.

La predicación por medio de la cual el espíritu de estupor fue abatido en la década de 1730, era escrutadora y convincente. Se estaba levantando un grupo de hombres para quienes la gravedad del pecado, la posibilidad de una profesión falsa de fe en Cristo y la indiferencia de un mundo perdido les era una carga apremiante. Detrás de sus declaraciones públicas estaba su visión de Dios y de la eternidad. Sus valles de humillación personal se habían convertido en valles de visión y, como dijera alguien que siguió en los pasos de Edwards siglos después: “Cuando los pastores captan una vista del valle de visión, y del abismo sin fondo en el cual cada hueso se va hundiendo, sienten que es importante advertir y alarmar a los pecadores, y solo entonces predican para muerte, predican para la eternidad, predican para el tribunal de Dios, predican para el cielo y predican también para el infierno”.—Ibid, 133.

Esta edicion en audio MP3 narrado por Jose Garcia.

children.description: “Sự trả thù thuộc về Ta, Ta sẽ báo ứng, Vào lúc chân của chúng nó trượt ngã, Vì ngày hoạn nạn của chúng đã gần, Ngày tận số của chúng đang vội vàng tiến đến.” –Phục  Truyền Luật Lệ K. 32:35

children.title: Entre les mains d'un Dieu en colère
children.description:
Prêché à Enfield, dans le Connecticut, le 8 juillet 1741, ce sermon est peut-être le plus grand jamais prononcé en Amérique — et certainement l'un des plus célèbres. En raison de la franchise avec laquelle il aborde la colère de Dieu ainsi que sa haine intense du péché et du pécheur, il est aussi l'un des plus controversés. En effet, pendant plus des trois quarts du sermon, Edwards enchaîne sans relâche des descriptions saisissantes et effroyables du danger qui menace les hommes non régénérés. Bien qu'il soit difficile de lire un langage aussi cru, la conclusion du sermon offre un immense espoir. Edwards s'exprime ainsi : « Et maintenant, vous avez une occasion extraordinaire, un jour où Christ a grand ouvert la porte de la miséricorde et se tient là, appelant et criant à haute voix vers les pauvres pécheurs. »

Si ceux qui préfèrent ignorer la justice de Dieu au profit de sa miséricorde condamnent Edwards et son sermon, les personnes présentes qui l'ont entendu prêcher ce jour-là ont réagi d'une manière bien différente. Selon le journal du révérend Stephen Williams, qui a assisté au sermon : « Avant la fin du message, de grands gémissements et des cris ont retenti dans toute l'assemblée : "Que dois-je faire pour être sauvé ? Oh, je vais en enfer !", etc. » Le journal précise qu'Edwards a dû interrompre son sermon pour descendre s'occuper de ceux qui étaient saisis d'une si terrible conviction de péché. Ainsi, malgré ce que pouvaient penser ou dire les moqueurs, « la puissance étonnante et prodigieuse de Dieu » s'est manifestée parmi le peuple ce jour-là ; beaucoup ne sont pas tombés entre les mains d'un Dieu en colère, mais dans les bras d'un Sauveur tout-puissant.

files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Sins of Saints, The
sourceMetadata.description: “In every born again person there are two natures—the old and the new—the flesh and the spirit—which the apostle Paul tells us are contrary in the disposition, continually warring against each other.” Thus, A. W. Pink introduces this booklet which examines the subject of indwelling sin. He goes on to point out that since the old carnal nature remains in the believer as long as he continues in the body, there is always the possibility of his sinning. Pink addresses this important issue under four headings: a) one overtaken in a fault, b) the impossibility of a true believer being eternally lost, c) the consequences of a believer sinning, and d) preservation and perseverance of the saints.

sourceMetadata.title: Snare of Service, The
sourceMetadata.description: The main concern of the Christian should be thanking, praising, and adoring the One who has saved him with an everlasting salvation. But Satan cannot endure God being praised, so he will employ any and every device to turn the Christian aside from this. He is very subtle in his means with which he seeks to distract the believer from praising Christ. Pink warns that one of the chief hindrances Satan tempts the believer with is taking heed to the needs of others, rather than taking heed to his own godliness, as Scripture exhorts him to do. The highest privilege is not being engaged in service for Christ, but enjoying daily communion with Him. Service to our fellow men should be secondary to knowing God and studying His Word.

sourceMetadata.title: Soldier's Tale of Grace, A
sourceMetadata.description: This tract tells the touching story of Mr. Nordenberg, an engineer from Finland. He tells a story about Russian prisoners sentenced to be put to death at sunrise. While men on both sides raged, one of the Russian soldiers began to sing “Safe in the Arms of Jesus”. This man’s testimony led to an impromptu time of prayer and witness to the power of the saving love of Christ. The hatred of the Finnish soldiers for the Russians was changed into great respect. The death sentence was carried out, but Mr. Nordenberg’s heart was changed. He became a believer in the power of Christ’s redeeming love because of this captive’s testimony. This story is a testament to the power of the Holy Spirit to work in hearts and souls in even the most pitiful of circumstances.

children.title: Un soldado cuenta su experiencia de gracia
children.description: Este folleto relata la conmovedora historia del Sr. Nordenberg, un ingeniero finlandés. Él narra el caso de unos prisioneros rusos condenados a muerte al amanecer. Mientras los hombres de ambos bandos se dejaban llevar por la ira, uno de los soldados rusos comenzó a cantar «Seguro en los brazos de Jesús». El testimonio de este hombre dio lugar a un momento espontáneo de oración y de testimonio sobre el poder del amor salvador de Cristo. El odio que los soldados finlandeses sentían hacia los rusos se transformó en un profundo respeto. La sentencia de muerte se ejecutó, pero el corazón del Sr. Nordenberg cambió; gracias al testimonio de aquel cautivo, llegó a creer en el poder del amor redentor de Cristo. Esta historia es un testimonio del poder del Espíritu Santo para obrar en los corazones y las almas, incluso en las circunstancias más desoladoras.

sourceMetadata.description: A serious and solemn inquiry is presented in this tract: every person has an immortal soul which must spend eternity in either heaven or hell. What will it profit to gain the whole world and lose your soul? God has provided a way in which He can pardon sinners, without violating His justice or His truth. sourceMetadata.title: Spiritual Peace
sourceMetadata.description: In this booklet, Charles Spurgeon expounds on the spiritual peace of believers, which is peace with God and peace with our own conscience. First, he describes the solid groundwork of this peace and its noble character. Next, he discusses its effects—joy, love, desire for holiness, help in bearing affliction, and boldness at God’s throne. He goes on to deal with interruptions of this peace, which include temptations of Satan, ignorance of true doctrine, unconfessed sin, and unbelief. Finally, Spurgeon gives good counsel on maintaining and gaining peace with God. To maintain it, one does well to look always to the cross of Christ, walk humbly with God, and walk in holiness, avoiding every appearance of evil. files.description: In this booklet, Charles Spurgeon expounds on the spiritual peace of believers, which is peace with God and peace with our own conscience. First, he describes the solid groundwork of this peace and its noble character. Next, he discusses its effects—joy, love, desire for holiness, help in bearing affliction, and boldness at God’s throne. He goes on to deal with interruptions of this peace, which include temptations of Satan, ignorance of true doctrine, unconfessed sin, and unbelief. Finally, Spurgeon gives good counsel on maintaining and gaining peace with God. To maintain it, one does well to look always to the cross of Christ, walk humbly with God, and walk in holiness, avoiding every appearance of evil. And for those who have never had peace with God, Spurgeon implores them, “Seek this peace and pursue it; and above all, seek the Peace-Maker, Christ Jesus, and you will be saved.”

sourceMetadata.title: Spiritual Union and Communion
sourceMetadata.description: Spiritual Union and Communion is an indepth study on the topics of union and communion within the Godhead, in the person of Christ, and between Christ and His church. The church’s union with Christ is shown in its various steps or stages, of mediatorial, mystical, federal, vital, saving, practical, and experimental, culminating at the glory union in the glories of heaven. files.title: Strength Against Sin
files.author: Horatius Bonar
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Strength Against Sin
sourceMetadata.description: Men living in sin occasionally have the thought that they ought to rid themselves of it. Their conscience bears witness against them. Sin is a disease, bringing divine wrath upon the sinner. He loves his sin, yet may feel great shame and degradation because of it. The remedy, proposed by many false religions and philosophies, is to punish the body in order to eradicate the desire to sin and promote a desire to do right. Bonar shows us that God’s remedy is entirely different: He offers divine love and forgiveness as the root of holiness. A forgiven man seeks to keep the law. This is the Christian’s strength against sin. By the grace of God and because of God's great works for Him in Christ, the renewed man works for God, and avoids anything that would displease Him.

files.author: Charles H. Spurgeon
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Struggles of Conscience
sourceMetadata.description: In this booklet, Charles Spurgeon encourages those who struggle with an overactive conscience—specifically, those believers who long to know and be cleansed of their iniquities, and those unbelievers who think they must have a deeper conviction of sin before they can trust in Christ. Spurgeon’s message consists of Scriptural consolation and instruction, a caution not to confuse the work of the Spirit and the work of the devil, and finally an exhortation to those who are struggling to trust in Christ. He concludes by urging the latter to simply “Come as you are! Take Christ to be your all in all now.”

files.title: Subjection under God's Chastisement
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Subjection under God's Chastisement
sourceMetadata.description:
In this tract, A. W. Pink sets forth the believer’s proper response to God’s chastisement. All people are born into this world with an evil nature which manifests itself in a spirit of insubordination. Even after conversion, this rebellious nature is not entirely eradicated. Because of this, chastisement is needed to bring us into subjection to the Father. Pink examines various aspects of this subjection:

  • First, it denotes an acquiescence to God’s sovereign right to do with us as He pleases.
  • Second, it implies a renunciation of self-will.
  • Third, it acknowledges God’s righteousness and wisdom in dealing with us.
  • Fourth, it includes a recognition of His care and love for us.
  • Fifth, it involves an active performance of His will.

In the end, Pink reveals the two main reasons for this subjection—because He is our Father and because this is the secret of true happiness.
