files.title: Suppose an Unholy Man Were to Go to Heaven
files.author: John C. Ryle
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Suppose an Unholy Man Were to Go to Heaven
sourceMetadata.description: Suppose for a moment that you were allowed to enter heaven without holiness. What would you do? What enjoyment could you find there? And what would you have in common with the saints of God? Surely their pleasures are not your pleasures and their tastes are not your tastes. With this, J. C. Ryle begins this little tract. He goes on to consider the reader’s preferences—perhaps you love the company of the worldly-minded, the pleasure-seeker, and the profane. There will be no such people in heaven. Perhaps you think that believers are too strict and serious and would rather avoid them. These will be the only people in heaven. Ryle reminds of the Scripture: “Without holiness no man shall see the Lord” (Hebrews 12:14). And he pointedly asks the reader, “Are you holy?”

children.title: Supongamos que un hombre pudiese ir al cielo sin santidad
children.description: Supongamos por un momento que se te permitió entrar al cielo sin santidad. ¿Qué harías? ¿Qué disfrute podrías encontrar allí? ¿Y qué tendrías en común con los santos de Dios? Seguramente sus placeres no son tus placeres y sus gustos no son tus gustos. Con esto, J. C. Ryle comienza este pequeño tratado. Continúa considerando las preferencias del lector: tal vez te guste la compañía de los mundanos, los que buscan placer y los profanos. No habrá tales personas en el cielo. Quizás pienses que los creyentes son demasiado estrictos y serios y prefieren evitarlos. Estas serán las únicas personas en el cielo. Ryle recuerda la Escritura: “Sin santidad nadie verá al Señor”.

sourceMetadata.description: “Every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give an account thereof in the day of judgment” (Matthew 12:36). How easily awful imprecations roll off a profane tongue! The author speaks of the fear and horror that awaits those who so impiously and irreverently appeal to the Holy God. Those who call down damnation so glibly deprive themselves of eternal happiness, and plunge themselves into eternal misery. The author of this tract pleads with these souls not to continue taking advantage of the longsuffering of the God whose name they profane.

files.title: Take Heed How Ye Hear
files.author: I. C. Herendeen
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Take Heed How Ye Hear
sourceMetadata.description: The Bible is very practical and vitally important. Herendeen urges every soul to use “all diligence” to be “doers of the word, and not hearers only”. It is all too easy to listen without making any real effort to take in and put into practice what is heard. Many who sit under the ministry of a servant of God are “dull of hearing”, allowing their minds to be preoccupied with worldly cares and interests. Herendeen shows what characteristics are necessary for those who would truly hear the gospel, especially including earnest prayer for divine illumination.

files.title: Teacher's Daughter, The
files.author: William Reid
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained

sourceMetadata.title: Teacher's Daughter, The
sourceMetadata.description: In this short booklet, William Reid tells the touching story of young Mary Ann Whyte, a teacher’s daughter in Inverness-shire, Scotland. Mary Ann died rejoicing in Jesus Christ at the early age of seventeen. Relating several conversations leading up to her death, Reid’s story demonstrates her remarkable faith. For example, two days before she died she said to her father, “I know that death’s pangs are on me, but I fear it not. He (Jesus) was three hours in death’s pangs Himself, and should He leave me the same time, I’ll get home at one o’clock; and oh, what a joyful hour.” As those of her household gathered around, her last request was this: “I have called you that I might see you once more, and exhort you for the last time to make sure of your interest in Jesus. Take Him, and you shall be happy in life and in death.”

files.author: Chapel Library contributors
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Thankfulness
sourceMetadata.description: "I will extol thee my God, O king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever. Every day will I bless thee; and I will praise thy name for ever and ever. Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; and his greatness is unsearchable. One generation shall praise thy works to another, and shall declare thy mighty acts. I will speak of the glorious honour of thy majesty, and of thy wondrous works. And men shall speak of the might of thy terrible acts: and I will declare thy greatness" (Psa 145:1-6). The subject of this issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster was chosen in 2004 after the devastation of Hurricane Ivan, in thankfulness to God for sparing Chapel Library. We pray it will be used by God to enflame your heart with thanksgiving to our great God. William Cooper, a Puritan preacher about whom little is known, introduces the theme of thankfulness by declaring why all men should be thankful. In another article he teaches us how to give thanks in everything, even affliction. Richard Sibbes, who inspired men such as John Cotton and David Martyn Lloyd-Jones, briefly describes thankfulness as the disposition of God's people. Thomas Manton explains the holy duty of thankfulness, while John Gill, with characteristic thoroughness, lists a catalogue of Christ-centered reasons for thanking the Triune God. In a message originally delivered to seamen, John Flavel shows how to give thanks for the mercies God has lavished upon us. Charles Spurgeon gives us three articles this time: he exhorts us to give thanks even in times of difficulty and then exposes ingratitude as a sin for which there is no excuse. He finally preaches from the story of the ten lepers whom Christ healed, in which only one returned to thank Him. We pray with all our hearts that your souls will be moved by this Broadcaster to greater and continual thankfulness to our merciful God. He has delivered our souls for ever in Christ Jesus. "In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you" (1Th 5:18).

sourceMetadata.title: The Duty of Self-Denial
sourceMetadata.description: Self-denial runs against the grain of our indulgent Western culture. “Self-denial lodges but in a few breasts. It is a sacred, exotic herb which has grown very scarce.” Modern misconception tends to relegate self-denial to an ancient world of monasteries, hair shirts, and self-flagellation. However, as Watson shows, there is nothing more Biblical or Christian than true self-denial. “Self-denial is the first principle of Christianity. It is the life-blood which must run through the whole body of religion.” Christ calls us to deny our wills, our own righteousness, our appetites, our ease, our inordinate passions, our relations, our estates, and even our lives for Him. There is no alternative to a life of self-denial: “There may be going to heaven without comfort, but there is no going there without self-denial.”

files.author: Sam Waldron

files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: The Lord's Day: Its Presuppositions, Proofs, Precedents, and Practice
sourceMetadata.description:
The Lord’s Day is a thoroughly up-to-date consideration of the Fourth Commandment and its ramifications for modern Christianity. Its four sections include the Presuppositions that influence our thinking; Proofs at creation, by Moses, and in the New Testament; Precedents in the Apostolic Fathers and John Calvin; and finally its Practice. While precise and careful, the author avoids extremes and makes the nuances and complexities of the theological issues clear for most Christians.

Dr. Sam Waldron is the dean of Covenant Baptist Theological Seminary in Owensboro, Kentucky, and its professor of Systematic Theology. He is also one of the pastors of Grace Reformed Baptist Church in Owensboro. Dr. Waldron received a B.A. from Cornerstone University, an M.Div. from Trinity Ministerial Academy, a Th.M. from Grand Rapids Theological Seminary, and a Ph.D. from Southern Baptist Theological Seminary. From 1977 to 2001 he was a pastor of the Reformed Baptist Church of Grand Rapids, Michigan. Dr. Waldron is the author of numerous books, including A Modern Exposition of the 1689 Baptist Confession of Faith, The End Times Made Simple, Baptist Roots in America, To Be Continued?, and MacArthur’s Millennial Manifesto: A Friendly Response.

children.title: El día del Señor: sus presuposiciones, pruebas, precedentes y práctica
children.description: Este libro es una consideración completamente actualizada del cuarto mandamiento y sus implicaciones para el cristianismo en la modernidad. Sus cuatro secciones permitirán al lector introducirse en (1) las presuposiciones que influyen en nuestro pensamiento cuando consideramos este tema, (2) las pruebas de su validez y vigencia en la creación por medio del testimonio de Moisés y del Nuevo Testamento, (3) los precedentes de su observancia en los Padres apostólicos y Juan Calvino, (4) y, finalmente, su práctica, en la que el autor es preciso y cuidadoso, evitando así los extremos y aclarando los matices y complejidades de las cuestiones teológicas que envuelven este importante tema.

sourceMetadata.title: Treatise of Self-Denial, A
sourceMetadata.description: Do you deny yourself? Our Lord makes self-denial an essential mark of every true disciple, yet it is little-understood and much-ignored in our self-gratifying age. A Treatise of Self-denial turns our attention again to Christ’s warning: “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself” (Mat 16:24). The book is a Puritan classic: it is thorough, biblical, relevant, insightful, timeless, vital, God-honoring, convicting, and immensely important reading for every Christian. It is especially important for pastors, to restore to their preaching this fundamental doctrine. Manton skillfully and convincingly explores our need to deny self-dependence, self-will, self-love, and self-seeking. We pray your life will be transformed by reading and applying this exhortation.

files.title: True Confessor, and the False
files.author: Horatius Bonar
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: True Confessor, and the False
sourceMetadata.description: In this tract, Horatius Bonar presents what the Bible teaches about true and false confessions, noting that they both use the same words, “I have sinned,” yet they do not mean the same thing. He goes on to give Scriptural examples of those whose confession was self-serving and false, including Pharaoh, Saul, and Judas. Why were these confessions false? Because they were selfish, superficial, impulsive, and temporary. In true confession, the sinner—as far as he is able—comes to see sin as God sees it: a consummate evil and willful rebellion against God and His commandments. The truly repentant sinner draws near with an honest heart, in full assurance of faith, knowing that “if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins” (1 John 1:9).

files.title: True Heart, The
files.author: Horatius Bonar
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: True Heart, The
sourceMetadata.description: Man’s heart by nature is not true to himself or to God. But what does it mean to have a true heart? Bonar answers that a true heart is one that has ceased to misunderstand and mistrust God’s character, but sees that character as it is revealed in grace, and rests on His forgiving love. A true heart knows God as gracious, pardoning, sin-hating but sinner-loving God. Bonar shows what a false heart is, and what is the cure of having a false heart. The power to cure a false heart comes from the Holy Spirit showing us what God really is, and how sadly we have misjudged Him. Looking to Jesus is the cure for a false heart, the only way to produce a true one.

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Turn or Burn
sourceMetadata.description: Introducing the somber theme of this sermon, Charles Spurgeon points out how unpopular the doctrine of hell and eternal punishment was in his day—as it clearly is in ours. “I fear in too many places the doctrine of future punishment is rejected and laughed at…but the day will come when it will be known as a reality.” He goes on to explain the nature of repentance and addresses why it is necessary that God should punish men if they will not repent. Finally, consistent with its provocative title, Spurgeon ends his sermon with a precious promise and a blunt warning, “He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; he that believeth not shall be damned.”

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Useless Kinds of Religion
sourceMetadata.description: In this short tract, J. C. Ryle explains that there are two ways a man may lose his soul. By living and dying without any religion at all—a sure way to hell—and by contenting himself with a false Christianity. The latter, which he calls a useless kind of religion, is the most common way to hell for those who profess to be Christians. According to Ryle, useless religions take two forms: those in which Jesus Christ does not fill the principal place and those which join anything with Christ in the matter of saving one’s soul. His conclusion? It is “an awful thing to be content with a religion than can do you no good. Do not let this be your case!”

children.title: NHỮNG LOẠI TÔN GIÁO VÔ DỤNG
children.description:
Trong tài liệu phúc âm ngắn này, J. C. Ryle giải thích rằng có hai cách để một người có thể đánh mất linh hồn mình. Bằng cách sống và chết mà không có bất kỳ tôn giáo nào cả—một con đường chắc chắn xuống địa ngục—hoặc bằng cách thoả lòng với một Cơ Đốc giáo giả. Cơ Đốc giáo giả, mà ông gọi là một loại tôn giáo vô dụng, là con đường phổ biến nhất dẫn đến địa ngục đối với những người tự nhận mình là Cơ Đốc nhân. Theo Ryle, các tôn giáo vô dụng có hai hình thức: những tôn giáo mà Chúa Jesus Christ không chiếm vị trí chính và những tôn giáo kết hợp bất cứ điều gì với Đấng Christ trong sự cứu rỗi linh hồn của một người. Kết luận của ông là gì? Đó là “một điều tồi tệ khi hài lòng với một tôn giáo không thể mang lại lợi ích gì cho bạn. Đừng để điều này xảy ra với bạn!”

While by God's justifying grace in Christ we are spotless in His sight, our flesh is still sinful, wretched, vile! A recognition of our vileness before God is essential to cultivating the humility and dependence on Christ that we so greatly need as believers.

articles.title: Christianity’s Influence on the Condition of Women

children.title: Feminidad virtuosa
children.description:
Entre las preguntas más cruciales y fundamentales registradas en la Palabra infalible de Dios está: “Mujer virtuosa, ¿quién la hallará?”. La pregunta misma destaca su escasez extrema. Y, como la mayoría de nosotros bien sabemos, más escasa, más valiosa: “Mujer virtuosa, ¿quién la hallará? Porque su estima sobrepasa largamente a la de las piedras preciosas.” (Pr. 31:10).

John Angell James contribuye con tres artículos a este número del Portavoz: El primero describe la transformación y liberación de mujeres y culturas. El segundo revela que la misión de la mujer desde la creación no ha cambiado. Por último, el tercero testifica del poder relevante de la maternidad y da instrucciones provechosas, a fin de educar a nuestros hijos para Cristo. Charles Bridges pinta un retrato hermoso de la mujer virtuosa basado en Proverbios 31. Thomas Vincent presenta vívidamente a Cristo como el “mejor” esposo y llama a las mujeres jóvenes a desposarse con él. William Gouge lista cuatro gracias importantes que harán que la sumisión de la esposa honre a Cristo y luego da motivaciones excelentes con el fin de conmover su corazón para realizar esa buena obra. Algunas mujeres no tienen esposos ni hijos y W. K. Tweedie discurre sobre la obra extraordinaria que realizan para el Reino de Cristo. Jonathan Edwards ofrece consejos sabios a la mujer recién convertida con un breve extracto de unas de sus cartas. Y Jabez Burns culmina este Portavoz con pensamientos conmovedores sobre su abuela, quien, habiendo vivido como una mujer fiel y virtuosa pasó de esta vida a la gloriosa y santa presencia de Cristo.

sourceMetadata.description:
According to Robert Murray McCheyne if you have been born again, you will cry in your heart, “Lord, take the idols from me.” He goes on to describe seven major idols that every Christian should be aware of.

  • Self-righteousness. This is the idol that man loves most and God hates most.
  • Darling sins. Every man has his pet sins.
  • Unlawful attachments. How many worship a piece of clay that will soon be eaten by worms!
  • Ministers. You have good reason to love them, but make not an idol of them.
  • Earthly pleasures. This is a smiling, dazzling idol that has ruined millions. Money. You must not love money.
  • Fear of man. This grim idol has devoured many souls and trampled them down into hell.

McCheyne sums it up this way: we belong to Christ now, so what have we to do any more with idols?

files.title: What If I'm Not Elect?
files.author: Walter Marshall
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: What If I'm Not Elect?
sourceMetadata.description: In this eight-page tract, Walter Marshall addresses an obstacle that hinders some in coming to Christ—uncertainty about whether they are among the elect. Attempting to dispel these fears, he appeals to a number of Bible verses including John 6:37, which affirms that all the Father has given to Christ will come to Him and equally affirms that all who come to Him He will in no wise cast out. In the end, Marshall assures these timid souls that it is not presumption, but one’s bound duty, to carry out the great work of believing on Christ for salvation—and this without questioning beforehand whether one is elect, for according to Deuteronomy 29:29, the secret things belong to God, but those things that are revealed belong to us, that we may do them.

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained

sourceMetadata.title: What If It All Be True?
sourceMetadata.description: John Newton wasted years of his life in sin and misery, but the gospel of God's forgiveness and everlasting life through Jesus Christ brought peace and total transformation to the "African blasphemer." What if it all is true?  Where are you in relation to God? Do you have a peace that will stand the test of death, the Day of Judgment, and the eternity to follow? The only answer that will hold strong through it all is to be found in simple faith in the gospel of the great Savior Jesus Christ.

children.title: ¿Qué si todo sea verdad?
children.description: John Newton desperdició años de su vida en el pecado y la miseria, pero el evangelio del perdón de Dios y la vida eterna a través de Jesucristo trajo paz y transformación total al "blasfemo africano". ¿Y si todo es verdad? ¿Dónde estás en relación con Dios? ¿Tienes una paz que resistirá la prueba de la muerte, el Día del Juicio y la eternidad que sigue? La única respuesta que se mantendrá firme a través de todo se encuentra en la fe sencilla en el evangelio del gran Salvador Jesucristo.

files.author: Billy Morrison
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: What Is Freedom?
sourceMetadata.description: Writing from a prison in Northern Ireland, Billy Morrison discusses freedom from the perspective of a prisoner. He points out that release from prison will never bring real freedom. It will simply be release from the physical bondage of a prison cell, but not from the spiritual bondage of sin—under which every human being lives from birth. He goes on to describe the real freedom that God mercifully provides. God's gift of freedom delivers us from our deadly bondage of sin. “When Jesus came to this earth, He came to set free all those who would repent and believe the gospel (Mark 1:15), to set them free from the bondage of sin and all that this brings.”

children.title: ¿Qué es la libertad?
children.description: Escribiendo desde una prisión en Irlanda del Norte, Billy Morrison analiza la libertad desde la perspectiva de un prisionero. Señala que la liberación de la prisión nunca traerá la libertad real. Simplemente será la liberación de la esclavitud física de una celda de prisión, pero no de la esclavitud espiritual del pecado, bajo la cual todo ser humano vive desde su nacimiento. Continúa describiendo la verdadera libertad que Dios misericordiosamente proporciona. El regalo de Dios de la libertad nos libera de nuestra esclavitud mortal del pecado. “Cuando Jesús vino a esta tierra, vino a liberar a todos aquellos que se arrepientan y crean en el evangelio (Marcos 1:15), para liberarlos de la esclavitud del pecado y todo lo que esto trae”.

sourceMetadata.title: What Is My Hope?
sourceMetadata.description: Is my hope set on the things of this world? If so I will be disappointed. Is my hope set on my own accomplishments? I will be the first to let myself down. What is my hope? A sure hope and confidence of God's blessing in this world and eternal joy to come are to be found only in Jesus. He has paid the infinite price God demanded for sinners' pardon, and He has secured the eternal glory that our souls long for.

children.title: ¿Cuál es mi esperanza?
children.description: ¿Está mi esperanza puesta en las cosas de este mundo? Si es así, me decepcionaré. ¿Está mi esperanza puesta en mis propios logros? Seré el primero en decepcionarme. ¿Cuál es mi esperanza? Una esperanza segura y confianza en la bendición de Dios en este mundo y el gozo eterno por venir se encuentran únicamente en Jesús. Ha pagado el precio infinito que Dios exigía por el perdón de los pecadores y se ha asegurado la gloria eterna que anhelan nuestras almas.

files.title: What Lack I Yet?
files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: What Lack I Yet?
sourceMetadata.description: The story told by St. Matthew of the rich young ruler is perhaps one of the most solemn in the gospels. Pink takes up this portion found in Matthew 19:16-22, as well as Mark 10 and Luke 18, and examines its relevance to us today. He examines the characteristics of this young man, including his age, occupation, and reputation. He believed he could be saved by his works, but he knew he was lacking something important: the love of God in his heart. Christ is so gracious in dealing with this young man: He shows the errors in his thinking and gives him opportunity to turn into the right path. Pink shows what actually stood in the way of this young man, which was his love of self, and warns every soul lest he fall by the same temptation.

files.title: When the Salt Loses Its Savour
files.author: Maurice Roberts
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: When the Salt Loses Its Savour
sourceMetadata.description: Christians are the salt of the earth, as our Saviour said in the Sermon on the Mount. This means that Christians should be the ones who stop the natural tendency of society to decay into lawlessness. Christians should raise the moral and spiritual tone of society. But sometimes salt can lose its savor. This happens when Christians habitually behave in a way that is inconsistent with what they claim to be or believe. Roberts exhorts true Christians everywhere to examine their lives in light of the Moral Law, the Ten Commandments, which Christ “came not to destroy, but to fulfil.” True Christians will seek to keep these commandments, in an effort to live a holy life. Roberts shows that obedience to God’s law is the Christian’s way to glorify and enjoy God on earth, for “the way of transgressors is hard.”

files.title: Where Are You Going?
files.author: I. C. Herendeen
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Where Are You Going?
sourceMetadata.description: Time flies by, and soon years have passed before we realize it. Herendeen warns about the danger of becoming so engrossed in day-to-day cares of life that we neglect to prepare for eternity. Many have little or no consciousness of their lost condition, and think that a moral life is all that is necessary to get to heaven. Men are disturbed when thinking about the judgment that God tells us will follow death, so they put such thoughts out of mind and go on in their own way. Herendeen encourages every person to think carefully about their eternal future and to prepare to meet their God.

children.title: ¿Adónde vas?
children.description: El tiempo vuela y, sin darnos cuenta, pronto han pasado los años. Herendeen advierte sobre el peligro de dejarse absorber tanto por las preocupaciones cotidianas de la vida que descuidamos prepararnos para la eternidad. Muchos son poco o nada conscientes de su condición de perdición y creen que llevar una vida moral es todo lo que se necesita para llegar al cielo. A las personas les inquieta pensar en el juicio que, según Dios, seguirá a la muerte; por ello, apartan tales pensamientos de su mente y siguen su propio camino. Herendeen anima a cada persona a reflexionar seriamente sobre su futuro eterno y a prepararse para encontrarse con su Dios.

files.title: Which Thief?
files.author: Harry Ironside
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Which Thief?
sourceMetadata.description: The heart of this short tract is a warning about procrastination in coming to Christ for salvation. The theme centers around the two thieves crucified with Christ and the salvation of only one of them. But “thousands forget there where two thieves. They remember the mercy of God that saved the one, while forgetting the judgment of God meted out to the other.” The author asks pointedly, “Which thief, reader, would you be like?” And ends with this ominous warning: “You must be with one or the other for eternity.”

children.title: ¿Cuál ladrón?
children.description:
Hay miles que se olvidan de que había “dos ladrones.” Ellos recuerden la misericordia de Dios que salvó a uno mientras olvidan el juicio de Dios que le tocó al otro. Con descuido siguen vagando con la espera de ser salvos al fin; pero ai, cuántos están cortados en su pecado y son condenados para siempre. A ellos se les había presentado el evangelio muchas veces pero ellos presumían de la paciencia de Dios y lo rechazaron hasta que ya no había remedio.

Te preguntamos, ¿cuál ladrón te gustaría ser?

El ladrón que fue salvo creyó en el Hijo de Dios y está con Cristo ahora. El ladrón que se perdió menospreció al Salvador y está en las profundidades del sufrimiento. Tú tienes que estar con el uno o con el otro para toda la eternidad.

The theme centers around the two thieves crucified with Christ and the salvation of only one of them. But “thousands forget there where two thieves. They remember the mercy of God that saved the one, while forgetting the judgment of God meted out to the other.” The author asks pointedly, “Which thief, reader, would you be like?” And ends with this ominous warning: “You must be with one or the other for eternity.”

files.title: The Sin of Unbelief
files.author: John Bunyan
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: The Sin of Unbelief
sourceMetadata.description:
This tract about salvation used to be titled "The White Devil."

Unbelief is the main hindrance to the sinner who would otherwise come to Christ. Bunyan shows unbelief pretending to be a counsellor of heaven, using a show of reason in keeping souls from Christ. Unbelief agrees with the sinner’s conscience—his lack of goodness, his debt of sin makes him unworthy to come to Christ. Unbelief keeps the soul doubting the faithfulness of God’s promise of eternal life in Christ. Unbelief is a cruel taskmaster. Faith unquestioningly believes God’s Word because it is true, while unbelief doubts because it is true. Faith comforts in the midst of fears, while unbelief causes fears in the midst of comforts. With these, among others, Bunyan shows the folly of unbelief by comparing it to faith.

files.author: Horatius Bonar
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Whither? Whither?
sourceMetadata.description: Where are you headed, child of eternity? You are a child of time as well. Your life began in time, and it will end in time. But you are really a child of eternity: your soul will live for ever, and for eternity after the resurrection you will either enjoy God's presence in glory or suffer His unspeakable righteous wrath in hell. To which of these destinations are you headed? Whither? Whither? That is the question you must answer. Christ gave His sinless and perfect life to secure the way for those destined to eternal destruction to go to eternal glory.

files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Why Men Will Not Come to Christ
sourceMetadata.description:
Upon reprint, this will be retitled "Why Men Refuse the Gospel: A Message to Preachers".

Jesus said, “And ye will not come to me, that ye might have life…” (John 5:40). In this message for pastors, Henry Mahan examines the Scriptural basis for the sad reality that sinners do not flock to Christ. Sinners are spiritually blind because “the god of this world" has blinded their minds. Sinners are spiritually dead in sin, and must be regenerated by God’s Spirit. Sinners hate God’s terms--repentance and faith. They will only abandon their rebellion when God strips them of their self-righteous rags. “God give us preachers today who will rout the sinners out of their refuge of lies and exalt the God of the Bible.”

files.title: Winter Afore Harvest
files.author: Joseph Charles Philpot
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Winter Afore Harvest
sourceMetadata.description: J. C. Philpot compares the growth of grace to the stages of a shoot of vegetation. The spring of fresh regeneration brings its new bud of hope, and afterward it flowers into the summer of the peace of God. Yet the harvest does not directly follow. Philpot attests: "Harvest does not succeed summer in the kingdom of grace, as in the kingdom of nature. 'Afore the harvest' another season comes. A long and dreary winter intervenes, and with winter comes the pruning knife of the heavenly Husbandman, who purgeth the vine." But after the winter of trial's difficulties in the pruning of the Lord, it brings forth the harvest of spiritual fruit. The soul is edified as the Spirit of Christ moves upon the soul in His timing and working, bringing forth the fruit in His perfect seasons.

sourceMetadata.title: Wisdom of God: Mystery of Redemption
sourceMetadata.description: God has demonstrated His great wisdom in His redemption of men. In this booklet, the history of God's plan of redemption is reviewed with clarity as James Haldane considers God's glory demonstrated by the gospel of Christ. Though man's condition after he fell appeared absolutely hopeless, God in His all-knowing power provided the way for the salvation of men. Neither contradicting His own just attributes nor faltering in His redemptive purposes, "from  the  foundation  of  the  world;  from  the beginning  He  has  acted  on  a  plan,  originating  in  infinite  wisdom  and  perfect  goodness."

files.title: Withered Fig Tree, The
files.author: Charles H. Spurgeon
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Withered Fig Tree, The
sourceMetadata.description: In this sermon, Charles Spurgeon unfolds the gospel story of the withered fig tree. Going beyond the normal interpretation, he urges the congregation not to consider it only in relation to nations and churches, but to apply the lesson to their own lives, taking it “home each one to his own heart.” He goes on to consider the leafy—but fruitless—fig tree as a picture of those who profess faith in Christ, but show no fruit in their lives. He does this under three headings: there are such people in the church, these will be inspected by Jesus at the final judgment, and the results will be “very terrible.” Spurgeon concludes with a prayer that none of his hearers will suffer such a fate: “Holy Spirit, produce fruit in us this day, through faith in Jesus Christ our Lord!”

sourceMetadata.title: Wordless Book, The
sourceMetadata.description: This gospel message illustrates the truth of Psalm 51:7, “Wash me and I shall be whiter than snow.” The “black leaf” of the book points to the foulness of our sin, defilement that reaches down to the depths of our humanity. The “red leaf” tells us about the blood of Jesus, sufficient and efficient to purge the guilt and power of sin from our lives. The “white leaf” shows us the cleansed sinner, pure and white, washed from sin in the blood of Jesus, and that forever!

children.title: Libro en blanco, El
children.description: Este mensaje del evangelio ilustra la verdad del Salmo 51: 7, "Lávame y seré más blanco que la nieve". La "hoja negra" del libro señala la impureza de nuestro pecado, la contaminación que llega hasta las profundidades de nuestra humanidad. La "hoja roja" nos dice acerca de la sangre de Jesús, suficiente y eficiente para purgar la culpa y el poder del pecado de nuestras vidas. La "hoja blanca" nos muestra al pecador limpio, puro y blanco, lavado del pecado en la sangre de Jesús, ¡y eso para siempre!

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: World Passeth Away, The
sourceMetadata.description: Horatius Bonar begins this tract by declaring “Ours is a dying world, and here we have no continuing city.” He contrasts this world with a world that does not pass away, which he describes as “fair and glorious…bright with the love of God, and the joy of heaven.” He goes on to employ a string of metaphors which describe the present vanishing world, including—like a dream of the night, a mist of the morning, or a fading flower. However, while this world is surely passing away, man is immortal. He will spend eternity either in great joy or in deep darkness and sorrow. So the critical question is this: how can a man make sure that his life after death will be spent in the light and joy of heaven? God has long since answered that question, “Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved.”

children.title: El mundo se acaba
children.description: Horatius Bonar comienza este tratado declarando: "El nuestro es un mundo moribundo, y aquí no tenemos una ciudad continua". Él contrasta este mundo con un mundo que no pasa, el cual describe como “hermoso y glorioso… resplandeciente con el amor de Dios y el gozo del cielo”. Continúa empleando una serie de metáforas que describen el mundo actual que se desvanece, incluso, como un sueño de la noche, una niebla de la mañana o una flor que se desvanece. Sin embargo, mientras este mundo seguramente está pasando, el hombre es inmortal. Pasará la eternidad en gran alegría o en profunda oscuridad y tristeza. Entonces, la pregunta crítica es esta: ¿cómo puede un hombre estar seguro de que su vida después de la muerte la pasará en la luz y el gozo del cielo? Hace mucho tiempo que Dios respondió esa pregunta: “Cree en el Señor Jesucristo, y serás salvo”.

children.title: 世界即将逝去
children.description:
“世界即将逝去”

波纳 (1808 - 1889) 著

这世界，和其上的情欲，都要过去。 惟独遵行神旨意的，是永远常存。(约翰一书 2:17）

我们所看到的东西是暂时的。这是一个垂死的世界，在这里我们没有持久的城市。也许不久后，这里的一切都会改变。也许不久后，主就要再来，末后的号角吹响，大审判即将临到各人身上。

files.title: Yet There Is Room
files.author: Charles H. Spurgeon
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Yet There Is Room
sourceMetadata.description: In this short booklet, Charles Spurgeon explains that there is yet plenty of room for sinners to come to Christ. He then asks three questions: Where is there room? When is there room? Why is there room? Answering the first, he gives a lengthy list of where there is room including the fountain of Christ’s blood, the Father’s family, the church, and heaven. Regarding when there is room, his response is simple: right now there is room. Finally, as to why there is room, he offers another list which includes the “vast and wide” latitude of God’s decree of election and the infinite value of Christ’s sacrifice. Spurgeon ends with a prayerful request, “May God grant that many shall come to Jesus this very moment, for His dear name’s sake! Amen.”

children.title: Aún hay lugar
children.description: En este breve folleto, Charles Spurgeon explica que todavía hay mucho espacio para que los pecadores vengan a Cristo. Luego hace tres preguntas: ¿Dónde hay lugar? ¿Cuando hay lugar? y ¿Por qué hay lugar? Respondiendo al primero, muestra que aún hay lugar en la fuente inagotable de perdón que es la sangre de Cristo, en la familia del Padre, en la iglesia y en el cielo. Respecto a cuando hay lugar, su respuesta es simple: ahora mismo hay lugar. Finalmente, en cuanto a por qué hay lugar, ofrece otra lista de razones entre las cuales se incluye la latitud “vasta y amplia” del decreto de elección de Dios y el valor infinito del sacrificio de Cristo. Spurgeon termina con una petición de oración: “¡Que Dios le conceda a muchos que vengan a Jesús en este mismo momento, por el bien de su querido nombre! Amén” .

sourceMetadata.title: You Think You Are Doing Time Now!
sourceMetadata.description: In this message to prison inmates everywhere, Billy Morrison speaks to souls about the eternal prison sentence that awaits unrepentant souls banished to everlasting punishment. Souls may suffer in an earthly prison, but the eternal prison is described as the “second death” where torments persist day and night for ever. Morrison speaks of the hope found in Christ for those who believe in Him. He describes the way of salvation and the pardon and peace that can be found by all who trust in Christ’s sacrifice.

children.title: ¡Crees que estás cumpliendo condena ahora!
children.description: En este mensaje dirigido a los reclusos de todas partes, Billy Morrison habla a las almas sobre la condena eterna que aguarda a aquellas que no se arrepienten y son destinadas al castigo eterno. Si bien las almas pueden sufrir en una prisión terrenal, la prisión eterna se describe como la «segunda muerte», donde los tormentos persisten día y noche para siempre. Morrison habla de la esperanza que se encuentra en Cristo para quienes creen en Él; describe el camino de la salvación, así como el perdón y la paz que pueden hallar todos aquellos que confían en el sacrificio de Cristo.

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained

sourceMetadata.title: Your Sanctification
sourceMetadata.description: A collection of three sermons by Charles Spurgeon on the subject of sanctification. God cannot have communion with naturally sinful creatures, but being perfected by the blood of Christ, God sets us apart and allows us to have access to Him. As the beautiful vessels of the Temple were set apart for the worship of God, so the believer is set apart to honor and worship God and spread His gospel among the nations. All three persons of the Trinity have a part in the believer’s sanctification. Spurgeon discusses many aspects of sanctification. He shows the work God does in the heart and life of the believer, causing conformity to Himself, and separation from the pleasures of the world.

sourceMetadata.title: ¿Adónde vas?
sourceMetadata.description: El tiempo vuela y, sin darnos cuenta, pronto han pasado los años. Herendeen advierte sobre el peligro de dejarse absorber tanto por las preocupaciones cotidianas de la vida que descuidamos prepararnos para la eternidad. Muchos son poco o nada conscientes de su condición de perdición y creen que llevar una vida moral es todo lo que se necesita para llegar al cielo. A las personas les inquieta pensar en el juicio que, según Dios, seguirá a la muerte; por ello, apartan tales pensamientos de su mente y siguen su propio camino. Herendeen anima a cada persona a reflexionar seriamente sobre su futuro eterno y a prepararse para encontrarse con su Dios.

parent.title: Where Are You Going?
parent.description: Time flies by, and soon years have passed before we realize it. Herendeen warns about the danger of becoming so engrossed in day-to-day cares of life that we neglect to prepare for eternity. Many have little or no consciousness of their lost condition, and think that a moral life is all that is necessary to get to heaven. Men are disturbed when thinking about the judgment that God tells us will follow death, so they put such thoughts out of mind and go on in their own way. Herendeen encourages every person to think carefully about their eternal future and to prepare to meet their God.

sourceMetadata.title: ¿A dónde? ¿A dónde?
sourceMetadata.description: ¿Hacia dónde vas, hijo de la eternidad? Eres un hijo del tiempo también. Tu vida comenzó en el tiempo, y terminará en el tiempo. Pero en realidad eres un hijo de la eternidad: tu alma vivirá para siempre, y por la eternidad después de la resurrección disfrutarás de la presencia de Dios en gloria o sufrirás Su indecible ira justa en el infierno. ¿A cuál de estos destinos te diriges? ¿Adónde? ¿Adónde? Esa es la pregunta que debes responder. Cristo dio su vida perfecta y sin pecado para asegurar el camino para que aquellos destinados a la destrucción eterna vayan a la gloria eterna.

parent.title: Whither? Whither?
parent.description: Where are you headed, child of eternity? You are a child of time as well. Your life began in time, and it will end in time. But you are really a child of eternity: your soul will live for ever, and for eternity after the resurrection you will either enjoy God's presence in glory or suffer His unspeakable righteous wrath in hell. To which of these destinations are you headed? Whither? Whither? That is the question you must answer. Christ gave His sinless and perfect life to secure the way for those destined to eternal destruction to go to eternal glory.

sourceMetadata.title: ¿Cómo ir a Dios?
sourceMetadata.description: ¿Cómo ir a Dios? trae las buenas nuevas del Evangelio de Jesucristo en nueve mensajes cortos, cada uno desde una perspectiva diferente, invitando a los que están en este mundo a considerar cuidadosamente las afirmaciones de Dios sobre sus vidas. Estos no fueron sermones originalmente hablados, como lo es gran parte de la literatura actual de siglos anteriores; más bien, cada mensaje corto fue escrito específicamente como un tramo para captar la atención de los lectores a través del tiempo y las culturas.

parent.title: How Shall I Approach God?
parent.description: How Shall I Approach God? brings the good news of the Gospel of Jesus Christ in nine short messages, each from a different perspective, inviting those in this world to carefully consider the claims of God upon their lives. These were not originally spoken sermons, as is much of the current literature from prior centuries; rather, each short message was written specifically as a tract to command the attention of readers across time and cultures.

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: ¿Conoce usted a Jesucristo?
sourceMetadata.description: En este tratado sobre la salvación, el Pastor Pollard toma como su texto Juan 17: 3. Y esta es la vida eterna: que te conozcan a ti, el único Dios verdadero, y a Jesucristo, a quien has enviado. Él señala que simplemente saber sobre Cristo no cambiará la condición del pecador de la muerte espiritual. Para tener vida eterna, debe conocer a Cristo por experiencia personal íntima. Pollard continúa explicando el evangelio en términos de los tres oficios de Cristo. Jesús vino como profeta para que el hombre pudiera conocer la voluntad de Dios. Él vino como sacerdote para ofrecerse a sí mismo un sacrificio por los pecados de su pueblo. Y vino como el rey soberano que otorga a su pueblo la fe y el arrepentimiento que llevan a la salvación. Conclusión: El que tiene al Hijo, tiene la vida; el que no tiene al Hijo de Dios no tiene la vida. (1 Juan 5: 12).

parent.title: Do You Know Jesus Christ?
parent.description: In this tract about salvation, Pastor Pollard takes as his text John 17:3. And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent. He points out that simply knowing about Christ will not change the sinner’s condition of spiritual death. To have eternal life, he must know Christ by intimate personal experience. Pollard goes on to explain the gospel in terms of Christ’s three offices. Jesus came as Prophet so that man might know God’s will. He came as Priest to offer Himself a sacrifice for the sins of His people. And He came as the sovereign King who grants His people faith and repentance leading to salvation. Conclusion: He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life. (1 John 5: 12).

sourceMetadata.title: ¿Cuál es mi esperanza?
sourceMetadata.description: ¿Está mi esperanza puesta en las cosas de este mundo? Si es así, me decepcionaré. ¿Está mi esperanza puesta en mis propios logros? Seré el primero en decepcionarme. ¿Cuál es mi esperanza? Una esperanza segura y confianza en la bendición de Dios en este mundo y el gozo eterno por venir se encuentran únicamente en Jesús. Ha pagado el precio infinito que Dios exigía por el perdón de los pecadores y se ha asegurado la gloria eterna que anhelan nuestras almas.

parent.title: What Is My Hope?
parent.description: Is my hope set on the things of this world? If so I will be disappointed. Is my hope set on my own accomplishments? I will be the first to let myself down. What is my hope? A sure hope and confidence of God's blessing in this world and eternal joy to come are to be found only in Jesus. He has paid the infinite price God demanded for sinners' pardon, and He has secured the eternal glory that our souls long for.

sourceMetadata.title: ¿Cuál ladrón?
sourceMetadata.description:
Hay miles que se olvidan de que había “dos ladrones.” Ellos recuerden la misericordia de Dios que salvó a uno mientras olvidan el juicio de Dios que le tocó al otro. Con descuido siguen vagando con la espera de ser salvos al fin; pero ai, cuántos están cortados en su pecado y son condenados para siempre. A ellos se les había presentado el evangelio muchas veces pero ellos presumían de la paciencia de Dios y lo rechazaron hasta que ya no había remedio.

Te preguntamos, ¿cuál ladrón te gustaría ser?

El ladrón que fue salvo creyó en el Hijo de Dios y está con Cristo ahora. El ladrón que se perdió menospreció al Salvador y está en las profundidades del sufrimiento. Tú tienes que estar con el uno o con el otro para toda la eternidad.

parent.title: Which Thief?
parent.description: The heart of this short tract is a warning about procrastination in coming to Christ for salvation. The theme centers around the two thieves crucified with Christ and the salvation of only one of them. But “thousands forget there where two thieves. They remember the mercy of God that saved the one, while forgetting the judgment of God meted out to the other.” The author asks pointedly, “Which thief, reader, would you be like?” And ends with this ominous warning: “You must be with one or the other for eternity.”

sourceMetadata.title: ¿Es realmente tan malo el aborto?
sourceMetadata.description: Más de 53 millones de niños no nacidos han sido asesinados en abortos legales cometidos en los Estados Unidos y Canadá. Ciertamente, deberíamos tener una base ética sólida para sancionar legalmente el final de tantas vidas en nuestras naciones, más más de un millón cada año. Por lo tanto, examinamos los argumentos utilizados por aquellos que promueven el aborto para determinar en qué medida se basa esta práctica. Luego nos dirigimos a un tribunal de autoridad más alto que el razonamiento humano para exponer las verdades de la Palabra de Dios que están involucradas en el tema del aborto.

parent.title: Is Abortion Really So Bad?
parent.description: Over 53 million unborn children have been killed in legal abortions committed in the United States and Canada. We certainly should have a strong ethical basis to legally sanction the ending of so many lives in our nations, plus over a million more each year. We therefore examine the arguments used by those who promote abortion to determine on how strong of a foundation this practice is based. Then we turn to a higher court of authority than human reasoning to set forth the truths of God’s Word that are involved in the issue of abortion.

sourceMetadata.title: ¿Qué es el cristianismo?
sourceMetadata.description:
El tercer capitulo de Filipenses nos da el modelo de un cristiano verdadero.

  1. La posición del cristiano
  2. El objetivo del cristiano
  3. La esperanza del cristiano

Mackintosh analiza Filipenses 3, pasaje que nos presenta el modelo del verdadero cristiano: su posición, su objetivo y su esperanza. A la luz del evangelio, el legalista debe dejar de lado su propia justicia, tras haber hallado una justicia superior en Cristo. Si bien los pecados pueden llevar al pecador hacia Cristo, lo más importante es que las excelencias de Cristo nos atraen hacia Él. Mackintosh señala que el objetivo es conocer a Cristo y fijar la mirada en Él. Al tener a Cristo como nuestra justicia, anhelamos conocerle y procuramos con mayor fervor ser como Él.

parent.title: What Is Christianity?
parent.description: Mackintosh discusses Philippians 3, which gives us the model of a true Christian: his standing, his object, and his hope. In light of the gospel, the legalist must cast aside his own righteousness, having found a better righteousness in Christ. Sins may drive the sinner to Christ, but more importantly, Christ’s excellencies draw us to Him. Mackintosh shows the object is to know Christ, to fix our gaze on Him. With Christ as our righteousness, we long to know Him, and more ardently seek to be like Him.

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained

sourceMetadata.title: ¿Qué es la libertad?
sourceMetadata.description: Escribiendo desde una prisión en Irlanda del Norte, Billy Morrison analiza la libertad desde la perspectiva de un prisionero. Señala que la liberación de la prisión nunca traerá la libertad real. Simplemente será la liberación de la esclavitud física de una celda de prisión, pero no de la esclavitud espiritual del pecado, bajo la cual todo ser humano vive desde su nacimiento. Continúa describiendo la verdadera libertad que Dios misericordiosamente proporciona. El regalo de Dios de la libertad nos libera de nuestra esclavitud mortal del pecado. “Cuando Jesús vino a esta tierra, vino a liberar a todos aquellos que se arrepientan y crean en el evangelio (Marcos 1:15), para liberarlos de la esclavitud del pecado y todo lo que esto trae”.

parent.title: What Is Freedom?
parent.description: Writing from a prison in Northern Ireland, Billy Morrison discusses freedom from the perspective of a prisoner. He points out that release from prison will never bring real freedom. It will simply be release from the physical bondage of a prison cell, but not from the spiritual bondage of sin—under which every human being lives from birth. He goes on to describe the real freedom that God mercifully provides. God's gift of freedom delivers us from our deadly bondage of sin. “When Jesus came to this earth, He came to set free all those who would repent and believe the gospel (Mark 1:15), to set them free from the bondage of sin and all that this brings.”

sourceMetadata.title: ¿Qué es un cristiano bíblico?
sourceMetadata.description:
¿Qué es un cristiano bíblico? es una investigación puntual y extremadamente útil sobre el verdadero estado del alma. El autor se pregunta: “De acuerdo a las Escrituras, ¿Cuándo tiene un hombre, mujer, niño o niña derecho al nombre de cristiano? Uno no debe asumir a la ligera que él o ella es un verdadero cristiano. Una conclusión falsa en este punto es trágica y fatal. Por lo tanto, quiero presentarles cuatro líneas de la respuesta de la Biblia a la pregunta: ¿Qué es un cristiano bíblico?

Albert N. Martin servido durante cuarenta y seis años, de 1962 a 2008, como pastor de la Iglesia Bautista Trinity de Montville, New Jersey. Su ministerio de enseñanza es conocido por la exposición completa y poderosa de la Palabra de Dios. Hoy sirve en el ministerio de escribir y conferencias desde su casa en Michigan.

parent.title: What Is a Biblical Christian?
parent.description:
What Is a Biblical Christian? is a pointed and extremely helpful inquiry into the true state of the soul. The author asks: “According to the Scriptures, when does a man, woman, boy or girl have the right to the name Christian? One must not make the assumption lightly that he or she is a true Christian. A false conclusion at this point is tragic and fatal. Therefore I want to set before you four strands of the Bible’s answer to the question: What is a Biblical Christian? ”

Albert N. Martin served for forty-six years from 1962 to 2008 as pastor of Trinity Baptist Church of Montville, New Jersey. His teaching ministry is known for thorough and powerful exposition of God’s Word. Today he serves in writing and conference ministry from his home in Michigan.

parent.title: What If It All Be True?
parent.description: John Newton wasted years of his life in sin and misery, but the gospel of God's forgiveness and everlasting life through Jesus Christ brought peace and total transformation to the "African blasphemer." What if it all is true?  Where are you in relation to God? Do you have a peace that will stand the test of death, the Day of Judgment, and the eternity to follow? The only answer that will hold strong through it all is to be found in simple faith in the gospel of the great Savior Jesus Christ.

¿Vivo o muerto? por J. C. Ryle, postula la pregunta que ha enfrentado cada ser humano que jamás ha vivido: ¿Te encuentras tú entre los vivos o  los muertos? En su estilo directo y llamativo, el autor desafía al lector a considerar su propia condición antes de “cerrar este librito”. Los temas que trata son: 1. Todos están espiritualmente muertos, 2. Todos necesitan que Dios les dé vida, 3. Cómo cobra vida un alma muerta y 4. ¿Estás vivo?

Narración: Ernesto Rodriguez

parent.title: Alive or Dead?
parent.description:
J.C. Ryle’s Alive or Dead asks the question faced by every human who has ever lived: Are you among the living or the dead? In his direct and engaging style, Ryle challenges the reader to consider his own condition, and call upon God to turn him in the right direction before he “lays down this booklet.” Sections include
1. All are spiritually dead 
2. All need to be made alive
3. How a dead soul is made alive
4. Are you alive?

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained

sourceMetadata.title: Arrepiéntete o perecerás
sourceMetadata.description: "Antes si no os arrepentís, todos pereceréis igualmente." (Lucas 13: 3). Lamentablemente, esta verdad bíblica rara vez se escucha en nuestras iglesias modernas. Pero como señala AW Pink, "el arrepentimiento es absolutamente necesario si el pecador debe hacer las paces con Dios". Continúa describiendo el arrepentimiento como "Un odio santo y el horror del pecado, un profundo dolor por él y su reconocimiento ante Dios, y un corazón completo para abandonarlo ". Pink termina este breve tramo con una declaración escalofriante y una pregunta, “Cambia de tu curso de voluntad propia; Gire con todo el propósito del corazón para complacerlo y servirle: o ser atormentado día y noche, por los siglos de los siglos, en el Lago de Fuego. ¿Cuál será? ”

parent.title: Repent or Perish
parent.description: “Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish” (Luke 13:3). Sadly, this Biblical truth is seldom heard in our modern churches. But as A. W. Pink points out, “Repentance is absolutely necessary if the sinner is to make peace with God.” He goes on to describe repentance as, “A holy hatred and horror of sin, a deep sorrow for it, and acknowledgement of it before God, and a complete heart forsaking of it.” Pink ends this short tract with a chilling statement and a question, “Turn from your course of self-will; turn with full purpose of heart to please and serve HIM: or be tormented day and night, forever and ever, in the Lake of Fire. Which shall it be?”

sourceMetadata.description: En este breve folleto, Charles Spurgeon explica que todavía hay mucho espacio para que los pecadores vengan a Cristo. Luego hace tres preguntas: ¿Dónde hay lugar? ¿Cuando hay lugar? y ¿Por qué hay lugar? Respondiendo al primero, muestra que aún hay lugar en la fuente inagotable de perdón que es la sangre de Cristo, en la familia del Padre, en la iglesia y en el cielo. Respecto a cuando hay lugar, su respuesta es simple: ahora mismo hay lugar. Finalmente, en cuanto a por qué hay lugar, ofrece otra lista de razones entre las cuales se incluye la latitud “vasta y amplia” del decreto de elección de Dios y el valor infinito del sacrificio de Cristo. Spurgeon termina con una petición de oración: “¡Que Dios le conceda a muchos que vengan a Jesús en este mismo momento, por el bien de su querido nombre! Amén” .

parent.title: Yet There Is Room
parent.description: In this short booklet, Charles Spurgeon explains that there is yet plenty of room for sinners to come to Christ. He then asks three questions: Where is there room? When is there room? Why is there room? Answering the first, he gives a lengthy list of where there is room including the fountain of Christ’s blood, the Father’s family, the church, and heaven. Regarding when there is room, his response is simple: right now there is room. Finally, as to why there is room, he offers another list which includes the “vast and wide” latitude of God’s decree of election and the infinite value of Christ’s sacrifice. Spurgeon ends with a prayerful request, “May God grant that many shall come to Jesus this very moment, for His dear name’s sake! Amen.”

sourceMetadata.title: Bebés
sourceMetadata.description: Esta edición de Portavoz de la Gracia se trata de bebés. Juan Calvino presenta este tema vital explicando la majestuosidad creada de hombres y mujeres, y destaca con cuidado que Dios diseñó nuestros cuerpos para engendrar y tener hijos. Martín Lutero nos recuerda que Dios mandó a hombres y mujeres que dieran fruto y se multiplicaran. El puritano Thomas Manton declara con aplomo que los hijos son herencia y recompensa del Señor. Una vez que Dios nos bendice con hijos, ¿qué hacemos con ellos? Para responder a esta pregunta J. R. Miller presenta un resumen maravilloso de cómo amar y cuidar a nuestros bebés. ¿Qué quiso decir Pablo cuando escribió que la mujer “se salvará engendrando hijos”? Stephen Charnock, otro predicador y teólogo puritano, nos da una buena respuesta a esta pregunta difícil. Richard Adams, también predicador puritano, nos ofrece una perspectiva general de las cuatro gracias necesarias para tener hijos y nos ofrece un segundo artículo acerca de la mejor manera de animar y apoyar a la mujer embarazada. A. W. Pink explica la gran fe de Sara de que concebiría en su vejez. El puritano Thomas Jacombe ofrece consuelo a aquellos que no pueden tener hijos. Y, por último, Thomas Boston enfoca el tema del bebé más importante de todos los tiempos.

parent.title: Babies
parent.description:
This issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster delves into the theology of bearing children from a biblical and Puritan perspective.

Babies are made in God’s image, God’s elect come from babies, and God’s promise of salvation was promised and fulfilled in a baby. “She shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins” (Mat 1:20-21). Babies are important.

Explore this fascinating subject with articles from John Calvin, Martin Luther, Thomas Manton, J. R. Miller, Stephen Charnock, Richard Adams, Arthur Pink, Thomas Jacombe, and Thomas Boston.

articles.title: La imagen de Dios y la bendición de Dios
articles.description: Un examen reflexivo del hecho de que Dios creara al hombre a su imagen, y la hermosura majestuosa del hombre como varón y hembra. Dios los diseñó específicamente para que produjeran hijos.

articles.title: Fructificad y multiplicaos
articles.description: Una exposición del mandato de Dios para la procreación humana y su gran bendición sobre ella.

articles.title: La herencia del Señor
articles.description: Los hijos no son simplemente producto de un acto biológico; cada uno es una bendición y un regalo de Dios.

articles.title: Amor y cuidado del niñito
articles.description: Cuando Dios bendice al esposo y a su esposa con un bebé, ¿qué hacen después? Ésta es una vista panorámica que alienta a padres y madres a cumplir sus responsabilidades con los pequeñitos dados por Dios.

articles.title: Se salvará teniendo hijos
articles.description: ¿Qué quiso decir Pablo cuando escribió que la mujer “se salvará teniendo hijos”? Ésta es una explicación provechosa de una porción de las Escrituras acaloradamente debatida.

articles.title: Cuatro gracias necesarias
articles.description: Pablo dijo que la mujer que tiene hijos se salvará si permaneciere en fe, amor y santificación, con modestia; éste es un estudio conciso de estas cuatro gracias.

articles.title: Sara dio a luz por fe
articles.description: Palabras alentadoras para que la mujer confíe en Dios ante los retos del embarazo.

articles.title: El mejor apoyo a la maternidad
articles.description: Pensamientos para esposos y esposas sobre cómo encarar las pruebas del embarazo y del nacimiento.

articles.title: Cuando Dios no da hijos
articles.description: Dios, quien ordenó “Fructificad y multiplicaos”, no siempre da la bendición de procrear. ¿Cómo debe reaccionar el cristiano frente  a este dolor?

articles.title: Un niño nos es nacido

sourceMetadata.title: Belén y las buenas nuevas
sourceMetadata.description:
“Belén no tenía nada de grandioso. Era pequeña para ser en los millares de Judá (Mi. 5:2); quizá apenas una aldea de pastores o un pueblo cuya vida giraba alrededor del mercado; no obstante, allí el gran propósito de Dios se convirtió en un hecho. El Verbo fue hecho carne”.
Así comienza este tratado de Horatius Bonar sobre la encarnación. Aquí vemos la gloria de Dios haciéndose hombre y el amor que Dios mostró al enviar a Su Hijo a vivir y morir en humildad. En Belén podemos aprender sobre el camino a Dios, la vanidad de la tierra, una vida de santidad, un corazón de humildad y negación propia.

parent.title: Bethlehem and Its Good News
parent.description:
"There was nothing great about Bethlehem.  It was 'little among the thousands of Judah' (Mic 5:2); perhaps but a shepherd-village or small market-town; yet there the great purpose of God became a fact; 'The Word was made flesh.'"

Thus begins this tract by Horatius Bonar about the incarnation.  Here we see the glory of God becoming man and the love that God showed in sending His Son to live and die in humility.  At Bethlehem we can learn about the way to God, the vanity of the earth, a life of holiness, a heart of humility, and self denial.

sourceMetadata.title: Buenas obras
sourceMetadata.description: Presentamos esta edición de Portavoz de la Gracia enfocando el tema de las Buenas Obras. Charles Spurgeon nos presenta el primer artículo preguntando si es posible que un pecador tenga obras. Seguidamente, David Martyn Lloyd-Jones nos muestra lo que dicen las Escrituras acerca de la relación entre la gracia de Dios, nuestras obras y la salvación en Cristo Jesús. Arthur Pink nos pregunta si estamos obteniendo provecho de nuestro estudio de las Escrituras o no, describiendo el lugar, la necesidad, la naturaleza y el alcance de las buenas obras. Horatius Bonar  muestra que la justificación únicamente por gracia a través de únicamente la fe en Cristo Jesús no produce un vivir superficial, mundano o indiferente, sino que es la motivación para un vivir santo evidenciado por las buenas obras. Luego aprendemos de Ebenezer Erskine cómo la fe en Cristo influencia y produce buenas obras. El puritano Thomas Manton es un poco más difícil de leer que algunos de nuestros otros autores, pero la lectura cuidadosa y devota de este artículo sobre ser celoso de buenas obras beneficiará ricamente al lector. Erskine nos ofrece un artículo más en el que declara con intrepidez la necesidad de mantenernos constantes en hacer buenas obras y lo que esto significa. Por último, concluimos este tema con dos artículos por Juan Bunyan. Primero, nos da la mejor manera de motivar las buenas obras entre los creyentes y concluye este número de Portavoz de la Gracia enfocando las obras del creyente en el Día del Juicio.

parent.title: Good Works
parent.description:
Good works do not save a sinner, but there is no saint without them.  This issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster explores the relationship of the believer to good works.  Where do they come from? What role do they play?  How essential are they? 

"Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us,...This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works." -- Tit 3:5, 8

sourceMetadata.title: Como estar libre de la amargura
sourceMetadata.description: Cómo Estar Libre de la Amargura ayuda al lector a romper las cadenas de uno de los señores más terribles: el pecado de la amargura. A través de este folleto, se expone qué es la amargura, su causa y cómo resolverla. La raíz de la amargura en la vida de una persona solo puede ser extraída por el poder de la gracia de Dios en el evangelio, enfrentando honestamente su pecado y acercándose a Dios para llenar su corazón con el agua dulce de su amor.

parent.title: How to Be Free from Bitterness
parent.description: How to Be Free From Bitterness helps the reader break the chains of one of the most terrible masters—the sin of bitterness. Through this booklet explore what bitterness is, its cause, and how to solve it. The root of bitterness in a person’s life can only be extracted by the power of God’s grace in the gospel, honestly facing their sin, and coming to God to fill their heart with the sweet water of His love.

files.title: Como vienen los hombres a Cristo
files.author: Charles H. Spurgeon
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Como vienen los hombres a Cristo
sourceMetadata.description: En este tratado, Charles Spurgeon explica la verdad que Cristo declara en Juan 6:44: ningún hombre puede venir a Cristo a menos que el Padre lo atraiga. Primero, refuta un punto de vista arminiano común que sugiere que Dios usa la predicación solo para atraer a los hombres a Cristo, dejando el resto a los hombres. También repudia la afirmación de que Spurgeon, y aquellos como él, enseñan que Dios arrastra a los hombres a Cristo en contra de su voluntad. Pero como todos los hombres son naturalmente resistentes, ¿cómo los atrae el Padre? Según Spurgeon, Él envía al Espíritu Santo para cambiar los corazones de los hombres para que vengan voluntariamente al Salvador sin ninguna obligación. ¿Cómo se logra esto? Solo Dios sabe, pero si la influencia del Espíritu Santo no se ejerce, "nunca ha habido y nunca habrá un hombre que pueda venir o que vendrá al Señor Jesucristo".

parent.title: How Men Come to Christ
parent.description: In this tract Charles Spurgeon explains the truth Christ declares in John 6:44: no man can come to Christ unless the Father draw him. First, he refutes a common Arminian view that suggests God uses preaching alone to draw men to Christ, leaving the rest up to man. He also repudiates the assertion that Spurgeon, and those like him, teach that God drags men to Christ against their will. But since all men are naturally resistant, how does the Father draw them? According to Spurgeon, He sends the Holy Spirit to change men’s hearts so that they come willingly to the Savior without any compulsion whatever. How is this accomplished? Only God knows, but if the Holy Spirit’s influence is not brought to bear, “there never has been and there never will be any man who either can or will come to the Lord Jesus Christ.”

sourceMetadata.title: Cristo murió por los impíos
sourceMetadata.description: Este tratado evangelístico muestra que Dios da testimonio contra el hombre, señalando que es pecador. Por naturaleza, el hombre se encuentra en enemistad con Dios en todo momento. El mayor de todos los pecados es que el hombre no cree en el nombre de Cristo ni le ama. Bonar demuestra que, a pesar de este conflicto del hombre contra Dios, Dios ha provisto esperanza —un camino hacia la reconciliación— a través del Hijo de Dios crucificado.

parent.title: Christ Died for the Ungodly
parent.description: This evangelistic tract shows that God bears witness against man, that he is a sinner. Man naturally is at enmity with God at all times. The greatest of all sins is that man does not believe on the name of Christ and does not love Him. Bonar shows that despite this conflict of man against God, God has provided hope, a path to reconciliation, through the crucified Son of God.

sourceMetadata.title: Culto familiar
sourceMetadata.description:
El fundamento bíblico, la práctica y los beneficios del culto familiar.

Existen muchas ordenanzas externas importantes implícitas en las Escrituras que reflejan el estado de nuestro corazón y revelan si sentimos o no un amor ferviente por Dios y por su servicio. Uno de los deberes más importantes de un verdadero creyente es el culto familiar. Las Escrituras establecen un precedente desde el principio con el ejemplo de Abraham, de quien Dios dijo: «Porque yo sé que él mandará a sus hijos y a su casa después de sí, que guarden el camino del Señor, haciendo justicia y juicio». Se pronuncian terribles advertencias contra quienes descuidan este deber: «Derrama tu furor sobre las naciones que no te conocen, y sobre las familias que no invocan tu nombre». Pink advierte que el culto privado no es suficiente: se requiere que los creyentes honren a Dios también en el seno de sus familias. Él destaca las ventajas y bendiciones que se derivan del culto familiar, tales como prevenir el pecado y transmitir un sentido de la majestad y la autoridad de Dios.

parent.title: Family Worship
parent.description:
The biblical basis, practice, and benefits of family worship.

There are many important outward ordinances implied in Scripture, which are an indication of the state of our hearts and whether or not we have an ardent love for God and His service. One of the most important duties of a true believer is that of family worship. A precedent is set early in Scripture with the example of Abraham, of whom God said, “For I know him, that He will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment.” Fearful threatenings are pronounced on those who neglect this duty. “Pour out thy fury upon the heathen that know Thee not, and upon the families that call not upon Thy name.” Pink warns that private worship is not enough: believers are required to honor God in their families as well. He speaks of the advantages and blessing that come from family worship: preventing sin and conveying a sense of God’s majesty and authority.

sourceMetadata.title: Deberes familiares
sourceMetadata.description: En este fragmento del folleto *Christian Behavior* (La conducta cristiana), John Bunyan aborda los roles y las relaciones entre los miembros de la familia inmediata. Los padres tienen la responsabilidad de dirigir todos los aspectos del bienestar espiritual y físico de su familia. «Él mandará a sus hijos y a su casa después de sí, y ellos guardarán el camino del SEÑOR». Las esposas deben respetar la autoridad y el liderazgo de sus maridos. Los padres son responsables de instruir y corregir a sus hijos, de «criarlos en la disciplina y amonestación del Señor». A los hijos se les manda: «Obedeced a vuestros padres en el Señor, porque esto es justo». Este folleto ofrece instrucciones prácticas para todos aquellos que deseen modelar sus relaciones familiares según el patrón de las Escrituras.

parent.title: Family Duty
parent.description: John Bunyan, in this excerpt from the booklet Christian Behavior, addresses the roles and relationships between immediate family members. Fathers are responsible for commanding all aspects of their family’s spiritual and physical well-being. “He will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the LORD.” Wives should respect the authority and leadership of their husbands. Parents are responsible to instruct and correct their children, to “bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.” Children are commanded to “obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.” This booklet provides practical instruction for all who desire to model their family relationships after the Scripture pattern.

Los padres tienen la responsabilidad de dirigir todos los aspectos del bienestar espiritual y físico de su familia. «Él mandará a sus hijos y a su casa después de sí, y ellos guardarán el camino del SEÑOR». Las esposas deben respetar la autoridad y el liderazgo de sus maridos. Los padres son responsables de instruir y corregir a sus hijos, de «criarlos en la disciplina y amonestación del Señor». A los hijos se les manda: «Obedeced a vuestros padres en el Señor, porque esto es justo». Este folleto ofrece instrucciones prácticas para todos aquellos que deseen modelar sus relaciones familiares según el patrón de las Escrituras.

sourceMetadata.title: Eduque a los niños para Cristo
sourceMetadata.description: Un mensaje instructivo de Edward Hooker dirigido a padres cristianos reflexivos que desean criar a sus hijos para que sean siervos útiles de Cristo. Tanto los padres como los ministros y maestros cristianos deben enseñar a los niños a su cargo no solo a amar a Dios y a su obra, sino también a subordinar su propia voluntad a los intereses del reino de Cristo. La mejor manera de lograrlo es dando un buen ejemplo en todos los aspectos de la vida: primero mediante la oración y luego a través de una enseñanza fiel, inculcándoles desde temprana edad la necesidad de la conversión como preparación para una vida de servicio y de amor exclusivo hacia Dios. Las madres cristianas constituyen una bendición especial para el mundo, ya que se encuentran en la posición ideal para influir y guiar constantemente a sus hijos en este sentido.

parent.title: Children To Be Educated for Christ
parent.description: An instructive message by Edward Hooker for thoughtful Christian parents who desire to raise their children to be useful servants of Christ. Parents, as well as Christian ministers and teachers, need to teach the children in their charge not only love for God and His work, but must also teach them that their will must be secondary to the work of Christ’s kingdom. This is best done by setting a good example in every aspect of life, first, by prayer, then by faithful teaching, and instilling in them early the need for conversion in preparation for a life of service and love for God alone. Christian mothers are a special blessing to the world, having and being in the best position to constantly influence and guide their children in this way.
